reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, our stay at Hilton London Metropole was extremely disappointing, especially as this trip was supposed to be a special celebration for our anniversary and my wife’s birthday.

The biggest issue was the elevators. My wife became stuck in one of the elevators for around an hour. What made an already stressful situation much worse was how poorly it was handled by the hotel.

The hotel staff were aware that the lift was not working, yet they still failed to take appropriate action. My wife and the other people trapped inside repeatedly pressed the emergency button, but it did not appear to be working. No one responded, despite their attempts to raise the alarm. Shouting and banging on the doors also did not help. This entire situation could have been avoided if the hotel had acted promptly and appropriately.

When I contacted reception, at one point a member of staff actually called me back to tell me that all the elevators were working and that nobody was stuck. I had to explain again that my wife was still inside the elevator with other people and tell him exactly which elevator and which side of the hotel she was on. After I explained this, he simply ended the call without saying anything.

Throughout the situation, getting through to reception was extremely difficult. Calls regularly went unanswered, and on occasions when someone did answer, the call was disconnected. We were also very concerned that the emergency button inside the elevator did not appear to be working, despite being pressed multiple times by those trapped inside.

My wife had only gone downstairs for five minutes to collect our food so that we could have dinner with our children. Instead, she ended up trapped in an elevator for around an hour. By the time everything was resolved, our food was cold, the children were tired and ended up going to sleep without eating, and the whole evening was ruined.

We spoke to three different managers in an attempt to resolve the issue. Each time, we had to explain again what had happened and then email ourselves a summary of the conversation. With every handover, the details became increasingly watered down, which was extremely frustrating and made us feel that the seriousness of the incident was not being properly understood or recorded.

The managers later tried to resolve the situation by offering 50% off our first night. While I appreciate that they attempted to do something, considering we paid around £327 per night for what is advertised as a four-star hotel, I don't feel this reflected the seriousness of what happened or the way the situation was handled. It is astonishing to pay this amount and still experience such poor communication, coordination and customer care.

My main concern isn't simply that an elevator broke down. Mechanical problems can happen anywhere. It is the fact that hotel staff were aware the lift was not working but still did not take action, combined with the apparent failure of the emergency button, the lack of communication, the repeated need to explain the incident to different managers, and the way reception responded while guests were actually trapped inside. This raises serious concerns about the hotel’s standards of maintenance, safety and customer care.

What was meant to be a special stay for our anniversary and my wife's birthday became an unnecessarily stressful experience. Sadly, based on our experience, I expected significantly better standards from a Hilton hotel.

Cuando nos fuimos quisimos poner una queja formal y nos dieron una dirección de correo a la cual incluso adjuntamos foto con el polvo acumulado y explicamos el problema de mis hijas. Nos respondieron que investigarían el tema y jamás nos volvieron a contactar. Es una vergüenza que un Hilton de cuatro estrellas funcione así y que no tenga capacidad de respuesta. Jamás volveremos a alojarnos en uno de sus hoteles, ni recomendaré a nadie que lo haga.

reviews.text: BEWARE!!!  We checked into The Zedwell Piccadilly in October 2026.  The location is great - right in the heart of the theatre district.  The room appeared clean though lacking in storage.  It also only has frosted glass on the entire bathroom leading my tween daughter to feel way to exposed and uncomfortable changing clothes and showering.  The worst part, however, was BED BUGS!!!!  We found bed bugs the morning after our first night.  We immediately alerted staff.  They steamed our luggage and offered to switch our rooms.  Unfortunately, while we were standing there, another customer came up with the exact same issue indicating to me a wide spread issue.  We decided we had to check out.  The hotel refused to refund us the 4 nights we prepaid for and would not be able to use.  Our reservation was $1800 and we lost that money and had to pay for another hotel, an uber, and to have all of our clothes laundered.  We also lost a full day of vacation due to dealing with this issue.  I understand that bed bugs are an unfortunate reality -- but it is unacceptable for hotels to refuse to refund money for nights we could not stay there due to the issue.  We reached out to management and corporate and have received no response.  I would NEVER recommend anyone stay at this or any other Zedwell property based on our experience.  It is buyer beware.  They will not stand behind their property.

reviews.text: The most important thing about staying at Zedwell is that you have to know what you're getting yourself into. You will be nickeled and dimed for everything (is there a British equivalent to that expression?). Want to check in early, check out late, or store baggage? Extra charge. "Cocoon" is also code for windowless prison cell. You will trip on your luggage trying to walk from the bed to the bathroom even though it's only two steps. If there are two of you, you will trip on each other trying to get out of bed to get to the toilet. But here's the thing... I loved staying here and would stay here again. I split my trip into two parts and stayed at an airbnb in zone 2 for the second part, and if I had to do it again, I would choose my Zedwell prison cell over the one bedroom flat with a kitchen and laundry. Why? Location, location, location. I love to walk and this location is unbeatable. The plus side of the windowless prison cell is absolutely zero street noise. Zero street noise when you're located on the busiest intersection in London with those stupid pedicabs blasting music all night? It's a miracle. I had to set an alarm because I would have slept all day because with the lights out the room is pitch black. You'd think it'd feel claustrophobic, but I honestly felt it calming and relaxing... like a cocoon. I was also staying alone, maybe I'd feel differently sharing the room with a partner or friend. The price of the cocoon prison cell would be absolutely ridiculous for what you get if it were in any other city, but for being in the heart of central London, it's relatively reasonable.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text: One of the worst hotels I’ve ever had the misfortune of staying at. The experience started as you enter the lobby and are met with iPads. No friendly concierge to greet you and check you in, which is a sad absence indeed for someone who likes to ask them for restaurant recommendations or directions to a location. Once you enter the room, this is where it truly becomes more of a hostel than a hotel. There is no mini fridge, no microwave (can’t take any restaurant leftovers with you), and nowhere to sit besides the bed. This was my main gripe: a complete lack of surfaces, no locations to put your belongings down other than the floor, the bed, or on top of your suitcase (as thankfully there is a singular luggage stand). Upon further inspection of the room, all the vents were missing grates so there were three gaping holes in our ceilings. The bed itself is also quite poor, as the mattress had outlived its use, and there were no fitted sheets, just a loose sheet placed on top. What you were left with were flat pillows (only 2 provided for a double bed) and a comforter, no top sheet. Then there’s the issue of the washroom, if you can call it that. The only sense of privacy provided is a sliding glass door with a hole for a handle, so there is absolutely no division at all and sound travels as if there was nothing there. Once again you encounter the problem of no surfaces in the washroom, since a classic counter around the sink is completely absent. The shower is behind a glass semi divider that does not cover enough, so water gets everywhere. A ceramic base with a lip would do wonders in keeping the water within the shower, and then beyond that maybe a sliding door or curtain to once again give you any sense of privacy as you use the facilities. Sure the location is good, but it’s also good to come back to a good hotel after a long day on the town. If you’re more used to a hostel then this will be perfect for you. But at these prices I really don’t see what the benefit is either way. It’s not hotel quality and it’s not priced like a hostel so it ends up being worthless.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
The location of this place is absolutely excellent – it really could not be more central, which was a huge advantage during our stay in London. The room itself was also clean, tidy and nicely designed, and the general concept of the accommodation is good. Self check-in and self check-out worked fine, although everything is automated and there is no traditional reception.

However, I would definitely not recommend the 8-person room for a group of eight. We booked a room with four bunk beds, which technically provides sleeping space for eight people. To be fair, this was stated on Booking.com and we simply misunderstood it when booking. The beds themselves were not the problem – the size of the room was. The room was extremely small for eight people and there was barely enough space for everyone and their luggage. In my opinion, a room of this size would be much more suitable for around four people. I had expected the room to be approximately twice the size.

There is also a separate beauty/get-ready room with mirrors, hairdryers and power outlets, which was a very nice and useful feature.

Unfortunately, the biggest issue happened after our stay. I accidentally left my AirPods underneath my pillow and only noticed this around six or seven hours after leaving. I contacted the accommodation immediately through Booking.com and was automatically instructed to contact them by email, which I did.

It has now been two days and I have still received no response. What concerns me even more is that, according to the location shown for my AirPods, they were moved after I had already returned to Germany. I obviously cannot say who took or moved them, but this raises serious concerns. Either the room was not cleaned thoroughly enough for the AirPods to be found underneath the pillow before the next guests arrived, or they were found and were not reported as lost property. Either way, I find this very disappointing.

Mistakes happen and I fully accept that leaving the AirPods behind was my responsibility. However, I would expect an accommodation to respond promptly when a guest reports a valuable lost item – especially when the item appears to have been moved after check-out.

Overall, the location is fantastic, the accommodation was clean and the concept has potential. However, the room was far too small for eight people, and the lack of any response regarding my missing AirPods has unfortunately left a very negative impression of our stay.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Our experience at this hotel was deeply disappointing and, at several points, made us feel unwelcome.

From the moment we arrived with our luggage, a member of staff asked us whether we were “in the right place.” As Black guests arriving to check into a hotel where we had a reservation, the implication of that question was incredibly uncomfortable and made us feel as though we did not look like people who belonged at this hotel.

The following night, when we returned after hours, we were stopped and asked to show our room keys—even though entry through the hotel’s locked front door already required us to use our room key. Combined with our experience at check-in, this left us feeling singled out and scrutinized as guests.

Unfortunately, the service and cleanliness issues were just as concerning. We discovered what appeared to be bodily-fluid stains on our bed linens that did not belong to us. At approximately 7:30 p.m., before leaving for dinner, we brought this to the front desk’s attention and asked for the bedding to be changed. The request was initially treated as though it would be extremely difficult to accommodate, but we were eventually told it would be taken care of.

We returned to the hotel around 3:00 a.m.—approximately 7.5 hours later—to discover that the linens had never been changed.

I went back to the front desk and explained the situation. Again, I was met with resistance and told there was not enough staff available to address it. That response was unacceptable. I had reported the issue more than seven hours earlier, when staff were available. More importantly, a guest should never be put in the position of having to argue about whether they are expected to sleep in a bed with someone else’s bodily-fluid stains on the linens.

I specifically asked for a complete set of clean bed linens so that, at minimum, I could change the bedding myself. After further back-and-forth, I was given only a single sheet rather than a complete set of bedding.

I understand that hotels can be short-staffed and that mistakes happen. What I cannot understand is the repeated resistance to resolving a basic sanitation issue, particularly after giving the hotel more than enough time to address it.

Between being questioned about whether we belonged at the hotel, being asked for additional proof that we were guests when returning, finding stained linens, and then having to repeatedly advocate simply to have clean bedding, this stay left us feeling both unwelcome and poorly cared for.

I will be seeking further resolution directly with hotel management. At this price point—or frankly, at any price point—guests should be able to expect clean bedding, respectful treatment, and prompt action when a serious hygiene issue is reported.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text: If I could give this hotel zero stars, I would. This is hands down the dirtiest hotel I have ever stayed at in my life, and I have traveled all over the world. I live in the United States, and if I ever return to London, I will never step foot in this establishment again. I gave management ample time to correct these issues before writing this, but the company's resolution was to offer me a measly 25% off if I returned. What a complete joke.Our nightmare experience began after traveling for approximately 12 hours. We arrived and checked in at 12:14 p.m. on Saturday. Despite arranging an early check-in ahead of time, I was told no rooms were available. I had to demand to speak with a manager just to finally be assigned a room.It only went downhill from there:The First Room: It was completely unclean, unfit for a human guest, and the wrong room type. There was trash covering the floor, the mattress was flipped entirely over, and dirty sanitary pads were left on the ground. I immediately went back to reception to report this biohazard.The "Upgrade" Room: At 12:42 p.m.—just 28 minutes after checking in—the manager assigned us what they claimed was an "upgraded" room. It was just as repulsive. There was what appeared to be blood smeared beside the bed, leftover chips on the table, and a used contact lens on the floor.Broken Amenities: To make matters worse, the air conditioning did not work at all.Wrong Bed Configuration: Our reservation was explicitly for two beds. Instead, we were given one bed and two couches.Do not stay here. reviews.text: I checked into this hotel, needing a safe place to stay for 3 nights. Upon entering, the room was highly unsanitary and a severe health hazard. The bathroom bin was covered in bodily fluids, the basin had stagnant water and mould, and the toilet areas had not been cleaned. There was even used chewing gum and hair in the bed.I immediately notified reception that the room was uninhabitable and requested a refund for the £300 stay. I was told refunds couldn't be processed on-site and to email management. The general manager only offered a generic 20% off a future stay. When I rejected this, they copied and pasted the exact same response, completely ignoring the hazardous conditions. Management and the hotel group have since ignored all my emails.While this was a non-refundable booking, providing an uninhabitable room is a material breach of contract and a breach of consumer rights and health and safety regulations. I expect this to be taken seriously.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text: I stayed here (Zedwell Piccadilly Circus) not long after it first opened for 3 nights and it was great. This time however, was a very different experience indeed. The first time I stayed was right in the middle of the summer and it was very cheap. This time (tonight is my last night of 4), it was pro rata 3 times the price. The cracks are beginning to show. Customer service is utterly non existent. It’s not possibly for them to care any less. Your pod is selected at random; and when I got given a ground floor pod it was difficult for me to get in and out as I have mobility pain. Last time was fine as my pod was up a level on some steps and it was dead easy. So, I dumped my stuff in the pod and asked for a move. I explained the situation and was asked if I had entered my pod. I said I had but just dumped my bag inside. I was then told, astonishingly, that once a pod has been entered it can’t be removed from the system. What?? It’s your system. You control it. So what if I was sick in it or something? Do I have to lay in my own vomit for 4 nights because you can’t remove it from the system? What patronising nonsense. I email customer services and as yet…DAY 4…have not received a reply. Add to that, there are broken toilet seats, many toilet cubicles with no paper, black mould in some showers. Sanitary towels (used) left in toilet cubicles, used make up pads left in the sink area, items of clothing left in sink area. It’s awful. As for the pod area…total and absolute carnage. Stuff scattered everywhere. Massive suitcases, pairs of shoes, socks, towels, clothing, underwear items, scattered everywhere like a minefield. Absolutely horrific. The two stays could not possibly be more different  but you know what? You get what you pay for don’t you? This is what cheap means. First time I stayed, you could go into the toilet at 3am and there would be cleaners in there. It was immaculate. Not now. Because now it’s awful by comparison. This place…unless they address such issues PROPERLY….will be beyond awful and full of the worst kinds of people within a year. The attendants could not care a tiny bit. There is NO management. There’s absolutely no security and it’s only a matter of time before there is a serious incident between people, as some don’t care for rules or for being considerate to others around them. This stay was absolutely horrific and I was a huge supporter of it at first but I can say now with complete conviction I’ll never set foot in this place again. The vending machines in reception didn’t work the first time I stayed and still don’t work now. Unless you can’t afford anywhere else avoid this place until they get their act together. The ONLY good thing about now is the location, but I’d rather be anywhere else if comfort and a good vibe is what’s important.

reviews.text:
My experience with this hotel is definitely **mixed feelings**. 😅

Let me start with the positive because, honestly, there is one major thing this hotel has going for it: **LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!** 😂

The hotel is right in the center of London, around **Chinatown/Soho**, and within walking distance of many major attractions, including Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, the National Gallery, Chinatown, Soho, and many other places. If your goal is to be in the middle of everything and walk around London, the location is excellent.

And now… that’s where the good news ends. 😂

### 🏨 THE HOTEL EXPERIENCE

Check-in is at **3:00 PM**. If you want to check in earlier, you have to pay an additional **£60**. 😳

Our room was **6133 on the 6th floor**, and let me tell you—getting to the room was an adventure by itself! 😂

The hotel is HUGE and feels like a maze. There are so many rooms and hallways that if you are not paying attention, you might need Google Maps just to find your own room! 😂

The hallways are also quite dark and have low ceilings, which makes the whole place feel a little unusual.

Then we opened the door to our room…

The room was **VERY small**. There were **no windows, no side tables, no TV, and no telephone to call the front desk**. And there really isn't a traditional front desk service like you would expect in a regular hotel.

Check-in and check-out are done on the **first floor**, using one of the tablets lined up there. So don't expect someone at a traditional reception desk waiting to greet you and hand you a room key. 😅

For two guests, our room had **two twin beds, two towels, and one pillow per bed**.

And here's another surprise: we were told that the room is cleaned **every FOUR days**.

Yes… FOUR days! 😂

So if you are expecting your room to be cleaned every day, fresh towels, and your bed beautifully made when you return from sightseeing, you might want to adjust your expectations.

We actually had to go downstairs and ask the staff for additional towels. 😩😂

### 🤔 MY HONEST THOUGHTS

I have stayed in hotels in **Dubai, Paris, and on cruises**, so maybe those experiences have spoiled me a little. 😂

But compared with those experiences, this was definitely one of the **simplest and most basic hotels** I have ever stayed in.

And that's important to mention because this hotel is located in such a prime area of London, where you would expect a little more in terms of comfort and service.

I was also told that there are cheaper hotels farther outside central London that offer **better amenities and better service**.

Since this hotel was part of the **flight + hotel package we booked through Expedia**, I can't say that we specifically chose this hotel based on its individual price or amenities.

### ⭐ FINAL THOUGHT

If your priority is **LOCATION**, this hotel has that covered. You are right in the heart of London, close to restaurants, attractions, shopping, Chinatown, Soho, and many famous landmarks.

But if you are looking for **comfort, space, daily housekeeping, room amenities, and attentive hotel service**, I would definitely do more research before booking.

For me, the location was great, but the **hotel amenities and customer service were disappointing**.

Would I stay here again? **Probably not.** 😂

But hey… at least we were in the heart of London, so when the hotel disappointed us, we could walk outside and enjoy London! 🇬🇧😂

**Lesson learned: When booking a hotel, don't just look at the location—check the room size, amenities, housekeeping schedule, and customer service too!**

This hotel is located at a strategus place in London, walking distance from Buckingham Palace, the National Gallery, and a lot of restaurants.  It is clean on the inside and has an attached caffe in the lowest floor.  There is a number of homeless people right outside the hotel, but it is safe inside the hotel as their staff is on site 24/7.  The room we had was pretty small, but it had what we needed: bed, toilet, shower, sink.  We had to ask for towels every night because they do not change them and they do not clean the room until every 5th day.

Unfortunately, we had an incident.  After they cleaned on the 5th day, we found a finger nail and stains on the bed.  The staff was unwilling to compensate for this gross mishap, and was borderline rude about it when we complained.

As far as customer service, they are difficult to get a hold of before travel.  On site, they are rigid and not willing to work with your circumstances.  They would charge extra if you wanted to drop off your luggage before check-in or if you wanted to leave it in a safe place after check-out which is promptly at 10:00 AM.

I will have to give them credit for their help during another incident.  On our last night, one of us got sick in the middle of the night and threw up in the bathroom.  A staff member was able to instantly come to clean the bathroom and freshen it up in the middle of the night, which we definitely appreciated.  They did not charge us extra for this, even though we offered to pay extra.

Overall, would recommend the place for its location and safety, but if customer service and cleanliness are important to you, it may not be the best fit.

Absolutely unacceptable experience – appalling cleanliness and customer service

I have two friends who have experienced serious issues at this hotel, one two years ago and another today. Unfortunately, these experiences raise serious concerns about the hotel's standards and customer service.

My friend had requested an early check-in online and received confirmation that it was approved. She arrived at 12 noon, expecting to check in early as agreed, but was made to wait until 3:30 pm while her room was supposedly being cleaned. After waiting three and a half hours, she finally went up to her room, only to find it in an absolutely disgusting condition.

The toilet had faeces inside the bowl, and there was dust throughout the room. She urgently needed to use the bathroom, but it was so unhygienic that she had to leave the hotel to find another toilet elsewhere.

What made the experience even worse was the attitude of the reception staff. When my friend complained that the bathroom was not clean, the receptionist dismissed her concerns, insisting that it was clean and suggesting that perhaps it simply did not meet my friend's standards. My friend had to explicitly point out that there was faeces inside the toilet bowl before her complaint was taken seriously.

The room was eventually cleaned, but this does not excuse the experience. Dust was still present throughout the room, and valuable time had already been wasted. She had to wait hours beyond her approved early check-in time, was given an unhygienic room, and then had to argue with staff just to have a legitimate hygiene concern acknowledged.

A clean room, basic hygiene, and respectful customer service are the bare minimum any hotel should provide. Mistakes can happen, but dismissing a guest's concerns instead of taking them seriously is simply unacceptable.

What is particularly concerning is that another friend experienced problems at this hotel two years ago. Hearing about another terrible experience raises questions about whether these issues are being properly addressed.

Based on these experiences, I would not recommend this hotel. Management seriously needs to improve its housekeeping standards, check-in procedures, and staff attitude towards guests.

Excellent Location, but a Very Disappointing Experience – Certainly Not Worth the Price

I really wanted to enjoy our stay at Park Plaza Westminster Bridge, especially as I had chosen this hotel specifically for a family trip with my two children. Unfortunately, the experience was disappointing from beginning to end, and certainly not what I would expect from a hotel in this price category.

The problems started before we even reached our room. We arrived at the official check-in time, only to be kept waiting for an entire hour with two children, while other families were being checked in. Despite repeatedly asking for updates, all we received were apologies. No refreshments, no gesture of goodwill, and no meaningful attempt to make up for the inconvenience.

When we were finally given our room, it was not even properly prepared for our arrival. Although our reservation clearly specified three guests, only two sleeping places were available. This meant yet another trip to reception to resolve something that should have been arranged before our arrival.

The cleanliness was particularly disappointing. The room had clearly not been cleaned to an acceptable standard. The cups and spoons were dirty, as were the sinks and taps. Basic toiletries and sufficient towels were also missing and had to be requested separately. I will be attaching photographs, as I believe they speak for themselves.

One of the main reasons I chose this hotel was the swimming pool, which my children were particularly looking forward to. I had even contacted the hotel in advance to enquire about pool access, but received no response. Upon arrival, we discovered that the pool was unavailable due to maintenance issues. It only became accessible the following day, which was extremely frustrating given that we had specifically booked this hotel for its facilities.

Breakfast was another disappointment. On Tuesday morning, at approximately 8:30 am, we had to queue for 10–15 minutes simply to be seated. We then waited another 20 minutes for a bowl of porridge. For a hotel of this size and supposed standard, I would expect considerably better organisation.

As we had to leave very early on our departure day, we also requested a takeaway breakfast in place of the breakfast we had already paid for. Unfortunately, even this simple request could not be accommodated.

What made the entire experience particularly frustrating was the lack of effective customer service. Whenever I raised an issue, I was passed from one member of staff to another. Everyone seemed perfectly capable of saying "sorry", but very little was actually done to resolve the problems or make us feel valued as guests.

We genuinely felt unwelcome and left to deal with everything ourselves. Travelling alone with two children, I had hoped for a comfortable, relaxing stay, not a constant series of visits to reception to request things that should have been provided as standard.

To be fair, I would like to mention the staff at the swimming pool, who were genuinely friendly, welcoming and professional once the pool finally reopened. They were a refreshing exception to an otherwise disappointing experience.

The hotel's location is undoubtedly excellent, with Westminster and many of London's main attractions within easy reach. Unfortunately, that is its only significant advantage.

For the amount we paid, I expected far better cleanliness, organisation, communication and customer care. A convenient location simply does not compensate for such a disappointing level of service.

I left feeling that we had paid a premium price for an experience that fell far below reasonable expectations.

I would not choose to stay here again, and I find it very difficult to recommend this hotel to families.

reviews.text:
Tekst

⭐ **1/5 – Katastrofa! Zdecydowanie odradzam ten hotel!**

Zdecydowanie najgorszy pobyt w czterogwiazdkowym hotelu, z jakim miałem do czynienia. Hotel w centrum Londynu, z wysokimi cenami i aspiracjami do czterech gwiazdek, a poziom usług, czystości i obsługi jest skandaliczny.

Zarezerwowaliśmy apartament dla dwóch dorosłych i dwójki dzieci z widokiem na Big Bena oraz studio dla dwóch dorosłych, również z widokiem na Big Bena. Zameldowanie miało nastąpić o godzinie 15:00. Na miejscu poinformowano nas, że zamówiony apartament jest niedostępny, i zaproponowano pokój o znacznie niższym standardzie, bez obiecanego widoku. Ostatecznie właściwy apartament udostępniono nam dopiero o **21:30, czyli z ponad sześciogodzinnym opóźnieniem!**

Przez cały pobyt panował brud i bałagan. Zakurzone meble i lustra, brudne kubki i kieliszki, niewystarczająca liczba ręczników, brak szlafroków, mydła i uzupełniania herbaty. Sprzątanie pokoi to kompletna fikcja. Pokojówka zamiast pościelić łóżka, rzucała poduszki i piżamy na biurko. Łazienka była sprzątana niedokładnie, a zużyte naczynia i resztki jedzenia po room service stały na korytarzu aż do rana.

**Jedzenie paskudne!** Śniadania fatalnej jakości, obrzydliwa jajecznica, której nie dało się jeść. Po hotelu tej kategorii można oczekiwać przynajmniej świeżych, smacznych posiłków, a nie jedzenia, które skutecznie odbiera apetyt.

Dodatkowo przez cały pobyt nie mogliśmy korzystać z basenu. Pomimo prób rezerwacji każdorazowo informowano nas o awarii. Tym samym jedna z istotnych atrakcji hotelu była całkowicie niedostępna.

**To absolutnie nie jest standard czterogwiazdkowego hotelu!** Brud, fatalne jedzenie, niekompetentna obsługa, brak podstawowego wyposażenia, niedziałający basen i lekceważenie gości. Szczególnie bulwersujące jest to, że za pobyt z rodziną płaci się niemałe pieniądze, oczekując komfortu i odpoczynku, a otrzymuje się stres, rozczarowanie i warunki nieadekwatne do ceny.

**Żądamy zwrotu 50% kosztów pobytu z uwagi na rażąco niski standard świadczonych usług.**

**Jedna gwiazdka to i tak zdecydowanie za dużo. Nigdy więcej! Zdecydowanie odradzam, szczególnie rodzinom z dziećmi.**

I would like to say a huge thank you to Stephen and Damien at the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge London for the outstanding service, kindness and support they have shown us during an incredibly difficult and emotional time for our family.

From the moment we checked in, Stephen was fantastic. He welcomed us warmly, helped arrange an upgrade to our room and made us feel looked after straight away. What could have been a straightforward check-in turned into something much more meaningful, given the difficult circumstances.

We originally only needed to stay for one night, but unfortunately, due to the situation, we needed to extend our stay. This morning, Damien, the Assistant Manager, went above and beyond to help us. He made extending our stay as stress-free as possible, arranged another room for us. His understanding, compassion and willingness to help have made a genuinely difficult situation that little bit easier to manage.

Both Stephen and Damien have been absolutely brilliant. They have shown us that hospitality is about so much more than rooms and service; it’s about understanding that sometimes people are going through things in life that are far more important than the reason they originally booked a hotel. Their kindness, professionalism and genuine willingness to help have not gone unnoticed.

They are both a real credit to the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge team and the Radisson Hotel Group. I hope this review reaches the right people because staff like these deserve recognition for the difference they make to guests.

Thank you both again for everything you have done for us. It genuinely means a lot. Outstanding service from two outstanding members of staff.

reviews.text: I have been waiting to stay at this hotel for a long time. The impression and reviews were very good. I will note that there was already a reservation that was canceled due to a personal event and the charming and professional management team made sure to keep the room for me at the same price for a year ahead. Truly admirable. The hotel itself is spacious, luxurious, and in the best location you can get in London, the beds are comfortable, the toiletries are excellent, and we had a wonderful stay as a couple. Unfortunately, however, I must share some serious management problems that made us very sad and are not appropriate for such a luxurious hotel. 1. I pre-ordered a fruit bowl for a fee to surprise my wife, but upon arrival it was not in the room and I had to ask and remind.. 2. There were no bags in the trash can, despite requests over the phone, they did not come to clean the room, only the next day, even the day after they partially cleaned and forgot to replace the products. 3. The day after arrival we went up to the room after a long day... the cards did not work, we had to go down and wait for them to be reissued.  4. On the last day we received a delivery to the hotel that was left with the concierge, when we asked for it he was adamant that we had received nothing, after we returned with a picture he found the delivery clearly placed on his desk with our room number, we were very offended by the disrespectful treatment as if we had come to steal something. 5. What is worse than all of this is the lack of privacy we experienced several times. On the second evening we asked for a corkscrew from the reception, after a few minutes a nice representative arrived and brought the corkscrew. We entered the bedroom... and we were close and suddenly there was a knock on the door, we were not in a position to answer, and suddenly the door opened and another representative came in to put another corkscrew. Luckily for us it was a suite and the bedroom were separate, think what would have happened if it had been a regular room... it would have been really embarrassing. How is it possible for a representative to enter the room at 11 pm without permission??? 6. On the last day we checked out late, in the morning we checked that it had been received and arranged. At 3 pm we arrived at the room and went to shower and sleep before the flight.  And suddenly a cleaning lady enters the room and opens it without permission while we are in an unpleasant situation, we explained to her that it was not time yet and she left. Half an hour later the door opened again and someone else from room service came in... She got confused in the room... She woke us up from our sleep without any consideration. A complete shock. We really enjoyed our stay with you and the potential is high. But things like this should never happen. You will have to improve the communication between the staff and the guests. And update the staff online with accurate information.

Absolute scandal and heartless staff behavior. (Incident from October 6th)

I found myself in a desperate emergency in a foreign country. My main phone (which had my flight boarding pass and bank app) completely died. I only had a secondary work phone left with exactly 2% battery and no payment cards saved on it. I managed to scan the QR code for the power bank rental machine in the lobby with my dying phone. Even though the first 2 hours were free, the app still required me to input my card number and CVV code – and the CVV was on the completely dead phone!

I literally begged the man at the front desk to just let me plug my dead phone into a standard wall socket for ONE MINUTE so it could power on enough for me to retrieve the code. He coldly refused, telling me to use the free wireless charging pad. I desperately tried to explain that a completely dead phone won't turn on that way and needs a cable connection to wake up, but he just didn't care. To make matters worse, instead of helping a person in crisis, he actually laughed at me and started gossiping about me to the other staff members right in front of my face!

I am an 18-year-old with autism. I was stranded without access to my funds or my flight home, and I was panicking. What was I supposed to do? Grovel at his feet? Cry in the middle of the lobby just to get an ounce of basic human decency out of him? Their heartlessness put me in real danger of being left on the streets of London. Disgusting lack of empathy.

Ein wunderbares Hotel an toller Lage - mit einem kleinen persönlichen Wermuthstropfen, welcher 2 Sterne Abzug zur Folge hat, weil er massiven Einfluss auf unser aller Wohlbefinden (sowohl emotional als auch körperlich) hatte.

Wir haben das Hotel u.a. gerade deshalb gebucht, weil es ein Gym hat. Unsere Tochter (14) muss täglich Physioübungen machen und braucht diese Infrastruktur (genügend Platz, Spiegel, Gymnastikmatte, eine leichte Hantel). Das Gym ist jedoch leider erst ab 16 zugänglich und auch mit schriftlicher Einwilligung meinerseits oder gar Anwesenheit einer elterlichen Aufsicht wurde ihr NICHT erlaubt, das Gym zu besuchen. Unbegreiflich! Für mich war das wirklich SEHR (!) enttäuschend. Policy hin oder her - ich hätte mir da wirklich mehr Entgegenkommen gewünscht. Schliesslich ist ein medizinisches ‚Problem‘ die Ursache hinter unserer Bitte nach Einlass.  Seit 6 Jahren besuchen wir Hotels mit Gyms und hatten bisher noch nie (!) Probleme. Das SPA sowie Rezeptions-Persional hat uns nicht einmal eine Alternative angeboten (z.B. ein separater Raum, in welchem sie mit der hauseigenen Gymnastikmatte und einer Hantel hätte ihre Übungen machen können - Anmerkung: Unser Zimmer war zu klein, als das sie dort hätte ihr Physioprogramm absolvieren können). Ich finde sowas ziemlich grenzwertig, zumal unsere Tochter die Konsequenzen davon Wort wörtlich zu spüren bekommen hat. Zwei Sterne Abzug.

Ansonsten ist es ein tolles Hotel an top Lage. Das Essen in den Restaurants ist ausgezeichnet und das Bar-/Restaurant-Personal sehr zuvorkommend. Besonders Niyati und Hanan waren besonders freundlich und haben auch Extrawünsche (z.B. Essen aus dem Französischen Restaurant an der Bar serviert) ohne zu zögern möglich gemacht. DAS ist wahrer Kundenservice. Dieser representiert das Haus. Auch sonst waren alle sehr zuvorkommend und freundlich.

Als Schweizerin ist noch zu erwähnen: Das ‚Müesli‘ beim Frühstück war wirklich TRAUMHAFT lecker. Das werde ich vermissen.

★★★★★ Exceptional Service Once Again for a Very Special Family Occasion

We recently stayed at Park Plaza Westminster Bridge from 23rd–27th September for my son’s wedding, with several members of our family also staying at the hotel.

We have stayed at Park Plaza Westminster Bridge on several previous occasions, as have members of our family from Guernsey, and the service has always been exceptional. This latest stay was no exception. The consistently high standard of care, professionalism and genuine hospitality is one of the main reasons we continue to return.

A very special thank you must go to Claudia & the Guest Services team, whose kindness, thoughtfulness and attention to detail helped make such an important family occasion even more memorable.

Claudia arranged a wonderful upgrade for the newlyweds, to a beautiful suite with a balcony overlooking the London Eye. The room had also been decorated to celebrate their marriage, which was such a lovely and thoughtful surprise. They were absolutely delighted, and it created a very special memory for them. We were also incredibly touched by the kind gift of a bottle of red wine too.

The outstanding service extended throughout the hotel. Everyone in Guest Services was professional, courteous, friendly and genuinely eager to help. The teams in Housekeeping, Reception and the Restaurant were equally excellent and made us all feel extremely welcome and well cared for.

We must also mention the wonderful Concierge, who very kindly helped arrange for a parcel of wedding decorations to be sent back to our home after the celebrations. The Doormen were fantastic too, always ready to help with taxis and transport and always greeting us with a smile.

Having stayed here previously, we know that this level of service is not a one-off. Every visit has been met with the same exceptional standards, and it is the wonderful people at Park Plaza Westminster Bridge who make each stay so enjoyable and memorable.

Our heartfelt thanks to Claudia and the entire team for all the thoughtful touches, kindness and genuine hospitality. You helped make our son’s wedding celebrations even more special, and we are extremely grateful.

A wonderful hotel with an outstanding team and consistently exceptional service. Five stars without hesitation. We look forward to returning and seeing everyone again.

reviews.text:
Booked the Park Plaza Westminster for a long 4 day weekend with family of three.
It is an "Okay" hotel. Maybe slightly expensive for what you get. In my opinion there are better options in London for the same price.
1- We chose the hotel because of the location. We thought it was  good, but ended up being just alright. The fact we had to cross the Westminster Bridge did not help, the bridge is always overcrowded and packed with people. Difficult to walk through. So it turns out the location was not a positive factor.
2- Hotel truly overcrowded, and it seems the staff where overwhelmed with so much people. Queues to check in - 15 min wait to self check in, the software was faulty, so the staff then advised to queue for reception check in - 30 mins more.
Queues for breakfast. Breakfast starts at 7:00 am, I advise to go very early, otherwise you'll face a queue.
3- We book this hotel also to enjoy a bit of the swimming pool after long walking days. It turns out we have to book the swimming pool in anticipation. The problem is, the vacancies were booked really advanced, so when we try to book on the hotel website, the swimming pool vacancies are fully booked for days. We only found one vacancy, of 30 mins only. The pool had nothing to do with the image showed on the website, there was a development happening and they did not warned the public for the development. So two sides of the pool were not accessible. The water was not clean in my opinion.
4- The room was good sized and decent. Bathroom handle was loose. There was a smell of vomit in the bathroom, which stayed for the whole journey. We kept the door close the whole time.
5- The check out was very easy, simple and effective, we were approached by this gentleman, hotel employee,  who got the key card from us, and told us we didn't need to worry about anything else, as the check out was done.

Overall, it all depends of your expectations and what is your threshold.

Regarding the feedback by the hotel to all the reviews, they are processed by artificial intelligence. :-)

reviews.text:
London Autumn Break at Street Palace Hotel
We visited London for our autumn break and stayed at the Street Palace Hotel, and we were extremely happy with our choice!
• Room & Comfort: The Superior Queen room turned out to be quite spacious. Although our window faced the main street, the interior shutters could be closed for the night, providing excellent insulation from street noise and light. The beds were comfortable, and the bed linen was crisp and fresh. The bathrobes and slippers came in very handy after a long shower, and the welcome chocolate and biscuits were a very sweet touch.
• Dining & Service: Since we arrived late in the evening, we had dinner at the hotel restaurant, where we were treated to complimentary drinks. The fish and chips were simply amazing, served with mushy peas and various sauces. We also ordered three different salads—all of them delicious and beautifully presented. The service was exceptionally friendly, and we truly felt welcomed.
• Breakfasts: The breakfasts were delicious and offered a great variety, accompanied by good-quality coffee.
• Convenience: The room came with branded drinking water in eco-friendly sugarcane bottles, which you can refill at the water station in the hallway or even keep as a nice souvenir—a very neat feature.
• Location: The hotel is located right in the heart of London. Our evening walks to Covent Garden, along the Thames to Big Ben, the London Eye, Buckingham Palace, and St. Paul’s Cathedral were simply delightful.
We also went to see Stranger Things at the Phoenix Theatre, which was just a 15-minute walk from the hotel. The surrounding area offers a fantastic choice of restaurants and pubs.
We are completely satisfied with our stay and would love to come back!

⭐ Extremely disappointing experience at The Savoy – Beaufort Bar

We hired the Beaufort Bar at The Savoy for my brother’s 50th birthday celebration, expecting the exceptional level of hospitality and professionalism associated with The Savoy name.

Unfortunately, the way an incident involving one of our guests was handled left us absolutely disgusted.

During the evening, one of our guests had a fall and was clearly in need of some assistance. At a moment when we expected basic care and compassion, we were shocked by the response from members of staff/security. When we asked for water for our guest, this was refused, and instead of trying to calmly help with the situation, we felt the staff became rude, defensive and increasingly intimidating towards us.

What upset us even more was seeing members of staff laughing about the situation in front of us, other staff members and some of our guests. For this to happen during a private 50th birthday celebration that we had hired the Beaufort Bar for was humiliating and completely unacceptable.

We chose The Savoy because of its reputation for outstanding service and because this was such an important family occasion. We certainly did not expect to be treated this way when one of our guests needed assistance.

The way the incident was handled put a very upsetting end to what should have been a wonderful milestone celebration.

For an establishment of The Savoy’s reputation and standing, we expected considerably better — particularly when it came to the welfare of a guest.

A deeply disappointing experience and one that we feel The Savoy should take very seriously.

reviews.text:
1/5 – £134.50 charged for meals already paid for. The hotel admitted its error; resolving it was another ordeal.

I stayed at Novotel London West from 1–4 October 2026 for the BOPA oncology pharmacy conference. The hotel's location near Olympia is convenient. Almost everything else about my experience raised serious concerns about its administration, communication and accountability.

BOOKING ASSURANCES REVERSED

Before arrival, I called to clarify half board, early check-in and late check-out. I was verbally assured that additional meals would be available on my arrival and departure days; no £45 dinner cap was mentioned. At check-in, those assurances were disputed because I had no written proof or the employee's name. Staff even gave conflicting dinner allowances: first £30, then £45. The message I took away was that the burden fell on me to prove what the hotel's own representative had said.

£134.50 DOUBLE-CHARGED — CONFIRMED IN WRITING

Although I had already paid for half board, the hotel added £45, £45 and £44.50 for three dinners. My payment came to £833.14 rather than £698.64 excluding those charges.

After I complained, the Assistant Front Office Manager confirmed IN WRITING that dinner was included and all three charges were mistakes. A £134.50 refund was promised. This was not a dispute about whether I had bought the meals: the hotel acknowledged that it had billed me for included dinners.

A CHECKOUT THAT BECAME A CHASE

At about 8am on 4 October, I challenged the charges. I was told to return at 9am, rushed breakfast and did so, only to be told reservations would not be available until Monday. The duty manager could not resolve the issue. I left around 9:30am; together with traffic, this contributed to a late arrival for a pre-booked Thorpe Park visit.

A Monday follow-up was promised but did not arrive as assured. I had to make repeated calls, wait on hold, be passed between departments and explain the same issue again. Promised callbacks and an email failed to materialise. It should not take this level of effort to get a hotel to rectify its own admitted billing error.

HOUSEKEEPING AND AFTERCARE

From what I observed, my bedding was not changed during the three-night stay. The bathroom had mould-like discolouration around the shower sealant and damage near the bottom of a wall. Even a toothbrush and toothpaste request required chasing.

I also asked for clarification about a separate £100 card pre-authorisation and for a corrected invoice. The hotel's initial reply acknowledged the inconvenience but did not substantively address my request for a goodwill remedy beyond repayment of the overcharge.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Mistakes happen. What matters is whether a business owns them promptly. Here, a documented billing error became hours of avoidable effort for the customer. Returning £134.50 is correction of an overcharge, not an answer to the wider failures.

My advice: obtain every booking assurance in writing, check restaurant charges daily and scrutinise your final invoice. I cannot recommend this hotel based on my experience.

reviews.text:
Disappointing stay – unacceptable standards for a 4-star hotel !

We stayed at Novotel London West for two nights with our family and our dog. Unfortunately, our experience was extremely disappointing, particularly regarding the cleanliness and overall condition of our room.

For a hotel advertised as four-star, we expected a much higher standard of accommodation.

The room showed numerous signs of poor maintenance and inadequate cleaning:

* A large, unsightly stain and damaged surface on the ceiling, suggesting previous water damage.
* Numerous cobwebs and accumulated dust around the windows.
* Dirty and marked walls, along with several noticeable stains on the carpet.
* A bathroom in poor condition, with discoloured seals, limescale, dirty fittings and visible signs of deterioration around the shower enclosure.
* A ventilation grille heavily covered in dust, which was particularly unpleasant and concerning from a hygiene perspective.

These were not isolated minor imperfections. The accumulation of these issues gave us the impression that the room had not received proper maintenance or a thorough deep clean for a considerable time.

We were also disappointed by our interaction with the receptionist, Divya. Although she was initially friendly, we felt pressured to leave a positive Google review mentioning her by name. We found this inappropriate and uncomfortable. Guests should be able to share their experiences freely, without feeling obliged to leave positive feedback.

However, we would like to acknowledge two positive aspects of our stay.

Firstly, the beds were comfortable, and we slept well.

Secondly, the gentleman welcoming guests at breakfast was particularly kind. He generously offered breakfast for our daughter, believing she was 15 years old when she was actually 16. We genuinely appreciated this thoughtful gesture and his friendly attitude.

Unfortunately, these positive experiences do not make up for the disappointing condition of the accommodation.

In our opinion, the room simply did not meet the standards expected of a four-star hotel. Cleanliness and proper maintenance should be fundamental priorities, not optional extras.

We hope the hotel management takes these comments seriously and makes the necessary improvements.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Divya at the reception was very helpful and kind.

I’m updating my original review now that we have experienced our full stay. At check-in, we were asked to leave a Google review and mention the receptionist’s name because she would receive a bonus. She was friendly and welcoming, but asking for a review before guests have experienced the hotel feels inappropriate. My initial review did not reflect the stay itself.

Unfortunately, we were very disappointed, particularly with the cleanliness. I have never seen a hotel room carpet with so many stains. The bathroom was not properly cleaned either: there were dried brown marks on the walls that we could remove ourselves with a wet wipe. The shower screen hinges and the seal along the bathtub were particularly dirty.

There were also several maintenance issues. The bathroom sink would only drain properly if we completely removed the plug, the fridge did not seem to work properly, and the safe was not secured in place and could simply be carried out of the room.

Our sleep was disturbed by other guests shouting in their rooms and running along the hallway from around 6:30 a.m.

Breakfast was disappointing for the price. The buffet felt limited and poorly thought through from a guest’s perspective. The pineapple and orange pieces still had their skin or rind attached, leaving guests to remove it with a small breakfast knife, while the other fruit was whole. The sliced cheese was stacked together in a block, making individual slices difficult to separate with the tongs provided. There were no small dishes for jam or syrup, so we ended up using a cereal bowl or an espresso cup to keep the syrup from spreading across the whole breakfast plate. The kitchen door also slammed shut loudly whenever staff passed through, repeatedly disrupting breakfast.

There were three positives: the comfortable beds, the friendly receptionist at check-in, and the kind member of staff checking room numbers and taking payments at breakfast. He initially offered our daughter free breakfast because he thought she was under 15. When we clarified that she was 16, he said, “You’re lucky I said that,” and still did not charge for her breakfast. We appreciated that gesture.

Unfortunately, those positives did not make up for the overall experience. We continued our trip to a two-star accommodation, and even that room was better than the one here. For a hotel advertised as four-star, the cleanliness, maintenance and value for money fell well below our expectations.

Room 4126, stayed 25–26 Sept 2026

Honestly, avoid this place.

We booked three nights at over £200 a night. First night in, I got woken up in the middle of the night absolutely itching — felt like something was crawling on me. Didn't sleep a wink. Even after we checked out, me and my son were still itching all over. They refunded the last two nights, but we paid for that first night ourselves. So basically we paid to get bitten.

The room was rough. The corridor's got about 70–80 rooms and just one sign, and you only find it after you turn a corner. The sealant round the bathroom was peeling and mouldy. The air con vent was caked in fluff. The bedding was really old and worn thin.

Breakfast wasn't great either — some plates were clean, some clearly weren't, all just stacked together.

Air con vents and old bedding are exactly where mites and bugs hide. If you do end up staying here, check the bed and the air con vent before you settle in. Wouldn't recommend it if you care about cleanliness.

reviews.text:
Novotel London West is a prominent, well-rated modern hotel catering to business travelers and families alike. Guest feedback consistently highlights its prime West London connectivity and spacious accommodations, alongside occasional notes regarding maintenance in older rooms.
​Customer Feedback Overview
​Location & Convenience: Highly praised for its excellent transport links. Guests consistently highlight the short 5-minute walk to Hammersmith Underground station, making travel around Central London and to Heathrow Airport straightforward.
​Service & On-Site Assistance: Guests mention attentive reception and concierge staff who help with navigation, local advice, transit applications, and quick room changes when issues arise.
​Dining & Amenities: Features on-site dining (including the Artisan restaurant) with good breakfast options and courteous waitstaff. Additional amenities include a gym, bar, and extensive conference facilities.
​Room Comfort & Feedback: Rooms are described as comfortable and unusually spacious for London. However, some guest reviews mention older room fittings (such as bathroom doors lacking locks) and occasional inconsistency with daily housekeeping replenishments.
​Directions & Transportation
​By Underground / Tube: Take the Piccadilly, District, or Hammersmith & City line to Hammersmith Station. From the station exit, walk approximately 3 to 5 minutes along Talgarth Road onto Shortlands.
​By Car & Parking: Located off the A4 (Talgarth Road). On-site underground parking is available for guests (subject to daily fees).
​From Airports: Direct access via the Piccadilly Line from Heathrow Airport directly to Hammersmith Station.
​On-Site Assistance & Services
​Front Desk & Concierge: 24-hour reception desk to assist with check-in, local travel recommendations, public transit guidance, and luggage storage prior to check-in or post check-out.
​Guest Services: Dedicated staff available on-site for immediate resolution of room preferences or maintenance requests.

reviews.text:
Extremely misleading parking charges and appalling handling of our complaint

Our stay at the Novotel West London was completely soured by what I consider to be an extremely misleading and predatory approach to parking.

We stayed for just one night, around 20 hours, and were charged £120 for parking.

The hotel's parking signage clearly states “Hotel residents £40 a day.” There is absolutely nothing on that signage to indicate that the £40 rate is only available if you have purchased a specific £40 parking package when booking your room. Naturally, we understood this to mean that, as hotel residents, we would pay £40 for a day's parking.

The information on Booking.com was equally misleading. When booking, it stated that parking was £40 per day and that reservation was not required. There was no clear warning that failing to purchase a particular parking package at the time of booking would result in a vastly higher charge.

When we checked in, nobody mentioned the parking arrangement, nobody asked whether we had purchased a parking package, and nobody warned us that parking would cost £120 rather than £40.

We only discovered the £120 charge when we came to leave.

We went back into the hotel to query it, at which point we were told that the £40 rate was apparently only available to guests who had purchased the £40 parking package when booking the room.

If that is genuinely the hotel's policy, it should be made completely and unambiguously clear at the point of booking, on the parking signage, and at check-in. It isn't reasonable to advertise parking to hotel residents at £40 per day, fail to explain the conditions attached to that price, say that a reservation isn't required, and then present a £120 bill when the guest leaves.

The fact that nobody mentioned this to us at check-in is particularly frustrating. Had someone simply said, “You've not purchased the parking package, so parking will be £120,” we could have made an informed decision about whether to leave the car elsewhere.

Instead, we were effectively presented with a £120 charge after the fact, when it was too late to make that choice.

Unfortunately, the way our complaint was handled made the situation even worse. The staff member we raised the issue with was incredibly defensive and dismissive. We felt that our concerns weren't being listened to and that we were simply being brushed off rather than having someone genuinely try to understand why we felt the charge was unreasonable and misleading.

Since leaving the hotel, we've also tried to contact them to speak to someone about the issue, but nobody answers the phone. So not only were we unable to resolve the matter when we were there, we've been unable to properly raise it with the hotel afterwards either.

For a major hotel chain, this is an unacceptable way to handle additional charges. Whether this is a deliberate pricing strategy or simply an incredibly poorly communicated policy, the result for the customer is the same: the advertised £40 parking price is not what many guests will actually end up paying.

I would strongly recommend anyone staying here checks the parking terms extremely carefully and gets the actual price confirmed in writing before leaving their car there.

The hotel itself may have been perfectly adequate, but a £120 parking charge for approximately 20 hours, following what we felt was seriously misleading information, combined with the dismissive way our complaint was handled, has completely ruined our experience.

This experience has also completely put me off staying at Novotel again. There are plenty of other hotel chains where I can stay without worrying that an apparently straightforward advertised charge will turn into a £120 bill because of a condition that wasn't made clear to me. After this experience, I have no intention of staying at another Novotel.

Worst hotel experience I’ve ever had. Absolutely shambolic from start to finish.

After travelling seven hours, I arrived expecting to check in at 3pm. I was told my room wasn’t ready and that someone would come and get me shortly. Almost three hours later, I was finally informed there had been an issue with a damaged bathroom tile. The hotel was fully booked, so there was no alternative room available. By this point, it was nearly 6:30pm, and I just wanted to get upstairs and rest before heading out for the evening.

Unfortunately, things only got worse.

Upon entering the room, I discovered the toilet wasn’t flushing properly, there were hairs on the bathroom floor, toilet handle and dressing table, and what appeared to be cigarette ash, along with a noticeable cigarette smell. As someone whose allergies are triggered by cigarette smoke, this was particularly unpleasant, and I woke up the following morning with a severely blocked nose and irritation.

I contacted reception, and the manager, Tam, came upstairs to inspect the room. To his credit, he was polite, understanding and genuinely tried his best to help throughout. He arranged for cleaners and maintenance to attend.

However, maintenance then spent approximately an hour, possibly longer, working behind the toilet, making considerable noise. I couldn’t relax or even use the room properly, so I had to leave and wait downstairs.

Once that was finally resolved, I discovered the air conditioning wasn’t working. The room was unbearably hot, with no windows that could be opened. Once again, I had to call reception and wait for maintenance, who began dismantling the air conditioning unit. By this point, it was approximately 8:15pm.

After everything I’d experienced, the hotel agreed to a complimentary breakfast and late checkout the following day.

You’d think that would be the end of it, but unfortunately not.

The following day, a female member of management knocked on my door and told me I needed to leave because I was past checkout time. I explained that Tam had personally agreed to a late checkout, but she insisted this wasn’t recorded on their system and claimed she didn’t know who Tam was.

She then began questioning me about his name, as though I should somehow know the identities of her colleagues. Fortunately, Tam had left me his business card with his name handwritten on it, which I showed her. She then suggested I might have meant somebody else.

Despite my explanation, she told me to get ready and leave quickly because the room needed to be prepared for the next guest.

The irony of being rushed out so the room could be ready for the next guest, after I’d been made to wait almost three hours for mine the previous day, was unbelievable.

I appreciate that Tam made an effort to resolve the problems, and I want to acknowledge his professionalism. Unfortunately, his efforts couldn’t make up for the overall experience.

After a seven-hour journey, all I wanted was a clean, comfortable room where I could rest. Instead, I spent much of my stay waiting around, dealing with maintenance, reporting cleanliness issues and being inconvenienced at every opportunity.

I paid for a hotel stay and received nothing but disruption, poor cleanliness and unacceptable service.

Extremely disappointing, and certainly not somewhere I would recommend or return to.

reviews.text:
Stayed on the 11th floor while I was in the city for a work conference.
Arrived at 7pm but was told I wouldn’t be able to check in until the rest of the guests arrived as all four booking were made on 1 card - which is less than ideal but that’s the process so fair enough.
Finally got into the room and was slightly disappointing especially considering my room had been upgraded to a ‘premium’. It was a very standard room which wouldn’t have been out of place on the Blackpool promenade, felt very tried with chipped and worn furniture, it didn’t particularly give me a clean or pleasant vibe. Not to mention my ‘double’ bed was two singles pushed together with a notable notch in the mattress between the two. Breakfast was also really not up to scratch, you’d be better off finding a Wetherspoons nearby and avoiding the £12.50 cost.

My biggest issue was the incredibly thin interconnecting doors in the rooms which allowed me to be woken up multiple times throughout the night from the nightmare next door, thin enough to the point I could quite easily hear next door talking on their phone in the morning as well as the ‘videos’ they were playing 🤦‍♂️ One thing I will say is the staff were quick to deal with the situation which was appreciated, although it hadn’t resolved anything.

Overall if this was a budget hotel I wouldn’t really bat an eye but for the prices they charge and the reputation as a ‘4 star’ hotel I was left massively disappointed.

reviews.text:
I had a truly excellent dining experience at this steakhouse, which stands out as a remarkable destination for anyone who appreciates outstanding food, an interesting setting, and a touch of sophistication.

Located in one of London’s most prestigious and expensive neighbourhoods, the restaurant certainly lives up to the expectations associated with its surroundings. The interior is particularly impressive, featuring an interesting and distinctive design that gives the place its own character. The atmosphere strikes a very pleasant balance between elegance and comfort, making it an enjoyable setting for a memorable evening.

The highlight of the visit, however, was undoubtedly the steak. I can confidently say that it was one of the best steaks I have had in quite some time. The quality of the meat was exceptional, the cooking was perfectly executed, and the flavour was absolutely outstanding. Every bite was a reminder of how impressive a properly prepared steak can be. It is always a pleasure to visit a restaurant where the quality of the main dish genuinely exceeds expectations.

The overall experience was thoroughly enjoyable, with the combination of excellent cuisine, distinctive surroundings, and an appealing atmosphere making a particularly strong impression.

London certainly has no shortage of excellent steakhouses, especially in its more exclusive neighbourhoods, but this establishment deserves recognition for delivering such a memorable dining experience.

I would be delighted to return and would wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone looking for a truly exceptional steak in an elegant and interesting setting.

The rooms were very dusty, and the cleaning was nowhere near the standard you would expect from a 5-star property. The furniture was also old and worn out, and some of the drawers weren’t even closing properly.

I specifically booked an executive room expecting a bigger and more spacious room, only to find out that the regular rooms were actually more spacious. This was very disappointing, especially considering the extra price paid for the executive room.

Anything you request or need delivered requires at least two phone calls and takes around an hour to arrive. One day, I requested towels and it took exactly 2 hours and 3 phone calls before they were finally delivered.

Overall, the service, cleanliness, room quality, and condition of the hotel were extremely disappointing. Definitely not worth the price and nowhere near the standard of a 5-star hotel. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

This is a tough hotel to rate and here's why.

The rooms are clean and well appointed, but not sound proof enough due to the guests who stay here.  We arrived to find the courtyard full of exotic cars:  lamborghinis, G wagons, GT3s etc.  We thought maybe an exotic car show was going on at the hotel.  It wasn't an exotic car show at all.  These were the cars of the guests WHO LIVE AT THE HOTEL.   More on the problem with the soundproofing later...

Check in was smooth and the staff welcoming and polite.  The location is good as it's walkable to many attractions within a 20 - 30 minute walk.  The problem was the other guests and the staff's seeming inability to do anything about it.

I understand that hotels cater to guests of many nationalities, cultures, and practices, however, common courtesy should be upheld despite your culture.  I was invisible.  The men of the predominant culture would push past me to get in and out of the elevators as if I didn't exist.  And when I say predominant, I mean the lobby looked like an embassy.  Okay, so you have no respect for women, but then, at midnight, the guests with the thunderous cars would go to the courtyard, idle their engines, rev them a lot, and then finally squeal off into the night.  This is unacceptable behavior no matter where you come from.  The next morning, we complained to the front desk clerk who disappeared into the back room for at least 10 minutes and then came out and said there was no room they could move us to.  This is an enormous hotel.  I find it very difficult to believe that there was no room further away from the courtyard to move us to.  Rather than have a policy prohibiting idling in the courtyard after 10pm, or speak with their guests with the loud cars, they chose the path of least resistance, simply tell the American guest at the American hotel, "no".   They were polite, but the answer was still no.  I guess the Marriott isn't going to mess with their bread and butter guests who live there.

When I'm a guest in a foreign land, I gladly adapt to the acceptable customs (like wearing modest clothing and a head covering at the Blue Mosque), but when foreigners travel to western lands, they get to do whatever they want?  That is not acceptable.  Western courtesies of allowing ladies to go first and maintaining quiet time after 10pm are what I expect in a western hotel.

That said, unless you're a night owl and love the sound of revving engines at midnight and enjoy getting shoved past in the elevator by rude men, avoid the JW Marriott Grosvenor House like the plague.  Worst nights stay ever at a luxury hotel.  Not Western or American friendly.

Extremely disappointing customer service and a complete lack of compassion.

Following a very enjoyable visit in 2024, We purchased a £500 voucher for The Ritz in London as a special gift for my mother-in-law and father-in-law to enjoy dinner together. Unfortunately, since purchasing the voucher, my mother-in-law has been diagnosed with liver cancer and is undergoing chemotherapy. Understandably, they are no longer in a position to enjoy the experience we had hoped to give them.

My wife contacted customer services to explain the circumstances, hoping that a little understanding and compassion might be shown, given the seriousness of the diagnosis. The matter was escalated to ‘Sal Gowili (the general manager) who ultimately refused to offer her any refund whatsoever. My wife even offered to provide an official letter from the Christie’s hospital to prove her condition, but to no avail. To add insult to industry, his suggestion was to extend the validity date on the voucher by 2 months. Given the gravity of my mother-in-laws diagnosis, I find the lack of empathy and total lack of tact to be completely unacceptable.

I fully appreciate that businesses have policies and terms and conditions, but there must surely be room for compassion when faced with circumstances as serious as a close family member being diagnosed with cancer and undergoing chemotherapy. We were not asking for anything unreasonable; we were simply hoping that a £500 gift, which could no longer be used due to circumstances entirely beyond our control, might be treated with some understanding.

For an establishment with the reputation and prestige of The Ritz, I found this response particularly disappointing. Luxury hospitality should be about more than the surroundings, the food and the price tag. It should also be about how people are treated, especially when they are dealing with something as devastating as cancer.

The refusal to offer even a gesture of goodwill has left a very bitter taste. What should have been a lovely gift for my wife’s parents has instead become an upsetting and frustrating experience at an already difficult time for our family.

Sadly, based on this experience, I would question whether The Ritz’s reputation for exceptional service extends to showing basic humanity and compassion when it really matters.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
I rarely write reviews, but this experience truly deserves one.

I was traveling solo from the USA on a work trip and decided to make a quick stop at The Ritz before heading out shopping. I wasn’t even aware that there are only three Ritz hotels in the world — Paris, London, and Madrid — so thank you, Felipe, for enlightening me!

From the moment I arrived, the service was absolutely immaculate.

I have to start with Alexandra, the sommelier. Coming from the Napa region and having had the opportunity to meet and know many sommeliers, I can honestly say that Alexandra is remarkable. She has an incredible ability to understand your palate and recommend exactly the right Champagne. Her knowledge, intuition, and genuine passion really stood out.

Then there was Felipe, the manager, who sincerely took the time to check on me and make sure I was having the best possible experience. And finally, Karen, an amazing waitress who not only provided wonderful service but also gave me some fantastic recommendations for my Champagne trip.

Each of them made such an impression that I would honestly come back to London just to visit them again. They turned what was supposed to be a quick stop into a truly memorable experience.

And a little tip: do not miss the Rothschild Brut — it’s a Ritz exclusive! 🥂

P.S. I very rarely take the time to write reviews, but this one absolutely earned its place.

My sister and I brought our Mum to the Ritz for afternoon tea to celebrate her 80th birthday; a gift given to her by her grandchildren in the form of a voucher, for £200.
Due to some health issues, for both Mum and her husband (who she cares for) the voucher was going to expire, so both myself and sister contacted the Ritz to explain and extend the £200 voucher by paying an additional £40.
They took the voucher code and booked us in. We were told nothing more.
When we arrived, we told our waiter we had a voucher, he said no problem, just show it when we pay.

We bought a bottle of champagne to celebrate Mums birthday, and the food was delicious.
However it was all ruined when we paid, as the Ritz wouldn’t accept our voucher, as it was out of date.
We had emails and booking information that we showed them, as proof that we could extend the voucher, but unfortunately the waitress and duty manager wouldn’t accept this.
We were embarrassed, humiliated and all 3 of us were in tears to be treated like this. We had travelled from Yorkshire, and stayed overnight in London to celebrate this occasion with our Mum, and that duty manager completely ruined our trip.

He apologised but would not listen to us, he said we needed to deal with the voucher company……which is the Ritz! He said his till would be down by £200 if he accepted the voucher, and we needed to deal with it afterwards and MAYBE we would get our money back.

We couldn’t believe we were treated like this, and no amount of apologies will change things.
I’d like to hear the owners opinion on our experience please
