I was refused entry because of the dress code and had to go out and buy a new outfit. However, I later noticed another customer having afternoon tea wearing exactly the same outfit as me, but dressed even more casually. This was very disappointing to see.

Even if that customer was a regular, I don’t think it is appropriate to treat guests differently based on who they are. Seeing such an obvious difference in treatment made me feel very uncomfortable and left a bad impression.

During the afternoon tea, my plate was cleared while I was still eating. I couldn’t understand why it was taken away so quickly, especially since it then took quite a long time for someone to come and take our payment.

Unfortunately, I also found the quality of the sweets underwhelming. I wasn’t particularly impressed with the attitude of the receptionist either, although the other staff members were kind and helpful.

The interior was very cute and charming, but overall, the experience was disappointing, especially considering how much emphasis was placed on the dress code.

reviews.text:
Unfortunately, our recent experience at The Ritz London was extremely disappointing and fell far below the standard we expected from such a prestigious hotel.

While we were sitting in the garden, a mouse appeared under our table. We appreciate that incidents involving wildlife can happen, but seeing a mouse so close to guests while dining was understandably unpleasant and raised concerns about hygiene and the overall guest experience.

What was even more disappointing, however, was the way we were treated afterwards.

During our visit, we were asked where we were from. We felt that the attitude towards us noticeably changed after we answered. We strongly believe that guests should be treated with the same courtesy and respect regardless of their nationality or background. Being asked about our nationality in itself was uncomfortable in this context, particularly because of the change in attitude that followed.

We also experienced an unpleasant interaction with security. We were recording a short video of a lady playing music. Security approached us in a very loud and rude manner and told us that we were not allowed to film people. We were not intentionally filming or interfering with anyone, and we found the way this was communicated unnecessarily aggressive.

The situation became even more uncomfortable when another customer approached and verbally disrespected us, calling us “beggars from the street” and telling us to “go back to the streets.” What was particularly disappointing was that security did not intervene to stop the customer’s disrespectful behaviour towards us. Instead, the focus remained on reprimanding us about filming.

We fully understand that a luxury hotel may have rules regarding photography and filming, and we are happy to respect reasonable requests when they are communicated politely. However, rules should be applied professionally and consistently, and guests should never be made to feel humiliated or discriminated against.

We visited The Ritz expecting a refined and respectful experience. Unfortunately, the treatment we received left us feeling unwelcome and deeply disappointed.

I hope the management will take this feedback seriously, review what happened with the staff and security involved, and ensure that all guests are treated with the level of courtesy, dignity and professionalism expected from The Ritz London.

The sandwiches were basic and I had to wait more than 35 minutes for some alternative milk – when I asked for the second time, the waiter looked around the table suspiciously for about five minutes before walking off to the kitchen to get some. The kitchen does not appear synced up with wait staff. At the price point of £95 pp, I felt it was underwhelming. It didn’t wow me as I expected. Having been to several other afternoon teas in London over the past few years I would not describe the Ritz as one which I would return to unless they materially improved quality of the food, the weight staff or broader experience. The other interesting aspect is my underwhelming experience isn’t isolated – reading through some of the other reviews, this appears to be a common thread. The Ritz customer services staff only seem to engage with the positive reviews here. What I did like was one of the macadamia nut sweets and the apricot cake.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
We had a very pleasant stay at the Marble Arch Hotel by Thistle, particularly appreciating its excellent location. Situated close to Oxford Street and Hyde Park, it is an ideal choice for those looking to enjoy London’s shopping, attractions, and beautiful green spaces, with many places conveniently accessible on foot.

The reception team were exceptionally friendly, welcoming, and professional, with special mention to Bianca, who was particularly warm, attentive, and helpful throughout our stay. Her professionalism and genuine hospitality made us feel very welcome from the moment we arrived.

Our room was clean, tidy, comfortable, and well maintained, with effective air conditioning. The bathroom was also spotless, with soft, quality towels and consistently hot water available 24/7, which added considerably to the overall comfort of our stay.

The only area that could benefit from some attention is the furniture and interior décor, which feel somewhat dated compared with more contemporary hotels. However, this did not significantly detract from our overall experience.

Overall, the hotel offers a comfortable and convenient stay, an outstanding location, and genuinely welcoming service. A special thank you to Bianca and the reception team for making our stay so enjoyable. We would be very happy to return and would highly recommend the hotel to anyone looking for a well-located base in central London.

reviews.text: We stayed here as part of an Insite Tour, both for 2 days beginning and 1 day at the end of our trip 3 weeks apart. We got to the hotel around noon and were told a room would be ready for us at 1:00. It was and with no extra charge for early check in. Both rooms were very nice and clean. The included breakfast buffet was very good with an extensive variety of items. Servers brought coffee/tea to the table and were quick to remove used items and ask if we needed anything. Tony at the front door was very friendly and helpful both times assisting with luggage. Food at the on-site restaurant was very good and reasonably priced. My only complaint is about the service elevators. There are 2 and 1 was out of service during both stays-3 weeks apart. It is the ONLY option to bring luggage from the first floor to ground level other than carrying it down an entire flight of stairs which I physically cannot do. The working elevator is also used by staff to transport supplies, laundry, etc as well as mobility scooters, wheelchairs and baby strollers. At the end of both stays it took us at least 10-15 minutes to go down 1 floor.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
This was an absolutely unpleasant stay.

The housekeeping standards were shockingly poor. The beds and sheets did not appear properly cleaned or changed, and the overall condition of the bedding was disgusting. For a hotel charging guests to stay here, basic cleanliness should be the absolute minimum not something guests have to repeatedly ask for.

Trying to reach housekeeping or even the operator was another nightmare. You can barely get anyone to answer, and when you finally do, some staff speak to you in a rude and dismissive manner.

I requested a simple dental kit and it took TWO HOURS to arrive. Two hours for a dental kit is ridiculous and says everything about the level of service in this hotel.

To make matters worse, one of the elevators had apparently been broken for more than a week, leaving only three elevators operating. Guests were constantly suffering because of the delays, yet hotel management seemed unable or unwilling to resolve the situation.

I genuinely struggle to find anything positive to say about this stay. The only good thing about this hotel is its location. Everything else from cleanliness and housekeeping to customer service, responsiveness, and maintenance was terrible.

For a hotel in such a good location, the level of service is embarrassingly poor. I would absolutely not stay here again.

reviews.text:
I stayed at this hotel from 16 to 23 September 2026. My wallet was inside my hotel room throughout my stay, and I did not take it outside the room at any point.

After returning to Saudi Arabia, I discovered that my wallet was missing. I then noticed multiple unauthorized transactions on my bank card on 23 September, including transactions at London Overground, King’s Cross ticket machines and a Co-op store. I was already travelling back to Saudi Arabia at the time and did not make or authorize these transactions.

I am extremely concerned about how my wallet could have gone missing from inside my room. I expect the hotel to investigate all individuals who had access to my room, including housekeeping, room service and any other hotel personnel who entered the room during my stay.

I am requesting that the hotel immediately preserve and review CCTV footage, room access/key-card records, housekeeping records and room service records for the entire period of my stay, from 16–23 September 2026.

I have already contacted my bank to dispute the unauthorized transactions and am taking the appropriate steps to report the incident to the relevant authorities.

This is a serious security matter, and I expect a formal written response and a proper investigation, rather than this being treated simply as a lost-property case.

I will also be formally reporting this matter to the Saudi Embassy in London and the relevant authorities, and I will provide them with the details of the incident, the unauthorized transactions, and my hotel booking.

بعد عودتي إلى السعودية اكتشفت اختفاء محفظتي، ثم لاحظت وجود عدة عمليات غير مصرح بها على بطاقتي البنكية بتاريخ 23 سبتمبر، من ضمنها عمليات في London Overground وماكينات تذاكر King’s Cross ومتجر Co-op. وفي ذلك الوقت كنت بالفعل في رحلة عودتي إلى السعودية، ولم أقم بأي من هذه العمليات.

لذلك لدي مخاوف جدية جدًا بشأن كيفية اختفاء المحفظة من داخل غرفتي، وأطلب من إدارة الفندق التحقيق مع جميع الأشخاص الذين كان لديهم صلاحية الدخول إلى غرفتي، بما في ذلك موظفي التدبير الفندقي (Housekeeping) وخدمة الغرف (Room Service) وأي موظف آخر دخل الغرفة خلال فترة إقامتي.

أطلب من الفندق بشكل عاجل الحفاظ على ومراجعة كاميرات المراقبة، وسجلات بطاقات/مفاتيح دخول الغرفة، وسجلات الـHousekeeping وسجلات Room Service للفترة كاملة من 16 إلى 23 سبتمبر 2026.

لقد بدأت بالفعل إجراءات الاعتراض على العمليات غير المصرح بها مع البنك، كما أتخذ الإجراءات اللازمة لإبلاغ الجهات المختصة.

The worst experience and by far the worst hotel I have ever dealt with in Europe!

We arrived at the hotel late at night, only to be shocked and extremely frustrated to find out that the hotel management had cancelled our reservation without informing us in advance.

When we confronted the staff and asked for an explanation, they casually told us that they had cancelled the booking three hours earlier — yet no one bothered to contact us or notify us in any way!

What makes this situation even more unacceptable is that three different families experienced exactly the same problem: another family was affected on the same day as us, and another family had the exact same issue the day before.

The reception staff were extremely rude, unprofessional, and completely unhelpful. They refused to have a proper discussion or even listen to our concerns. To make matters worse, one of the receptionists actually told us that we could sit in the lobby and look for another hotel ourselves!

Absolutely unacceptable treatment, especially after arriving late at night and expecting a confirmed reservation. The whole experience was incredibly frustrating, disappointing, and stressful.

I would strongly advise anyone to think twice before booking this hotel.

reviews.text:
The hotel has an amazing location, and the staff were genuinely incredible. Everyone we interacted with was friendly, helpful, and professional, which made the stay much more pleasant. Unfortunately, the hotel itself had several issues that significantly affected our experience.

The elevators were by far the biggest problem. One elevator seemed to be broken almost constantly, and the remaining elevator was extremely busy, especially at night. On one occasion, both elevators were out of service at the same time, leaving us essentially stuck and forcing us to use the stairs. This was particularly frustrating.

The room was also very small and barely had enough space for two people to move around comfortably. More importantly, the sheets were not properly clean, which was disappointing and something I would expect a hotel to get right.

Overall, the location is excellent and the staff deserve a lot of credit for their service. However, the issues with the elevators, room size, and cleanliness made the stay considerably less comfortable than expected. With improvements to these basic facilities and housekeeping standards, this hotel could offer a much better experience.

reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Stay – Poor Service and Unprofessional Staff

This was not my first stay at The Cumberland Hotel in London, but unfortunately, it was by far the worst. The decline in service, housekeeping standards, and staff attitude was shocking for a four-star hotel.

Something as basic as a vanity kit became an issue. I received one the previous evening, yet the following day, the staff claimed they didn’t even know what it was. When I explained this to the receptionist, she rudely responded, “Why are you arguing with me?” Simply explaining a situation should not be considered arguing.

Housekeeping was equally disappointing throughout my six-night stay. Personal belongings and pyjamas were carelessly thrown around, empty bottles and used tissues were left behind, and the bathroom was not properly cleaned. I will be attaching photos as evidence.

Despite repeatedly reporting these issues and speaking to the hotel manager twice, nothing improved. Every complaint was met with promises of an “investigation,” but no actual resolution. The manager mentioned having around six years of experience at the hotel, yet even basic service issues remained unresolved.

What disappointed me most was the complete lack of accountability or even a sincere apology from management. Ironically, the only person who genuinely tried to make things right was someone from the housekeeping team, which I appreciated.

Mistakes can happen, but how a hotel handles them says everything about its standards. As a returning guest, I expected professionalism, cleanliness, and respect. Instead, I felt dismissed and unwelcome throughout my stay.

Extremely disappointing experience. I would not recommend this hotel and certainly would not stay here again.

What I Liked:

* The location is absolutely excellent.
* The service is fast and efficient.
* The price is relatively reasonable.
* The hotel may be particularly suitable for families with children, as it offers connecting rooms.
* The air conditioning works very well and is quiet.

What I Didn’t Like:

* Like many hotels in London, the room was smaller and the overall standard was lower than I would expect. By our standards, I would rate it as a 2- or 3-star hotel rather than a luxury hotel.
* I paid extra for a room advertised as overlooking Hyde Park, but the actual view was of Oxford Street instead.
* The bedroom had a connecting door to the neighbouring room, and noise travelled easily between the rooms. We could hear our neighbours, and they could probably hear us too, which significantly reduced our privacy.
* The bed was uncomfortable because it appeared to consist of two single beds and mattresses pushed together.
* The shower was a very small, prefabricated unit. Turning on and adjusting the shower water was also unnecessarily difficult.
* No bidet spray was provided, and the hotel does not offer one.
* Slippers and toothbrushes were available only upon request.
* The wall artwork was very poor and unattractive.
* The lighting system was uncomfortable and not user-friendly.

Overall: The hotel’s location and fast service were its strongest points. However, the small room, misleading view, uncomfortable bed, poor shower design, and lack of basic bathroom amenities made the overall experience less satisfactory than expected, especially considering the price paid.

reviews.text:
Dear Hotel Management,

I honestly do not know how to adequately express my shock and disappointment regarding what happened to me during my stay at your hotel. In all my years of travelling and staying in hotels, I have never experienced anything so disturbing, unacceptable, and unprofessional.

On the final night of my stay, I contacted the reception desk to request a late check-out. I was informed that the standard check-out time was 11:00 AM, but that an exception would be made, allowing me to stay until 12:00 PM. I thanked the staff member for this arrangement and returned to my room, under the clear understanding that I had been granted this additional time.

However, at approximately 11:20 AM the following morning, something completely unacceptable occurred. A member of your staff knocked on my door and proceeded to open it, despite the fact that I had placed the “Do Not Disturb” sign on the door. The staff member then called out to me.

I cannot begin to explain how frightened and alarmed I was by this incident. I was asleep, and suddenly found myself in a situation where a hotel employee had knocked on my door, opened it, and called out to me despite the Do Not Disturb sign being displayed. This was a deeply unsettling experience that made me feel that my privacy and personal security had been disregarded.

When I approached the door, the staff member informed me that my check-out time was approaching and that I would have to pay if I wished to extend my stay. Given that I had just been startled awake and was still shaken by what had happened, I immediately paid the additional charge at the door.

I would like to raise two very serious questions:

1. Was this employee authorised to enter or open the door to my room under these circumstances, particularly when the “Do Not Disturb” sign was clearly displayed?
2. On what grounds does your hotel consider it acceptable for a member of staff to approach a guest in this manner, rather than contacting the guest by telephone to clarify their check-out arrangements?

The appropriate and professional course of action would have been to contact me by telephone, establish whether I intended to check out or extend my stay, and settle any additional charges accordingly. There was absolutely no justification for handling the situation in such a disturbing and intrusive manner without first attempting to contact me.

Let me be absolutely clear: this behaviour falls far below the standards of professionalism, courtesy, and respect that any hotel guest has the right to expect. It was not only discourteous but also deeply concerning in terms of guest privacy and the way your staff are trained to handle such situations.

I find it particularly unacceptable that, despite having been granted a late check-out arrangement, I was subjected to this distressing experience instead of being treated with basic consideration and respect.

I therefore expect the hotel management to take this complaint seriously, conduct a thorough investigation into the incident, establish why the employee acted in this manner, and explain what measures will be taken to ensure that no other guest is subjected to similar treatment.

If your hotel genuinely values its reputation, its guests’ comfort, and the trust placed in its staff, then this matter must not be dismissed or treated as a minor misunderstanding. I expect a formal response addressing the specific concerns raised in this complaint, including the unauthorised opening of my room door despite the Do Not Disturb sign.

I expect a clear explanation, accountability, and appropriate action—not a generic apology.

I look forward to your response.

Yours sincerely,
A Disappointed Guest

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience — third stay, and unfortunately the last

This was my third stay at The Cumberland Hotel in London, but based on this experience, it will unfortunately be my last.

Our check-in was on 26 September 2027, and the hotel’s system was down for approximately two hours. During this time, the only refreshments offered were soft drinks or water.

Our reservation clearly stated that we had two rooms:

* One room with a double bed for two people
* One room with a single bed for one person

We also made a clear request for the two rooms to be on the same floor.

During check-in, the receptionist was a trainee and initially refused to provide the two rooms on the same floor, despite our reservation and request being clear. After approximately one hour of discussion and negotiation, they eventually agreed.

Unfortunately, when we entered the rooms, we discovered that the wrong room had been assigned to us. When we raised the issue, we were told that the room could not be changed that day because the system was down.

On 27 September, we returned to reception. The staff acknowledged that the room provided was not the room we had reserved and was not suitable for two people. However, instead of simply correcting the booking, we were asked to pay an additional £30 per day for another room, or to come back the following day to see what could be done.

Then, on 28 September at approximately 22:45, we returned again. Unfortunately, the interaction with the staff (specially the shift manager at this time) was extremely frustrating. Initially, we were told that the double bed was a queen-size bed and that we simply had to accept it. We were then told that there were rooms available but that the hotel was fully booked. Despite the fact that we had already paid for the room we had originally reserved, there was no meaningful attempt to resolve the issue.

The attitude of the staff was particularly disappointing. When I explained that this would be my last stay and that I intended to leave a review, I was told, “It’s up to you, do whatever you want.” This response was especially disappointing considering that this was my third stay at the hotel.

There were also serious problems with the condition of the room:

* The room was not properly cleaned when we arrived.
* The toilet seat was covered with dirt and hair. I have photographs as evidence.
* When we asked housekeeping to inspect it, the housekeeper herself appeared shocked by the condition of the bathroom. No apology was offered.
* On other occasions, housekeeping cleaned the room but failed to leave towels, despite this being specifically requested.
* The in-room safety deposit box was not working, which is a significant concern because guests rely on it to safely store valuables. This should have been repaired promptly.

Overall, the biggest disappointment was not simply the technical problem with the hotel’s system. Technical issues can happen. The real problem was the lack of effective communication, the repeated failure to provide the room that had been reserved and paid for, the request for additional payment to correct their own mistake, the cleanliness issues, and the attitude of some members of staff when we asked for help.

After three stays at The Cumberland, I expected much better. Unfortunately, this experience has completely changed my view of the hotel, and I will not be returning.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously, particularly regarding reservation accuracy, room cleanliness, housekeeping standards, staff communication, and customer service.

reviews.text:
Claridge’s has been a favourite of mine since childhood, when my grandmother used to bring me here for tea. It is one of those rare places that carries memories with you, and so many years later, it still has the ability to delight the soul. There is a warmth and graciousness to Claridge’s that feels increasingly rare today. The service is not simply efficient; it is delivered with a sense of pride, discretion and genuine care that makes you feel you are somewhere special.

On a slightly amusing note, we had been corresponding with Thomas prior to our arrival regarding the restaurants. When we arrived at the hotel, the concierge called for Thomas, and when he came down to meet us, we naturally assumed it was the same Thomas we had been corresponding with.

There was clearly some confusion on his part about our conversation, but rather than question it or point out that something seemed amiss, he simply went along with it and graciously honoured what the original Thomas had proposed. It was only later, when we sat down for a drink, that the penny dropped: there are actually two Thomases at Claridge’s, and the concierge had summoned the Managing Director rather than the Thomas we had been dealing with!

What impressed me most was the way Thomas handled the entire situation. He never once acknowledged the mix-up or made us feel that we had somehow ended up with the wrong person. He simply rolled with it, took care of us and handled everything with such natural warmth and professionalism that we only understood what had happened afterwards.

And perhaps that is what I love most about Claridge’s. The service feels personal. There is a genuine sense that people care about the experience they are creating for their guests, and a level of grace and discretion that is increasingly difficult to find. Thomas was a wonderful example of that. It was a funny little misunderstanding, but he handled it beautifully—and left us with yet another memorable Claridge’s moment.

reviews.text:
Disappointing cleanliness and no response from guest relations

The cleanliness of our room was disappointing. The shower door was almost fully covered in limescale , and there were black spots that looked like mould around the edges of the sink and bathtub.

The coffee cups were also not properly washed. After housekeeping cleaned our room, everything had been put back neatly, just as it was when we checked in. However, when we opened the drawer to get cups for tea and coffee, we found visible coffee residue from the previous day. It looked as though the cups had only been briefly rinsed before being put away.

We raised these concerns at the front desk, hoping they would be addressed so other guests would not have the same experience. We were advised to email guest relations, which we did. More than a month later, we still have not received a reply.

Clean cups and a clean bathroom are basic expectations. The lack of any response made an already disappointing experience even worse.

The only staff we feel deserve our thanks are the room service team who delivered tasty food we've ordered and the lady who looked after the spa and pool area was friendly.

reviews.text: We’ve stayed at this hotel multiple times over the last six years.  The rooms are absolutely wonderful; clean,  pristine and modern.   Our last room had a soaking tub as well as the shower, which was great.  Every time we’ve stayed here, the rooms have been quiet.  There are so many interesting places to visit, and everything is a walk away.  The staff are always very friendly and super helpful.  We paid a little extra (£35 per couple) for breakfast in the restaurant. This was the only thing that could be improved upon.  it’s very chaotic, and the menu is a little old-fashioned compared with what you can get in restaurants these days. There were lots of sweet pastries, and even the oatmeal was sweet and creamy.  There wasn’t a good selection of fruit - just some cut up melon.  I would’ve loved some unsweetened granola, zero fat Greek yogurt, honey, and good fruit. We will definitely continue to stay at this hotel in the future.

My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel because of the reviews it had. It met our expectations tenfold.

The rooms were clean and roomy. Has all the necessities. The service is top notch, from the reception to the room service to the breakfast. I highly recommend you include the breakfast in your stay. We added the breakfast the day of, after seeing the spread it offered.

The next day we had our breakfast, we were greeted with such kindness and care. The hospitality and the attentiveness caught me off guard! Did not expect it. Our waitress Irene, was magnificent, she brought us eggs and pancakes, and since we had a small table, she moved us (mind you I didn’t even realize it) to a bigger table, just so we aren’t uncomfortable with all the plates on the small 2 person table. She constantly checked up on us and made sure we were doing well and enjoying the food. Y’all better give her a raise for her hard work!

A little shout out to Abu for noticing we wanted crispy bacon and coming up to us and telling us he can accommodate that, and continuously checking in on us. You need to make sure you keep them happy here Riverbank hotel!

The location is really nice. Not too far from anything. You are right next to a bus stop which can take you anywhere for really cheap instead of using a taxi or uber/lyft.

Highly recommend staying here. Def a spot I will be retuning to!

reviews.text:
I stayed at the Royal Lancaster three times this summer for work, and I definitely plan to return regularly.

It’s honestly one of my favourite hotels in London. The atmosphere is very relaxing, the rooms are comfortable, the beds are excellent, and the cleanliness is absolutely impeccable. I’m extremely particular about cleanliness, and I really couldn’t find anything to complain about, whether in the rooms or the common areas.

I also love the Hyde Café, which is excellent.

What I particularly appreciate is the staff. You can really tell they are well trained. Everyone is professional, attentive and genuinely pleasant. It’s the kind of service that makes you want to come back.

The Landmark has always been another favourite hotel of mine in London, so I was quite surprised to discover that both hotels belong to the same group. Having stayed at both, I’m honestly not surprised anymore, as the quality of service is equally impressive.

I’ve had a wonderful experience every time I’ve stayed here, and I look forward to coming back.

We had such a wonderful stay with our eight-month-old baby and could not recommend the Royal Lancaster enough, particularly for families travelling with children.

The attention to detail was exceptional from before we even arrived. The hotel contacted us to ask what we might need for our baby, and when we arrived, they had already placed a diaper genie and bottle steriliser in our room without us even asking and our baby was welcomed with his own beautiful Bobby teddy and special greeting card, accompanied by flowers in the room. Such thoughtful touches made our stay feel incredibly special.

What stood out most was how genuinely welcome we felt as a family. For example, at breakfast, a highchair was always provided, and when our baby got a little loud while eating, the staff immediately reassured me not to worry. Every member of staff we encountered was so sweet with him, and we never once felt that having a baby with us was an inconvenience or that we were somewhere we shouldn’t be.The warmth of the staff and their attention to detail made all the difference. We felt so well looked after.

reviews.text:
Delicious Cakes, but Absolutely Dreadful Service

The cakes and food were genuinely delicious, but unfortunately, the service was absolutely dreadful and completely ruined what should have been a lovely afternoon tea experience.

My friends and I spent over £300 on afternoon tea, and frankly, I would have been more than happy to spend £500 if the service had matched the quality of the food. Unfortunately, it was nowhere near the standard one would expect from an establishment charging premium prices.

At one point, while I was briefly checking my phone, a plate in front of me was removed without anyone even asking whether I had finished. Before I knew it, the food had been packaged for takeaway, despite my intention to enjoy it at the table. This was both unprofessional and incredibly frustrating.

Throughout our visit, we felt as though the staff were more concerned with getting customers out before 6 pm than ensuring they had an enjoyable experience. Rather than feeling welcomed and relaxed, we felt rushed, uncomfortable and unnecessarily stressed.

Beautiful presentation and delicious food mean very little when the service and attitude of the staff fail so spectacularly.

I would strongly recommend investing in proper staff training or reconsidering the recruitment of individuals who clearly lack the hospitality skills expected at this price point.

A premium afternoon tea experience should be about much more than beautiful plates and delicious cakes. It should make guests feel valued, welcomed and comfortable.

Sadly, the food was exceptional, but the hospitality was anything but.

I recently stayed at The Landmark London. It’s a very large hotel with lots of rooms and a really beautiful lobby. The interior is quite impressive, especially the main entrance and public areas.

The hotel feels a little dated in some places, but overall it’s well maintained, clean and comfortable. From what I could see, it also seems to be a popular place for business meetings, conferences and corporate events.

What really surprised me, though, was the minibar — completely empty! No drinks at all, which is quite unusual for a five-star hotel. There was coffee in the room, but the selection of bathroom amenities was also rather limited for a hotel of this category.

Apart from these details, everything was perfectly fine, and overall I had a pleasant stay.

reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and concerning experience.

I would strongly recommend reconsidering this hotel if your privacy and security are important to you.

Early one morning, while I was asleep, a man entered my room through the connecting door from the adjacent room, which had not been properly secured by the hotel. I woke up to find a man inside my room — an extremely frightening and unacceptable experience.

After the hotel was notified, they eventually came to my room, apologized, and offered a refund for one night. I did not accept this as an adequate resolution and asked them to reconsider and escalate the matter to senior management.

I submitted a formal complaint and followed up by email more than once, including asking them to clarify who this man was and whether he was a member of hotel staff. Unfortunately, I have still received no explanation, no response, and no refund or compensation.

For a five-star hotel, basic privacy and security should be non-negotiable. What is even more concerning is that the hotel has still not properly addressed what happened.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Don't book The Landmark if you're getting married! On arrival at 6pm the night before my wedding at Marylebone Town Hall, I was told they'd overbooked and they were moving us to their sister hotel.

I explained we couldn't be moved, as 1. we had arranged for everyone to get ready (makeup, hair, family/friends) at The Landmark, and 2. we specifically booked The Landmark so that we could walk over the to the venue (the sister hotel half an hour away).

They eventually told us they would find a room for us and we were repeatedly told it would just be 'another 20 minutes'. We waited in the lobby for 3 hours. This was annoying enough in itself. If they were honest from the outset we could have made other plans. Super bleak to spend the night before your wedding waiting in a lobby.

They gave us a room around 9pm. We had booked a suite. The room they gave us was tiny. It was super stuffy and honestly felt like a broom closet they had cleared out for us. The air-conditioner was directly above us and blasting in our faces. We couldn't turn it off.

Ultimately we decided to go home at 2am. As I left, I told the receptionist they needed to provide us with a suite the following day so we had adequate space to get ready.

I arrived back at The Landmark the following morning. They had not moved us. I called multiple times between 10am and 12pm to chase them. Again, we were told repeatedly 'someone will come and give you your new keys in 20 minutes'. H&MU arrived at 12pm and eventually the receptionist gave me the new room number and we all stood outside until someone came with the keys. Had I not chased them repeatedly, they never would have moved us.

The following day we checked out. I was told the manager would call me to discuss the situation, which was fine because we didn't want this mess to consume any more of our headspace over our wedding weekend. No one did call me, but eventually I called them a week later. They offered me a 'complimentary stay' as compensation. Why on earth would I want to go back there lol. They told me they couldn't refund me directly because I booked through a third party, and to go through them.

A couple of weeks later I did go through the third party. I asked for a refund because what we paid for was not what was provided - basic Consumer Rights law, right? I was told The Landmark has refused to refund the stay on the basis that I moved to their sister hotel. I clarified this was not the case multiple times and never heard anything back.

My rack of lamb was served cold and bland; we later realised that its sauce had mistakenly been given to my wife. The response was disappointing: the partly eaten lamb was reheated and returned with a replacement potato stack, rather than a fresh dish. A manager eventually offered a new plate, but said it would take around 20 minutes, by which time my wife was already well into her meal.
At £208 without wine, the food showed promise but was badly let down by service and by the handling of a fairly straightforward problem. We had intended it as a post-hospital-appointment treat and were relieved it was not a special occasion.

I am half-way through my stay at the London Hilton on Park Lane and have regretted my choice of hotel. As a Diamond member, I have stayed at the Trafalgar and many other Hilton hotels in the US. I have never experienced such inconsistent service, nor been treated like a criminal simply because I charged a Sunday lunch for my family of 7,  to my room.

1. Upon my arrival on 30 September, with 4 pieces of luggage and 2 backpacks, I observed 2 porters standing outside chatting. No one came to help so I had to get the luggage cart from inside the lobby, load my luggage and bring it into the front desk. Only then did one porter show up saying that he and his colleague were helping someone with directions. Does it take two porters to help one person with directions?

2. My wife and I had a late dinner at the Park Corner Brasseriecon 2 October. We were shown to our table where we sat, and sat, and sat. I observed 3 servers clearing up and preparing for the next morning's service. I eventually had to ask if we could be served.

3. I hosted my family for a Sunday Roast at the Park Corner Brasserie on 4 October. The host at the front of the restaurant informed me that I could add the charge to my room. Less than 24 hours later, a notice was slipped under my room door reminding me that I had an unpaid balance that needed to be paid "at my earliest convenience"!!!

Am I someone who would abscond without paying my bill??? More so, since this was only half way through my stay, AND MY AMERICAN EXPRESS CREDIT CARD IS ON FILE!!! I regard this as an insult to my integrity, and have never experienced this at any Hilton establishments in any other country.

In closing, I have received exceptional service from Sophie Rawlinson and Abdel Elsayeh. Unfortunately their service has done little to overcome my disappointment at the poor service that I experienced thus far. I will never return to this establishment given the other Hilton Hotels in London.

reviews.text:
My stay at Hilton London Park Lane was an extremely disappointing experience, and I genuinely regret choosing this hotel.
The most serious issue was the air conditioning, which was not working properly. The room became extremely hot and uncomfortable, particularly with my children, one of whom has asthma. I reported this repeatedly, yet the problem was not properly resolved. Instead, I was eventually offered a fan.
What made this even more frustrating was meeting another guest experiencing the same air-conditioning problem, who told me that his room had been changed without difficulty. When I raised this with staff, I received no satisfactory explanation for the apparent difference in treatment. I cannot know why this happened, but as a guest, it left me with a strong impression of unequal treatment.
The noise was another major issue. There was repeated shouting and significant noise around the room, including late at night. We reported it, including to security, but it was not adequately addressed. I understand that hotels cannot control every guest, but there is a difference between normal hotel activity and allowing behaviour that prevents other guests from resting.
Housekeeping was also deeply disappointing. The room was not serviced consistently and we repeatedly had to follow up. I also had concerns about the cleanliness of the bedding and bathrooms. More seriously, during the stay, personal makeup items belonging to my wife went missing from the room. I cannot state who was responsible or make an accusation without proof, but the fact remains that personal belongings disappeared during our stay. This is extremely concerning in any hotel.
I also had concerns regarding privacy, as there were occasions when staff appeared able to enter despite the “Do Not Disturb” sign being displayed.
The Guest Relations experience was equally disappointing. I found the attitude dismissive when I was raising a genuine issue affecting my family. At check-out, we were also initially told that breakfast was not included, despite it being included in our booking, and there was a significant delay before anyone assisted with our luggage.
For a hotel of this standing, these are not minor inconveniences. Air conditioning, hygiene, security, privacy, quiet and proper handling of complaints are fundamental.
I hope Hilton London Park Lane takes these issues seriously and reviews how guests are being treated.
Some staff members were helpful, but overall, the experience was unacceptable. I would not recommend this hotel to my friends or family, and I would not stay here again.

reviews.text:
Housekeeping entered while I was undressed — management told me I should have used the privacy sign

This afternoon, a member of housekeeping entered my room while I was changing.

He says he knocked three times. I have no reason to dispute that. I had been in the bathroom and simply did not hear him.

That is precisely the problem.

When I raised the incident, I was told that rooms are serviced every third day between noon and 6pm, and the duty manager pointed out that I could have placed the privacy sign on my door.

I accept that I had not done so. But surely the absence of a privacy sign cannot mean that a hotel guest should expect someone to enter their bedroom simply because they don’t hear a knock.

A guest could be showering, using the bathroom, asleep, wearing headphones or changing clothes.

I was changing clothes.

I want to be clear that I am not accusing the housekeeper of improper intent. My concern is the hotel’s procedure and, particularly, management’s response afterwards.

Security showed me footage, but whether the employee knocked once or three times misses the point. What safeguard exists when a guest is inside the room but does not hear housekeeping knocking?

I have travelled extensively around the world and have never experienced this. What I expected afterwards was empathy, an unequivocal apology and an assurance that the procedure would be reviewed. Instead, much of the conversation focused on the fact that staff had followed procedure and that I could have used the privacy sign.

A privacy sign should provide an additional layer of protection. Its absence should not be the thing standing between a guest getting dressed and an unexpected entry into their room.

I hope Millennium reviews this procedure and responds with the unqualified apology this situation deserves.

Until then, I cannot recommend this hotel to anyone for whom privacy and feeling secure in their room are fundamental expectations.

One of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had.

The first room I was given was completely unlivable. It had a horrific, overpowering smell of mold, and the window was left wide open upon arrival—which clearly showed they were already aware of the issue. When I walked out, a cleaner by the hallway even admitted that this specific room is known to be problematic.

I went to the front desk to complain, and there was not even a single apology. They just casually said they would move me to another room, acting completely unsurprised as if they knew about it all along. How can you knowingly put a guest in a room like that?

The second room they gave me smelled strongly of cigarette smoke mixed with heavy air freshener trying to cover it up. At that point, the reception suddenly tried to be "nice" and offered to upgrade me to a suite, but I was completely exhausted and done with this place. I packed my bags, left, and booked another place. Completely unacceptable service and conditions.

reviews.text:
A wonderful stay thanks to an exceptionally professional and friendly team!

We stayed at The President Hotel in London with our son, and we can wholeheartedly recommend this hotel.

Unfortunately, there was an issue with our Booking.com reservation, which meant that our room had been booked for two adults only, instead of two adults and one child. Although it was unclear exactly where the mistake had occurred, the team at The President Hotel did everything they could to find a solution for us. And they certainly succeeded!

What impressed us most was the exceptional friendliness, professionalism and customer service of the staff. To compensate for the inconvenience, we were offered a complimentary drink at the bar, as well as breakfast for our entire stay, at the hotel's expense. Such a thoughtful gesture that we truly appreciated! The hotel is also incredibly child-friendly, which makes travelling with a young child so much more enjoyable.

Our room was clean and well maintained, and it was clear that the hotel genuinely cares about making every guest's stay as comfortable and pleasant as possible.

The breakfast buffet also deserves a special mention. There was a wide variety of options, everything was beautifully presented and well looked after, and there was certainly no chance of leaving hungry!

All in all, this is a hotel where genuine hospitality is still a priority. The way the team handled an unexpected situation made all the difference to our experience. A huge thank you to everyone who went above and beyond to make our stay so enjoyable.

Thank you for a wonderful experience. We will definitely be back on our next visit to London!

Poor value for money and well below expectations.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Pros:
The room is spacious, tidy, clean, and smells nice. The lighting throughout the room is bright and good, which is definitely an advantage. There are USB ports near the bed for charging phones, which is very useful. In the bathroom, there is plenty of space to place items above the sink, and the lighting there is also good. The water pressure in the shower is excellent, and the toilet has a quiet, soft-close seat. The internet is good, stable, and worked perfectly throughout the entire stay.

Cons:
The bed is very small for two people, and the mattress is already quite worn out. If you sleep close to the edge, you start to feel like you are falling off when you are about 10 cm from it. The bed is therefore very cramped for two people, and there are no larger bed options in the hotel. There are no small reading lamps next to the bed, and the lighting beside the bed is very bright. As a result, if one person wants to read while the other wants to go to sleep early, it becomes a problem.

The shower, like those in many hotels nowadays, is open, so water splashes outside. When we arrived, the shower drain was also clogged, but it was fixed after we contacted reception. During the week, the drainage was acceptable but not perfect. The carpet in the hallway outside the room was a little dirty and was not vacuumed throughout the entire week we stayed at the hotel. The hand soap that ran out in the room was not replaced during the room-cleaning and refreshment service, nor even after we contacted housekeeping.

Very important when choosing a room:
It is recommended to avoid rooms on the street side, above the smoking area, and exposed to traffic noise.

reviews.text:
We stayed there for a week while attending a conference. The staff, from the doormen to the front desk to housekeeping, were professional, courteous, competent, and friendly. Service is on a par with a Peninsula or Mandarin, but without the four figure per night price. The two phone calls we made to the front desk (one to request laundry pickup, the other to request a bellman) were answered promptly. Both service requests were filled in under five minutes.

Our room featured a high ceiling and a large window. The high end decor was as expected for a hotel of this class. There was plenty of storage. The bathroom could have been brighter, and is getting a little dated, but is still quite nice. Overall, the room was lovely, and very comfortable.

The location is walking distance to both the finance hub and the British Museum, as well as Covent Garden. There is a tube stop at the end of the street. The entrance to the hotel is via a gated carriage way into a large enclosed courtyard.

Service and food in the hotel restaurant was wonderful, but we found that we preferred Gail's for breakfast (a slightly lighter menu). There are numerous restaurants at various price ranges within walking distance. There's a Waitrose a few doors down for snacks.

I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel.

reviews.text:
Out of sight - out of mind ... unfortunately I have to use this old idiom to describe my experience with the Melia White House in London.

I'm usually not the kind of person, who's flooding the web with negative feedback.

And there wasn't the slightest reason for a negative feedback during my stay in this hotel.

The location is almost perfect close to public transportation (less than 45 minutes to LHR) and also very close to the Regents Park.

The rooms are spacious, well equipped and modern.

The breakfast buffet is very good.

The relation price / value is ok (for London).

So why do I have to write a negative feedback?

I got an E-Mail in the morning of departure, that I can use Online Check-out in order to avoid the crowds at the front desk. I performed this Online Check-out and asked for an invoice by E-Mail. Since it was a business trip, I need an invoice for my travel expense claim. And this is, where the trouble started. I didn't get an invoice - I used the E-Mail from the website and kindly asked for an invoice (3 times up to now, without a single reaction) - I used the customer service desk of Melia (2 times up to now, without a single reaction). Meanwhile the deposit on my credit card was refunded, so that somebody must have accesed my account - but they don't send my an invoice.

I am really sorry to complain on this way - but I seriously have to warn other future customers, to check-out online, if there's a need for an invoice. Use the front desk and ask for a paper copy.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience, especially as this was a special occasion for my wife and me. I had high expectations because someone who had stayed here previously had spoken very highly of the hotel.

We arrived at 10:00 AM and, as expected, our room was not ready. We left our luggage and went on with our day.

At 7:30 PM we returned and asked for our room key and luggage. We were sent to the concierge and had to wait several minutes, explain the situation twice, and eventually were shown the wrong luggage. We then had to go and find our bags ourselves, which were stored in a high corner together with my jacket. We then carried everything to our room ourselves. What made this more frustrating was that there had been a bellboy with a luggage trolley when we arrived. I cannot say whether porter service is reserved for The Level guests, but the difference in treatment was noticeable. Porter assistance is hardly an extraordinary service; I have experienced it even in three-star hotels in Rome.

The room itself was very nice, although the hairdryer had a UK plug and there was no compatible socket in the bathroom, so we had to use it in the bedroom.

We also asked to borrow two travel adapters. None were available, which I understand. We asked whether two could be set aside for us later, but were told this was not possible. Instead, we could buy them from the hotel pantry for £20 each. Even if I were the Sheikh of Bahrain, I would think twice before paying £20 for a travel adapter. We bought them elsewhere.

We asked the concierge where we could find them. He simply told us there were stores on Oxford Street, with no directions or further assistance. My last visit to London had been 16 years ago, so I would have expected a little more from a concierge. He then repeated that we could buy them in the pantry. At that point it felt like a broken record: unavailable to borrow, impossible to reserve, but available for £20 each.

Dinner brought further surprises. I ordered two rum and cokes and was asked twice what I meant. Perhaps "Cuba Libre" would have been easier. They eventually arrived as two glasses of rum with two small bottles of Coca-Cola served separately, at £17.50 each.

When leaving the restaurant, the waiter selected the discretionary charge on the payment terminal and asked me to sign without really giving me the opportunity to decide whether I wanted to add it. The amount itself was not the issue, but the service difference between half-board and à la carte guests made this particularly difficult to understand.

Housekeeping was another problem. On the second day, the room was cleaned but the towels were not replaced. We waited more than 50 minutes for new ones and eventually had to wait until the following day to have a proper shower.

On the third day, the room was not cleaned despite the illuminated "Please Make Up Room" sign being activated. At around 5:30 PM, a staff member entered without knocking, even though I had already switched the sign off. Shortly afterwards, someone knocked repeatedly asking whether we wanted housekeeping service at 6:30 PM.

There was also no Chromecast in the room. After my negative post-stay survey, I was told by email that Reception could have explained the different room categories. After paying £599 for the stay, I found it rather difficult to understand why the solution was apparently to spend another £200-£300 simply to have Chromecast.

Breakfast was good, as was the food at dinner. The main issue was the service.

The two genuinely positive aspects were the room itself and Tania at Reception, who was extremely kind and tried to make things better by offering us complimentary drinks. I really appreciated her gesture.

Overall, I left genuinely disappointed. There were simply too many things that went wrong during what was supposed to be a special occasion.

I would not choose the Meliá White House again. Fortunately, there are other Meliá hotels in London, so I will try one of those next time, hopefully with a very different experience.

The Langham is situated in a beautiful historic building in central London. As an American Express cardholder, I received a complimentary room upgrade to the next category, and the room was absolutely beautiful. The beds were extremely comfortable, and the bed linen was of excellent quality.

However, there is one concern I would like to bring to the hotel’s attention. On our first night, we returned shortly after midnight and found nobody at the entrance: no doorman, bellman, or visible security staff. What concerned me even more was that the lifts could be accessed without a room key card, meaning that potentially anyone could enter the hotel and go directly up to the guest room floors.

Given the hotel’s central London location and its luxury status, I found this rather surprising and concerning from a security perspective.

Overall, we enjoyed our stay, particularly the beautiful room and exceptional bedding, but I do believe that guest security and access to the room floors deserve greater attention.

As someone who has stayed at The Langham in New York and Chicago, I have always associated The Langham brand with high standards of luxury and refined hospitality. However, my catastrophic experience at The Langham, Shenzhen has made me completely re-evaluate my loyalty to this global chain, including flagship properties like London.
During a recent stay at their Shenzhen hotel, staff actively monitored CCTV footage of hallway guests and repeatedly subjected my room to disruptive late-night phone calls demanding visitor registrations. Midnight surveillance and aggressive late-night harassment are completely unacceptable for a supposedly high-end international hotel group. When we raised privacy concerns, the handling of the matter and subsequent deposit disputes was thoroughly unprofessional.

A luxury hospitality brand must maintain consistent standards globally and, above all, respect guest privacy and peaceful rest. Sadly, the brand's lack of oversight and respect for guests' basic privacy has destroyed my trust in The Langham worldwide. Privacy-conscious and international travelers should beware.

Wir reklamierten sofort. Uns wurde gesagt, es sei kein anderes Zimmer verfügbar, und wir bekamen den Eindruck, dass wir dieses Zimmer aufgrund des späten Check-ins erhalten hätten. Dabei waren wir bereits mittags im Hotel. Man versprach uns einen Zimmerwechsel am nächsten Tag.

Am nächsten Morgen hieß es plötzlich, ein Wechsel sei doch nicht möglich, da alles ausgebucht sei – obwohl wir zahlreiche Gäste auschecken sahen. Eine Alternative, Entschädigung oder Preisreduktion wurde uns nicht angeboten.

Besonders ärgerlich: Wir bezahlen offenbar denselben Preis wie Gäste in normalen Zimmern mit Fenstern. Wenn solche fensterlosen Kellerzimmer angeboten werden, muss das unserer Meinung nach bei der Buchung klar ersichtlich sein.

Für uns absolut enttäuschend. Wir würden dieses Hotel nicht wieder buchen.

reviews.text:
Bad Experience
My wife and I don’t get away very often, so we were really looking forward to our stay, especially as it was for our 14th wedding anniversary. Sadly, what should have been a special break turned into a very disappointing experience.

We arrived at the hotel at around 4:15pm and had to queue for approximately 45 minutes. We completely understand that the hotel was busy, and we appreciate that these things can happen. However, after travelling and then waiting in a long queue, we expected a warm and welcoming reception. Unfortunately, this wasn’t the case. The receptionist was cold and unwelcoming, simply asking for our reference number before handing us our key. For a hotel reception, we found this very poor.

When we got to our room, we felt it was quite small, particularly as we were staying for five nights. We returned to reception and politely asked whether there was a slightly larger room available. We were told that we could move to a “super double” room, obviously at an additional cost, which I agreed to.

Unfortunately, when we entered the new room, it was exactly the same size as the room we had just left. We went back to reception and expressed our disappointment. We were then told that the “super double” room wasn’t actually any bigger it simply came with a few extras, including two larger pillows, a coffee machine and two KitKats. I have to say, after paying extra for what we had been led to believe was a better room, I was extremely disappointed.
We eventually settled in and went down for our evening meal. This was another unpleasant experience. The barman was extremely rude and unapproachable in the way he spoke to me. When I tried to order our meals, he attempted to charge us for everything. I explained that we were hotel guests and had already paid for our meals as part of our stay.

He then rudely explained that he doesn’t ask customers for their room numbers or whether they are hotel guests — he simply assumes that everyone coming into the restaurant is there to eat. I found his attitude completely unacceptable.
We eventually ordered our food, and the bill came to around £50. I asked whether there was an option to upgrade the meal deal, similar to what Premier Inn offers. I was told there was no upgrade and was bluntly told, “We’re not Premier Inn.”
The following day, however, we noticed that there was in fact an upgrade option on the menu. When I raised this with the member of staff at the bar, he admitted that he hadn’t realised there was an upgrade and said that he would refund me. Unfortunately, that refund never happened.

The whole experience was incredibly disappointing. We reached the point where we simply wanted to come home. The only reason we stayed was because we had already booked a show and were determined to make the best of the situation.
What makes this even more upsetting is that this was our 14th wedding anniversary. My wife has also been diagnosed with cancer, and I had really wanted to make this trip special for her. Instead, the experience with the hotel and some of its staff completely overshadowed what should have been a lovely and memorable occasion.

When we returned home, I contacted the hotel to make a complaint. They offered us £50 as a goodwill gesture. However, this was roughly the amount we had been charged for our first evening meal, which we believe we should not have been charged in the first place. So, unfortunately, it didn’t really feel like compensation or a goodwill gesture at all.

The hotel is in a good location, but for us, that was one of the only positives. The attitude of some of the staff, the room experience and the issues surrounding the restaurant left us extremely disappointed.

We certainly would not recommend this hotel, and sadly, what should have been a special anniversary break is an experience we will remember for all the wrong reasons.

This is extremely disappointing to hear. A guest’s bag goes missing while waiting for a delayed check-in, and five days later, the management still hasn’t responded? This is completely unacceptable.

As a hotel, you have a responsibility to ensure guests are treated with care and that incidents like this are taken seriously. At the very least, the guest deserves a proper explanation and an update on the investigation.

Hotel management, please take responsibility and address this matter instead of leaving your guest without answers. This lack of accountability is appalling and reflects very poorly on your hospitality standards.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
My son stayed at this hotel, and as someone who is a hotelier myself, I can confidently say this is one of the worst experiences of hotel management I have ever come across.

His check-in was delayed, and he was asked to wait. While waiting, he went to have breakfast and left his bag on a chair. When he returned with his food, his bag was missing!

What is even more shocking is that it has been 5 days, and there has been absolutely no response from the hotel management.

As someone who understands the hospitality industry, I find this level of negligence, lack of accountability, and complete disregard for a guest’s belongings absolutely unacceptable. Delays can happen in any hotel, but how management handles a serious incident like this speaks volumes about the establishment.

This is hospitality at its worst. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. Please be cautious before booking your stay here.

Very disappointing experience at The Churchill Hotel. We booked two rooms and arrived at 10 AM. We understood that the official check-in time was 3 PM, and the staff told us they would do their best to provide the rooms earlier.

We received the first room at 12 PM, but it was extremely small compared to the 27 m² advertised in our booking, so we requested a room change.

The second room was even more frustrating. Reception told us it was not ready, although housekeeping confirmed that they had already finished cleaning it. We waited from 12:30 PM until around 2 PM simply because the person responsible for inspecting the room was unavailable.

We called reception several times, and every time they promised to send the keys immediately, but nobody came. Eventually, my brother had to go downstairs himself to collect them.

The problem was not the official check-in time, which we completely understand. The problem was the poor communication, lack of organisation, repeated empty promises, and disappointing customer service.

Instead of enjoying our arrival and relaxing after a long journey, we spent hours feeling stressed and frustrated.

For a hotel of this standard, we expected much better hospitality and professionalism. Unfortunately, our first impression was extremely disappointing, and I would not recommend this hotel based on our experience.

We had a really nice stay at The May Fair Hotel in London. We stayed in a Collection Premium Room, and overall the experience was excellent.

The staff were definitely one of the highlights. From the front desk and concierge to housekeeping and everyone else we interacted with, the service was friendly, professional, and welcoming throughout our stay.

The location is also fantastic. You’re right in the heart of Mayfair, with Green Park just around the corner and many of London’s main attractions, restaurants, shopping areas, and cafés within walking distance. It’s also very convenient for getting around the city.

The only thing I found a little disappointing was the breakfast. For a five-star hotel, I expected more variety and a wider selection. The breakfast was good, but I think there is definitely room for improvement in this area.

We paid around £414 per night after my Radisson VIP/member discount. It’s not cheap, but considering the location, service, and overall experience, we were happy with our stay.

Overall, we really enjoyed our time at The May Fair and would definitely consider staying here again when we’re back in London.

I stayed at Sea Containers London with a friend and had a very pleasant experience.

The hotel is in a great location right by the River Thames. There is also a rooftop bar on the 12th floor with lovely views, although it is not open every day.

Blackfriars Station is the nearest station, about a 5–10 minute walk from the hotel. The Thameslink platforms are even closer, around 3–5 minutes away, with convenient direct trains to both Luton and Gatwick airports.

What impressed me most was the service. The staff were warm, friendly, and very efficient whenever we needed assistance. There are also several supermarkets nearby, which makes it easy to pick up drinks, snacks, or other essentials.

Overall, a comfortable hotel with a convenient location and excellent service. I would happily stay here again.

Unfortunately, my latest experience at Leonardo Royal Hotels was disappointing.

Let’s start with the irony. The hotel proudly displays a card in the room stating:

“If your stay is not a 9 or 10, please let the team know during your stay, so we can make it right! Press ‘0’ for Reception.”

What a wonderful sentiment — if only someone actually answered the phone!

Trying to reach reception was an exercise in frustration. Calls went unanswered, and getting hold of anyone to address an issue seemed virtually impossible, I had to physically go to the front desk to settle matters . How exactly is a guest supposed to give the hotel an opportunity to “make things right” when the most basic communication channel doesn’t work?

Then there is the cleanliness — or rather, the lack of it.

The room was simply not cleaned to an acceptable standard. I found hairs in various places, including the bathroom and on furniture. Even more disappointingly, some of those same hairs remained throughout my stay.

The overall coordination between hotel staff and departments was equally disappointing. There appeared to be little communication, accountability or genuine attention to the guest experience.

As a business traveller, I do not expect extravagant treatment.l, but I need a clean room, responsive reception, and reasonable coordination . These are not luxury requests. They are the absolute minimum.

What makes this experience particularly frustrating is that this is not my first disappointing stay. I have watched the standards deteriorate over successive visits, and instead of seeing improvements, each experience seems to bring a new level of disappointment.

I will sadly be forced to explore alternative accommodation for my next business visit. It is a shame, because I would much rather return to a hotel I know than have to start looking elsewhere.

My wife and I booked the Leonardo Royal London St. Paul's for a post-cruise visit to London for four nights to include the breakfast package.

From the moment we arrived we were treated with professionalism, courtesy, and extreme friendliness by the front desk staff. Due to being a Leonardo member, we were upgraded to the Executive Club and granted access to the amenities of that perk.

The hotel is upscale to include a bar/restaurant and a rooftop bar as well. The main atrium, serviced by glass lifts provides a spectacular view of the well-appointed public spaces. Really a unique hotel.

The location was selected sight unseen after conducting research into the area, and our desire to be centrally located in the heart of London near the major attractions. We were NOT disappointed! We were within walking distance to many of the sights we wanted to see, and conveniently near the Big Bus stop at St. Paul's.

Our room left little to be desired as it was spacious, clean, and very well stocked with coffees, teas, and snacks.

The concierge was extremely helpful in assisting us in navigating the city and in arranging transportation to LHR at the completion of our stay after four nights.

Leo's (on-site restaurant) and the breakfast buffet were remarkable in their choices and quality of food offerings.

All in all, the Leonardo Royal London St. Paul's exceed our expectations for coming into the booking blind. This will certainly be a recommendation for friends, and will be our go-to upon our return to London.

Exceptional Hospitality! A Wonderful First Impression of the Royal Garden Hotel

I recently visited the Royal Garden Hotel in Kensington to arrange accommodation ahead of a particularly important family visit, and felt compelled to recognise the exceptional service I received from Nicole.

From the moment we met, Nicole was an absolute pleasure to deal with. She was warm, gracious, knowledgeable and extraordinarily attentive, taking considerable time to show me around the property, explain the various accommodation options and understand what mattered most to us.

What particularly impressed me was her genuine thoughtfulness. At no point did I feel that I was simply making a hotel reservation. Nicole approached the entire experience with a level of personal care, patience and professionalism that is increasingly rare, even among London’s finest hotels.

Having stayed at and visited many excellent hotels over the years, I have come to appreciate that truly outstanding hospitality is rarely defined by the property alone, but by the people who represent it. Nicole is a wonderful example of this. She combines professionalism with a natural warmth and sincerity that cannot easily be taught.

Nicole has already given me tremendous confidence that my guest will be exceptionally well looked after. That peace of mind, particularly given the significance of this visit, is something I value enormously.

The Royal Garden Hotel is fortunate to have someone of Nicole’s calibre representing it. I very much hope her management recognises the outstanding impression she makes on guests, even before their stay has begun.

Thank you, Nicole. Your kindness and efforts have been genuinely appreciated, and I look forward to experiencing the hotel’s hospitality firsthand.

reviews.text:
When I first started planning my trip to the UK, I spent a lot of time deliberating over where to stay. I was torn between booking a hotel near the famous tourist attractions around Trafalgar Square and choosing the Hilton Paddington, which offered excellent transport links. After much thought, I decided on the Hilton Paddington, and it turned out to be the best decision I could have made. I booked an Executive Room with breakfast included for a five-day stay, and I was thoroughly satisfied with the experience.
1) The biggest advantage is undoubtedly the convenience of transportation. You can reach Paddington Station from Heathrow Airport in just 15 minutes via the Heathrow Express, and the hotel is directly connected to the station, making access incredibly easy—a huge plus for families traveling with a lot of luggage. Additionally, there is a subway station right in front of the main entrance, which was particularly convenient for using the Circle Line, and the bus stop for the famous No. 23 bus—which runs through several major districts—was also right there.
2) I had heard the hotel was older and worried the facilities might be outdated, but those concerns proved unfounded. The renovated room was spotless and spacious enough for a family of four. It was well-equipped with all the essentials, including a refrigerator; the housekeeping was excellent, and the bedding was incredibly comfortable.
3) The breakfast was delicious. It never felt overcrowded during breakfast hours, allowing us to enjoy a tasty meal in a relaxed and comfortable atmosphere.

If you are planning a trip to the UK and are undecided about where to stay, you certainly won't regret choosing the Hilton Paddington.

reviews.text:
Perhaps Wilde isn’t for long stays and we misjudged. That said, we checked in for 18 nights and were very disappointed by the following:

* Garbage pick up was every four days or by request through QR code. This was inconvenient as you have a kitchenette which by its very nature means food waste. Waste bins (bathroom and kitchen are small with no liners)
* Housekeeping was supposed to be every four days; they came only twice during our stay. This meant that towels were damp by days three and four. Again, you could QR it for replacements but that did not always work.
* The double bed was, in reality, two singles zipped together. You could feel the seam whilst in bed. The bed itself was pushed against the wall so whoever slept on that side had to either crawl over partner or crawl to the bottom of bed and the reverse process.
* Few drawers so best to live out of your suitcase.
* No interior secondary lock on room door.
* Safe didn’t work.

The location (Paddington Basin) was great and intentions of young staff are good. Short stays only.

Subject: Appalling Service and Mismanagement of Confirmed Booking

I am extremely disappointed by the handling of my arrival and the conduct of both the front desk staff and supervisor.

To avoid any inconvenience upon my early morning arrival after a long-haul flight, I had deliberately booked and paid for an additional night so that my room would be available immediately upon check-in. In addition, I had informed the Guest Relations team via email of my arrival plans and had also completed online check-in the night before.

Upon arrival, however, I was informed by Mamun at the front desk that while my room was supposedly "ready", I would instead be given a temporary and smaller room for a few hours while the air conditioning in my assigned room was being repaired. This explanation was both contradictory and unacceptable. If the room required repairs, then it was clearly not ready. More importantly, I had paid for the room from the previous night specifically to ensure it would be available upon my arrival. What is particularly difficult to understand is why the air conditioning issue was not identified and rectified during the period for which I had already booked and paid. The situation gives the impression that my original room had been allocated elsewhere despite the hotel's clear awareness of my arrival arrangements.

The response from the supervisor, Amit, was equally disappointing. Rather than offering a sincere apology or demonstrating any sense of accountability, he repeated the same explanation and attempted to argue that the room was technically ready despite the ongoing repair works. When I questioned why the issue had not been resolved the previous day, given that the room had been reserved and paid for, no satisfactory answer was provided.

What concerns me most is not merely the room issue itself, but the complete lack of ownership, empathy, and professionalism displayed in handling the situation. At no point did I receive a genuine apology, an acknowledgement of the inconvenience caused, or any indication that the hotel understood the impact this had on a guest arriving after a lengthy international journey. This experience falls far short of the standards I would expect from a hotel of this calibre and represents a serious failure in both operational management and customer service. The handling of my booking and arrival was, quite frankly, appalling.

Since then, their Front Office Manager, Alexandre has contacted me and promised to look into the matter, which i appreciated. He handled the situation with professionalism and he had been helpful for the remaining of my stay there. Good job to him.
