A Wonderful Stay—Made Exceptional by the Staff

After arriving nearly an hour early following an overnight flight, Nabiha at the front desk asked housekeeping to prioritize our room and kindly offered us a complimentary breakfast. Our room was ready before we had even finished our meal! It may sound like a small gesture, but it immediately set a “can-do” tone for our entire stay.

That first impression proved to be anything but a fluke. Throughout our week at the Marriott Marble Arch, everyone we encountered—from the front desk and restaurant to concierge, valet, and management—consistently demonstrated the same warmth, professionalism, and genuine desire to make our stay special.

If I had to identify one person who exemplified that experience, it would be Mrunal. Like her colleagues, she regularly went beyond her role to make us feel welcome and relaxed. What stood out most was her genuine interest in our visit to London. She remembered the little things we had shared and would later ask specific questions about our adventures and experiences. That personal touch meant a great deal to us.

My hat is off to the management of the Marriott Marble Arch for hiring, training, and retaining such a consistently considerate, professional, and genuinely pleasant team. The people are what made our stay memorable.

reviews.text:
I booked one of our Executives into this hotel for Tuesday 13th October through Booking.com. The reservation was made in his name, and he had the booking confirmation with him. The experience he had was extremely disappointing and, frankly, completely unacceptable.

First of all, £380 for a room without a window is absolutely obscene. At that price, I would expect a far higher standard of accommodation and service.

On arrival at around midnight, he was asked to provide ID, which he did not have with him. Despite having a confirmed booking in his own name, he was left having to download a bank statement to prove his identity. This caused unnecessary stress and a frustrating delay before he could finally get to his room. I book hundreds of hotel stays every year for our team, and in all that time, I have never encountered a situation like this. It is frankly astonishing that a guest with a valid booking confirmation should be put through this ordeal so late at night.

To make matters worse, he was then kept awake until 4am by someone in the neighbouring room talking loudly on the phone. While I appreciate that the hotel cannot necessarily control the behaviour of other guests, the lack of soundproofing is certainly worth bearing in mind if you value a decent night's sleep.

Overall, this was a thoroughly disappointing experience from start to finish. For £380, the standard of accommodation and the unnecessary hassle on arrival fell well below what anyone should reasonably expect. The combination of the extortionate price, the distressing check-in experience and the inability to get a proper night's sleep is simply unacceptable.

I regularly arrange accommodation for our team, and this experience has left a very poor impression. We will be avoiding RUI Hotels going forward, and I certainly would not recommend them to others based on this experience.

• Ubicación estratégica: Está literalmente al lado de la estación Victoria. Solo hay que cruzar la calle para tener acceso a una red de transporte público excelente. El barrio es muy tranquilo y cuenta con todo lo necesario a mano: restaurantes, supermercados y farmacias.
• Habitación y limpieza: La habitación era cómoda, confortable y con un mobiliario funcional que nos permitió mantener todo el equipaje perfectamente organizado. La limpieza, impecable en todo momento.
• Desayuno buffet: Estuvimos en régimen de alojamiento y desayuno, y fue todo un acierto. El buffet destaca tanto por su gran variedad como por su calidad.
• Atención al cliente: Nuestro agradecimiento más sincero a todo el personal. Son educados, amables y están siempre dispuestos a ayudar con una sonrisa. Un diez absoluto.
¡Ojalá podamos volver pronto a Londres! Sin duda alguna, repetiremos en este hotel.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Nos hospedamos en este hotel 4 noches. En general el hotel está bien, la ubicación es excelente (cerca a la estación de bus, metro y tren Victoria) y con varios cafés y restaurantes cerca.
El desayuno es lo mejor que ofrece este hotel, es buffet y tiene gran variedad, es delicioso y tiene máquinas de café y para calentar el pan. Sin embargo, para desayunar debes cruzar la calle a su otro edificio. Existe un puente en el segundo piso pero nunca lo encontramos, tuvimos siempre que cruzar la calle (y pasan buses y taxis). No es malo pero fue un poco incómodo.

Las habitaciones están bien, las camas eran cómodas y había suficiente espacio. El baño también es cómodo, sin embargo, para ser un hotel 4 estrellas siento que faltaron amenities como cepillo de dientes, pasta dental pequeña, etc. en otros hoteles 4 estrellas sí los ponen. Aquí solo te dan los básicos (crema de cuerpo, shampoo y jabón).

Algo que no nos gustó fue el trato del personal. No nos trataron mal pero tampoco nos trataron como se esperaría de un hotel 4 estrellas por el que pagamos tanto. Por ejemplo, a la hora de hacer check out, le comenté a la chica de recepción que necesitábamos un taxi. En otros hoteles, se ofrecen a llamar uno y te ayudan con las maletas (considerar que el Riu sí tenía personas carga maletas o botones). La chica me dijo, literalmente, que en la calle pasaban muchos taxis y que solo pare uno. Los botones nos vieron sufriendo para llevar las maletas a la calle y no hicieron nada.
Debo mencionar que el personal de limpieza y del desayuno sí es extremadamente amable y atento. Cuando te cruzas con ellos en el pasillo o les pides algo.

Por otro lado, tener en cuenta que el restaurante solo funciona para el desayuno. Tienen un lobby bar pero el menú no es muy variado, tienen más bebidas que comida. Realmente no puedes optar por cenar en el hotel.

En conclusión, buen desayuno pero mejorar en la proactividad del personal.

reviews.text: Suelo viajar a Londres por ocio muy a menudo y siempre al mismo hotel,el fin de semana del 12 de septiembre acudí de nuevo pero esta vez probando Riu Plaza London Victoria. Nos sorprendió muy gratamente. Ya se han destacado en otras reseñas su buena ubicación y por ello lo elegimos. Nuestra experiencia muy satisfactoria. Al llegar, nos atendió Macarena, muy amable y entendiendo que quedaban varias horas para poder acceder a nuestra habitación, nos preparó la habitación para que pudiéramos acceder antes y tuvo el gran detalle de mejorarnos la categoría de la habitación(entendemos que esto solo se puede hacer si hay disponibilidad y con una política de hotel flexible y emprendedora) .Al llegar a la habitación Macarena nos llamó para preguntarnos cómo estaba todo y si era de nuestro agrado, un excelente gesto. Las habitaciones son amplias y hay que destacar la buena limpieza. Nos encantó la accesibilidad del hotel y de las habitaciones, no todos los hoteles dan prioridad a las personas con dificultades en movilidad. Por último destacar el desayuno, nos encantó el amplio horario y por encima de ello la gran variedad; en fruta, en embutido...qué gran detalle ese queso con nueces y miel...o ese rincón para las personas celíacas...y por supuesto, destacar y agradecer pan de masa madre para el desayuno...una maravilla y la variedad de leches vegetales...todos estos detalles lo hacen singular y único desde mi punto de vista .El personal reponía constantemente y cabe señalar que quedando 10 minutos para el cierre seguían reponiendo y avisando del cierre a los clientes por si querían reponer antes del cierre, muy amables. Por describir alguna critica constructiva y entendiendo que somos muchos los clientes y no es fácil mantener todo pulcro, fui a calentar en el microondas la leche de almendras y necesitaba un poquito más de supervisión en limpieza y al llegar a descansar después de la comida al hotel el ruido de la aspiradora no permitía una calidad de sueño positiva. Son detalles mínimos y mejorables que no han enturbiado nuestra estancia porque en la balanza es un hotel excelente y que ya estamos pensando en reservar para nuestras navidades en Diciembre. Enhorabuena Riu Plaza London Victoria.

reviews.text:
I’m sorely disappointed! Based on the overall reviews, I was excited about staying at the Riu, particularly this location. I agree with other reviews that the hotel is situated in a nice location - right around the corner from
the Victoria Theater and the Victoria station. It’s also within a decent walking distance to Buckingham Palace. So from a location standpoint, it’s great! But that’s about where it ends for me.

As I was checking in, I heard one of the staff say that breakfast is actually across the street, not in the hotel. So forget any plans of running down and grabbing something to bring back to your room. And even if breakfast were in the building, if you’re not by the elevator, you’ve got a long trek ahead of you. Usually hotels have a hallway, possibly two when the room numbers are high. Not this hotel; it is literally a maze to get to your room. Imaging pulling all your luggage around all these twists and turns! I recently had a fall, so my ankle and knee have pain during long walks. I’ll take ownership that I should’ve asked where the room was relative to the elevator; but usually hotel staff give you some sort of heads up about these things, especially when the pathway is not as clear. Nope, none of that was given. On top of that, no one told me you have to put the key on the cardholder at the door to turn on the room’s electricity. So imagine my frustration as I’m clicking buttons and the AC, all for naught.

I’m currently in my room, and after a long overnight flight, I really need a place to shower and sleep. However, I’m honestly considering not unpacking and just finding another hotel or seeing about the Westminster location. Just sucks because I prepaid for my stay already. Truly sad because I really had high hopes for the hotel. It’s a key reason I chose London for part of my trip.

And leaving a negative review simply gets you a generic response with no true intentions of fixing the issue or compensating one for their troubles. An offer to be hosted again after an original horrible experience is not acceptable.

reviews.text:
Good mid week break around a presentation day at Westminster. A good 45-50mins walk from Waterloo station but pleasant in the autumn sunshine. Big and quick lifts in the hotel. Once the concierge and front desk understood my assistance dog was fully registered, they couldn’t have been nicer and more helpful including hailing a cab etc. They brought up extra tea and coffee plus milk on request. Friendly and really good service.
The restaurant is only open for breakfast and the need to knock on the fire doors to be let in, you have to go outside to access these doors, plus not much English spoken by the servers is a challenge for wheelchair using guest. None of them understood about assistance dogs access rights, but accepted when we explained albeit with muttering!Breakfast was not the best but not the worst either and clearly aimed for people who like a lot of salt! Hence only 4 stars.
The room was a very good space although the turning circle would have been tight for a larger powerchair. Was fine for us. Shower was a bit weak but did the job!
Clean, bright and very comfortable. Large room compared to most London hotels and remarkably quiet inside.

reviews.text: Gruesome experience with this hotel. On 01 Sep morning, our bag has got stolen from inside the Hotel's breakfast room (when we were taking taking breakfast) which was the hotel's own space and entry of each guest was checked and monitored by the hotel attendants (they were asking for room numbers of each entrant). The bag was never left unattended. The theft and thief were clearly visible on the CCTV footage. However, the hotel manager, to our dismay, strongly discouraged us from reporting to the police. The stolen bag contained our debit cards, credit cards, passports, identity cards and driver's license. The hotel did not help us in any way and their rude and straightforward denial to support us in reimbursing the cost of renewal of passports or even help us with transport was completely unexpected. One of the hotel attendants later told us that the thief seemed to be a hispanic person who very skillfully stole our  bag which was kept just beneath the table on the floor. Very non-cooperative hotel management who were totally unmoved by the incident. Initially they were even hesitating to have a look at the CCTV and delayed almost an hour in having a look at the footage. Later on the same day we reported to Metropolitan Police who is now investigating the case and the hotel management had to submit the footage to the police. Everyone should know this incident before booking at this hotel.

reviews.text:
I stayed at the InterContinental London Park Lane for three nights. While there were some positives, particularly the friendly and courteous staff, the overall experience fell short of what I would expect from a hotel of this standing.

The staff were generally polite and friendly, with the breakfast team being particularly attentive. The doorman was also consistently welcoming, helpful and courteous. However, the overall level of service was inconsistent. This was particularly noticeable at Theo Randall, where I had dinner one evening. Some members of staff appeared overly casual in their approach, which did not reflect the level of service I would expect from a fine-dining restaurant of this calibre.

For example, while replacing our cutlery, one member of staff was looking elsewhere and talking rather than focusing on placing the cutlery properly. While this may seem like a small detail, attention to detail is important in fine dining, and these small things leave a lasting impression. I would be more accepting of this level of service during breakfast, but not in a fine-dining restaurant. Having stayed and dined at St. Regis and other well-established luxury hotels and restaurants, I have experienced a considerably higher standard of service.

There were also a number of issues with the hotel itself. Two of the four lifts were out of service during our stay. This resulted in waits of around 5-10 minutes at times, particularly during busy periods, as the remaining lifts were relatively slow and often crowded. This was frustrating and certainly not what I would expect from a hotel of this category.

The condition and smell of the corridors were another disappointment. There was a noticeable odour throughout the hallways as we walked between our room and the lifts. The carpets also looked dated and quite worn. I believe a hard flooring solution, such as wood or tiles, would be a significant improvement, both aesthetically and practically. Air freshening in the corridors would also help address the persistent odour.

The carpet in our room had also seen better days and, in my opinion, would benefit from replacement. Hard flooring is increasingly common in hotels in many parts of the world and is much easier to keep clean and fresh. Carpets can accumulate dust and odours over time, and this was noticeable during our stay.

Finally, the concierge service could have been more knowledgeable when I asked about car rental companies. I was directed to Victoria Station, where I was told Sixt offered good value and was the best option. However, when I arrived, the Sixt representative informed me that they had another branch just minutes away from the hotel on Park Lane itself, and that several other rental companies were also located nearby. Better local knowledge from the concierge would have saved me an unnecessary journey.

Overall, there were some good aspects to the stay, particularly the friendliness of certain members of staff, but the inconsistencies in service, the condition and odour of the carpets and corridors, the lift situation and the lack of local knowledge from the concierge meant that the experience did not live up to the standards I would associate with a luxury InterContinental property. I have experienced significantly better service and facilities at other established five-star hotels, including St. Regis.

reviews.text:
I have always loved Mandarin Oriental and was genuinely looking forward to our stay. We usually choose The Peninsula or Rosewood in London, but decided to try MO because I have a soft spot for the brand. At a comparable price, our expectations were naturally high.

Before arrival, the hotel asked about our preference for a bathtub or shower and our estimated arrival time, only to reply that nothing could be guaranteed. We understand that requests depend on availability, but it made the advance communication feel rather pointless.

We booked through American Express, yet at check-in we received no information about breakfast times, the hotel’s facilities, the benefits included in our booking, or where the hotel credit could be used. There was no printed information or welcome card in the room either—small touches that are common at comparable five-star hotels and help guests feel properly welcomed.

After a long flight, our room was not available until exactly 3 p.m. While waiting, I asked for a power bank, but the hotel had none. This was surprising for a five-star hotel in 2026, and I had to sit in a corner charging my phone before I could go out for a walk.

The restaurant staff were lovely, as were the gentlemen at the entrance. Unfortunately, our experience with the reception and concierge teams felt more politely transactional than genuinely warm or accommodating.

There were also several housekeeping details that may seem minor individually but collectively affected the experience. There were no cotton buds, makeup-removal pads or body lotion, and the shower-gel bottle was empty. When it was eventually refilled, after pointing it out, cleaning supplies were accidentally left on the bathtub. We chose not to report this at the time because we did not want to get anyone into trouble. these are details that should be noticed before a guest arrives, particularly at a hotel of this level.

The extra blanket we had requested was also not in the room. The shower was extremely small, the wardrobe offered very limited space, and there was no complimentary water, and was brought after we asked for it. The rooms and corridors also felt somewhat worn and would benefit from refurbishment.

Another important point is the noise. Rooms facing the main road are extremely loud, with ambulances and other emergency vehicles frequently passing with their sirens on, including during the night. The sound insulation was poor, so the sleeping comfort was not what we expected. Guests sensitive to noise should request a room away from the road.
Buffet Breakfast was okay, but non even nearly as good as other Mandarin hotels,  especially in Asia. No asian food choices at all at the buffet, which also is rather strange as other Asian hotel chains offer it.
I am sharing this feedback constructively because I genuinely like the Mandarin Oriental brand and wanted to enjoy the stay. Nothing was disastrous in isolation, but the accumulation of these details made the experience feel below the standard expected from a five-star hotel in this price range. I hope these points can be addressed, as the property has the potential to offer a much more polished and welcoming experience.

From the moment I arrived and was greeted by Aleks and the welcoming team at the door, The Londoner completely impressed me. Being in the center of the theatre district made it easily walkable to fantastic fine dining restaurants and Chinatown, which was incredibly convenient.
What truly elevates this property to a world-class standard, however, is the remarkable hospitality, attentiveness, and professionalism of the staff. I actually noticed the owner dining at the hotel and went over to approach him. Even though I completely interrupted his meal, he was incredibly warm, kind, and took the time to talk to me and thank me for coming. That level of genuine care clearly trickles down and reflects beautifully in his entire team.
A few specific team members deserve the highest commendation for going above and beyond to ensure a perfect stay:
• Teadora (Reception Manager): Incredibly helpful and pleasant. When I inquired about a specific juice for a personal health protocol, she personally coordinated with the kitchen to ensure it was arranged for my entire stay.
• The Reception Team (Calantha & Rayana): Exceptional warmth and efficiency at the front desk.
• The Residence & Dining Staff: Scott provided stellar, attentive care up in The Residence. The amazing maître d' team at the stand, including Afori from Albania, as well as Olha, Anna (the manager of Whitcombs), and the exceptional Chef, all demonstrated an outstanding passion for service. There were also many other team members whose names I unfortunately didn't catch or are simply too numerous to mention, but who contributed just as much to making my stay seamless.
The dedication of this entire team reflects the absolute best of London hospitality. I look forward to returning in the near future and will certainly be recommending this beautiful hotel to family, friends, and colleagues.

We had a lovely stay at The Londoner, but what really stood out to us was the exceptional service from Dennis at the hotel entrance.

After checking out, our pre-booked airport transfer unfortunately didn’t show up. We waited for around 20 minutes, and even though we had already paid for the ride and were still hoping the driver would eventually arrive, Dennis took the initiative to arrange a backup taxi for us.

When our original driver still couldn’t give us a clear arrival time, Dennis was genuinely worried that we might miss our flight. Without hesitation, he helped us with our luggage and brought everything across the road to the backup taxi he had arranged, which was already waiting for us.

Here’s the good part first: Location is decent, but there are other good locations around London too depending on what you want to do. Dining staff is nice and patient. Bellboys and concierge are great and very helpful.

Here’s the bad part: Guest relations/front desk were completely unresponsive via email, so I called to inquire about upgrades. The staff told me it’d take X amount to upgrade to a suite. So I asked them to send me a list of all possible paid upgrades, which they didn’t. Once I reached, that X amount had become 2X. When I told the front desk that I didn’t get any expected communication and told them the quoted rate on phone, they said they can’t believe me without a phone recording. Since Hilton and most hotels records all phone calls you make to them, I asked them to listen to that which they refused. Then they told me they’ll investigate and get back the next day, they didn’t. They simply just didn’t say anything the entire trip. Another funny thing they said that more than 75% of their guests are diamond members so it doesn’t mean much to them.

Our “upgraded” room was claustrophobic. Literally nothing to see from the window.

You can find better options in that price range for sure.

The Theatreland Afternoon Tea at The Waldorf Hilton was such a lovely experience. I’ve had afternoon tea here before, but the Theatreland version felt especially fun and memorable. The setting is beautiful, and the West End theme makes it feel like a real occasion, especially if you’re heading to a show afterwards.

The food was 10/10. The sandwiches were fresh and delicious, the little cakes and desserts were beautifully made, and the theatrical details gave us plenty to admire before we tucked in. The scones with clotted cream and preserves were a highlight too. Everything tasted as good as it looked, which isn’t always the case with an afternoon tea this elaborately presented.

I also had a cocktail, which was wonderfully refreshing. At £59 per person, this felt like a special treat, and I’d happily come back for it. A gorgeous way to spend an afternoon in London.

I had the Bridgerton themed afternoon tea with friends on Saturday.
I am coeliac and often the gluten free version of things can be different to the "normal" versions but I'm happy to say it was amazing!  Everything was replicated as a gluten free version, so mine looked exactly like my friends and I didn't feel I was missing out in any way.  When you're gluten free, that's really important!

The food was absolutely fabulous - it looked lovely, with beautiful Bridgerton theming and tasted just as good as it looked.
The teas were served in a lovely dining room and there was a pianist playing throughout.
Serving staff were very attentive and happy to bring refills of sandwiches and tea.
Overall, a brilliant experience - we all really enjoyed it and I'd absolutely recommend it as an excellent gluten free afternoon tea.

We opted for the wine pairing so had the pleasure of meeting our sommelier (I’m frustrated I’ve forgotten her name but I will edit this if it comes to me!) who was so friendly, very knowledgable and worked with our likes, dislikes and added an additional little tasting just off the back of a conversation. reviews.text: I stayed at The Connaught for four nights at the end of August, and having had a few weeks to reflect on my stay, I find myself with mixed feelings about the experience. The hotel is beautiful, the Mayfair location is hard to beat, and without exception the staff were warm, gracious and incredibly helpful. The concierge team was particularly wonderful, securing every reservation I requested and making the final days of a long journey remarkably easy. Unfortunately, my first impression of the room was very different. I had booked the entry level category directly with the hotel at a rate of over $1,000 per night and had mentioned beforehand that, should availability permit, I would appreciate an upgrade. At check in I was told I had been upgraded from a queen to a king room. I was grateful for the gesture, although the room was extraordinarily small, with no practical place for my large suitcase other than the floor, almost no natural light, and a single window looking directly onto a vent. I had also noticed online that several other room categories remained available that evening, so the upgrade felt rather modest. The size, however, was ultimately not my biggest issue. The shower did not drain properly and, most importantly, the bed was genuinely uncomfortable. I slept terribly that first night, which after nearly a month of traveling was particularly disappointing. When I mentioned the mattress to management, it was suggested that I might be feeling the seam created by two twin mattresses being placed together. Having stayed in many hotels throughout Europe, I am very familiar with this arrangement, and that was not what I was experiencing. There was a pronounced dip on each side of the bed and the mattresses simply felt very worn. To the hotel’s credit, my concerns were handled graciously and I was moved to a beautiful and far more comfortable contemporary room, although its very modern design did not quite have the classic Connaught character I had been looking forward to. What stayed with me most was a manager, who was extremely kind, telling me that I should never book the entry level room category. I appreciated her candor, but found the comment rather telling. At a hotel of The Connaught’s caliber, there really should not be a room category that guests are advised not to book. An entry level room can be smaller and less elaborate than a suite, but it should still provide the comfort, attention to detail and sense of occasion that define a great hotel. There were also a few smaller service misses, including a request for additional hangers on my first evening that went unanswered until the following morning. None of these things individually would normally merit much attention, but expectations are understandably high at The Connaught. I genuinely enjoyed many aspects of my stay and have nothing but kind things to say about the people who looked after me. Still, after having some time to reflect, I was disappointed overall. You only get one chance to make a first impression, and at this level I believe the magic of a hotel should be felt whether you are staying in its grandest suite or its smallest room. With so many exceptional hotels to choose from in London today, I am glad I experienced The Connaught, but I am not sure I would rush back unless I were staying in one of its higher room categories.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text: I have stayed at The Royal Horseguards Hotel in London many times over the years, and it used to be one of my favorite hotels in the city. Unfortunately, after my most recent experience, I will never stay there again. The decline in customer service since the hotel changed hands is astonishing. I booked a Deluxe King Room, just as I have on numerous previous visits. Instead, I was placed in a miniature room that was practically half the size of the Deluxe King Rooms I had stayed in before. When I complained, the explanation was that "it's an old building and not all rooms are the same size." That's a convenient excuse, but it's also incredibly deceptive. If you're selling a particular category of room at a premium price, guests should reasonably expect to receive what they paid for, not a room half the size simply because the hotel chooses to give it the same label. Even the fire evacuation map clearly showed how much smaller my room was compared to the surrounding rooms. What made the experience particularly infuriating was the way the staff handled it. I complained multiple times to the front desk, only to be passed from one employee to another. Each assured me that they would get me moved to another room when their manager arrived, and each one conveniently seemed to forget those promises when the time came. When I finally spoke with the manager, she was surly, dismissive, and completely uninterested in resolving the problem. I explained that I was a repeat guest, knew exactly what I had booked, and knew what those rooms were supposed to be like. Her response was essentially that this was the room I was getting and it's an old building. When I explained that I expected compensation for being given a room substantially smaller than what I paid for, her response was even more astonishing: if that's how the hotel labels the room, then that's what counts. Apparently, at The Royal Horseguards, the room's actual size and what the guest reasonably expects are irrelevant. As long as they slap the right label on the door, they consider their obligation fulfilled (be careful they don't label it the penthouse from now on). That's an appalling attitude toward customers, particularly loyal guests who have stayed there repeatedly. It's genuinely disappointing to see a hotel I once loved fall this far.  They have no problem taking your money, but good luck getting what you actually paid for.

reviews.text:
This place has always had a special place in my heart; the night I got engaged to my husband, we stayed here. Years later when we lived in the UK, he planned a date night full of surprises and we stayed here. So when we returned for vacation, staying here was a no brainer.

During check in, the person working the front desk was indifferent, cold and inattentive. It was awkward standing there for several minutes,
So long that we began to wonder if something was wrong. We requested a paid upgrade, he ignored it. In the end, he simply slid the keys across the desk and gave us the floor. Didn’t specify room number, upgrade, lift locations, ask if we needed help with our bags…. Things any other 5-star hotel knows to do. Our room was an absolute joke, like a closet with dirty carpets and missing amenities. The next day, we requested house and were out for several hours. We came back in the late afternoon and it still hadn’t been serviced. The staff during our stay weren’t super professional and seemed more like frat bros joking and cursing. I can’t lie, it was a pretty interesting juxtaposition with people walking through the lobby in ball gowns and tuxedos.

I sent a message on WhatsApp and was told we’d hear from a manager, but of course radio silence. We left and came back after having to call and get it serviced, and they’d left a sad fruit bowl as an apology.

People go to 5-star hotels because they’re after a certain experience, otherwise, they’d stay at the Marriott. Unfortunately, the Horseguards has lost its luster of luxury, doling out motel amenities and charging Four Seasons prices.

I’m really grateful for the experience because it’s positioned me to convince my husband to try ACTUAL hotels in London that are deserving of their 5-star rating, so there’s the silver lining!

Location can’t be beat, so I’ll give them that, but next time I’m in London, we’re staying at the Rosewood!

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed here for our honeymoon in September, and we could not have asked for a better experience.

We arrived around 9:00 a.m. after nearly 26 hours of travel. We were exhausted and worried because check-in wasn't until 3:00 p.m. From the moment we arrived, though, the staff made us feel incredibly welcome. Mr.Pervez immediately greeted us, came to the car, and retrieved our bags, and the hotel offered to hold them while we waited.

At reception, we met Teodora, the Reception Manager. She was exceptionally kind, gentle, and welcoming. She seemed genuinely excited that we were staying there and immediately congratulated us on our marriage. She explained that check-in wasn't until 3:00 p.m., but she would do everything she could to find us a room early. She secured us a room on an upper floor and arranged for it to be cleaned as quickly as possible. While we waited, she very kindly offered us complimentary breakfast. After such a long journey, this meant a lot to us. Our room was ready around 11:00 a.m., much earlier than we expected.

The room was very nice and comfortable. Our only real complaint was that the carpet was noticeably worn and dirty in places from what appears to be constant use. We also had an issue with the shower leaking, but maintenance came and fixed it immediately.

One day, the complimentary bottled water in our refrigerator wasn't restocked. That evening, we asked at the lobby for water and were directed to the restaurant, where we were told we'd have to pay for bottled water. We were a little frustrated since we were only asking for the complimentary water that normally came with the room, and the price was quite high. It was a minor issue, though, and our only other complaint.

There was also a very loud event at a neighboring business on Friday night. This was completely outside the hotel's control, and the staff did a good job communicating with us. They explained that there was a curfew for the event and reassured us that the noise would soon stop.

What really made this hotel special was the staff. They truly went above and beyond. The day after we checked in, we returned around lunchtime and found a handwritten note from Teodora, along with a bottle of wine and chocolate-covered strawberries to celebrate our honeymoon. Another day, we found a complimentary bowl of fruit in our room. These thoughtful touches made our stay feel genuinely special.

The staff seem to truly enjoy their jobs and take pride in what they do. Every interaction was kind, professional, and welcoming. Teodora in particular made a lasting impression on us, and we sincerely appreciate everything she did to make our honeymoon special.

The location is also fantastic. The Tube station is about a two-minute walk away, the Thames is right outside, and Big Ben is just a short walk away. We could not have picked a better location for our first trip to London.

We also had cream tea at the Green Parlour one afternoon, and it was incredible. We honestly didn't have high expectations simply because it was at the hotel, but we were pleasantly surprised. It was very reasonably priced and delicious, especially the scones. We loved the tea so much that we're actually trying to find the same tea to purchase. It was a wonderful, relaxing afternoon activity and a perfect classic London experience.

Our room did feel a little cramped with our luggage, so next time we'd probably pay for a larger room, but we knew we had booked a smaller room going in.

Overall, we absolutely loved our stay and were genuinely sad to leave. We cannot wait to return to London, and this will absolutely be the hotel we choose again. We especially hope to see some familiar faces, including Teodora, when we return. Thank you to the entire team for making our honeymoon so memorable!

This is a review for the Spa and Afternoon tea combo.

This was a truly terrible experience for 3 of us when considering we paid over 1,000 GBP for the spa and afternoon tea package - you expect an amazing experience (massage quality and food), if not at the very least spectacular service for that price.

The spa was the better experience, however my sister had a masseuse (Stacie I believe) who was very rude to her. She has sensitive skin and when during the facial she complained that she didn’t like the face scrub experience, she insisted on proceeding saying “It’s make your skin smooth”. When my sister then insisted a second time she said “I don’t understand what you don’t like, you need to be more specific”. I’m not sure what type of training she is receiving but it’s entirely inappropriate to continue doing something your customer is clearly saying she doesn’t enjoy EVEN if you believe it’s good for her and then to tell her she’s not making sense.

The afternoon tea was even worse. The time was pre booked for 2:30pm and we arrived at our seats around 2:28pm. The tea only arrived closer to 3pm and we waited a total of 40 mins before I couldn’t take it anymore and got up to talk to the staff and they rushed over with the food. The server said there was a mix up and from what I could gather the food was ready but they just forgot to bring it to us for 40 whole minutes. It was not busy or crowded so there was really no excuse. To top it all off the sandwiches tasted like they came from Sainsbury (dry and bland) and the scones were not the right texture (they were more like cake). We are not new to afternoon tea experiences in the UK and this was easily the worst one as well as the most expensive.

I cannot in good conscience recommend the experience to anybody. Really quite amazing to be able to fail at every aspect of the service. Only reason it’s not 1 star is because Inga who did my service at the spa was actually quite decent.

Réservation effectuée via Booking.com, confirmée par l’hôtel et intégralement payée. Nous avons reçu une confirmation officielle ainsi qu’un message direct de l’établissement.
Un mois plus tard, nous sommes informés d’une “erreur tarifaire” et invités à payer plus de £7,700 pour maintenir la réservation. Après avoir refusé, la réservation a été annulée unilatéralement.
Entre-temps, nous avions organisé notre voyage (transports et congés) sur la base de cette confirmation ferme.
Aucune proposition alternative concrète ni solution satisfaisante n’a été apportée.
Très grande déception quant à la gestion de cette situation par un établissement de ce standing.

UPDATE :
Suite à nos échanges, la direction de l’établissement a repris personnellement notre dossier et une solution satisfaisante a finalement été trouvée.
Nous tenons à remercier l’équipe pour son écoute et son implication dans la résolution de cette situation. Nous apprécions le professionnalisme démontré et sommes désormais impatients de découvrir The Berkeley.

UPDATE 2 :
Un excellent séjour au Berkeley ! Le personnel est aux petits soins, toujours accueillant et attentionné, et le service de chambre est irréprochable.

Les petits déjeuners sont délicieux, avec une mention spéciale pour les pâtisseries de Cédric Grolet. Nous avons également beaucoup apprécié les deux magnifiques piscines, sur le toit et en intérieur.

Enfin, l'emplacement est idéal, juste au sud de Hyde Park, pour découvrir Londres.

Un grand merci à toute l'équipe pour ce superbe séjour. Nous reviendrons avec grand plaisir !

One of the most unsettling experiences we’ve ever had at a hotel happened during our last stay at The Berkeley. (June 2023)

The floor we were staying on was undergoing renovation, and on two separate occasions someone entered our children’s room — once at around 9 PM and again at approximately 2 AM in the middle of the night. Our room was on Do Not Disturb.

When we raised this with reception and asked to see the CCTV footage to understand exactly what had happened, we were not allowed to view it. We were told that it had been “room service” entering by mistake — both times. Given the DND sign and the fact that this happened twice, including at 2 AM, we found that explanation extremely concerning.

As parents, having someone enter your children’s room in the middle of the night is frightening, and the way the situation was handled left us with more questions than reassurance.

It is such a shame because we genuinely love The Berkeley and have always loved the rooms and the hotel itself. But after an experience like this, we simply cannot overlook the security concerns or the lack of transparency surrounding what happened.

I stayed here overnight last minute earlier this year, when another hotel in the same chain let me down, and I desperately needed a room close to midnight.
The positives - a nice room and friendly service in the morning at reception, plus the helpful Thomas hailed me a cab.
However, my check in experience was uncomfortablly frosty, even though I paid the £400+ room rate upfront. I checked at midnight due to the other hotel in the group double booking my room despite advance notice. I requested to also stay here an additional night and was told by the unfriendly reception manager with a superior attitude, that the hotel was fully booked for the following night and they couldn't accommodate me. However, my partner who is a platinum IHG member, later checked online and could see that there were several rooms available. So that made me feel sad and let down by both hotels in the group. My assumption is that because I initially booked the less expensive hotel, the manager here took the opportunity to look down on me and incorrectly assume I could not afford their rates. (I had a similar experience once before in the USA, the minute the staff confused us as not being 5* paying guests, the charm was switched off...)
Overall, my experience is that other 5* hotel groups in London are equally if not even more fabulous in their decor, yet deliver far more consistent and genuinely friendly service. The Rosewood for example, they are a really lovely brand and their staff couldn't be nicer.

reviews.text:
Disappointing service for a five-star hotel

I found my stay at Kimpton Fitzroy deeply disappointing. At check-in, the information from the front desk was brief. Even though I booked a basic room, it cost more than £300 a night. There was no still water in the room, the mirror on the wardrobe had old marks that suggested poor maintenance, and the position and height of the bedside table made it awkward to use an international plug adapter.

I came and went several times during my stay, and most staff did not acknowledge me. At check-out, I stood waiting while three staff members were at the front desk. One was helping another guest; the other two kept their heads down and did not acknowledge that anyone else was waiting.

This was a world away from my experiences at Rosewood London and Kimpton Glasgow, where staff acknowledged guests promptly even when they were busy. The building and public spaces here are beautiful, but the service fell short of what I would expect even from a three-star hotel. Even though hotels are busy with the start of the university semester approaching, I do not believe that excuses such disappointing service at a five-star hotel. As a young Asian woman travelling alone, I was left wondering whether I was the kind of guest this hotel wanted to welcome.

For travellers with a similar budget, I would recommend the newly opened Imperial nearby. It is not a five-star hotel, but in my experience its basic rooms offered more space, better cleanliness and amenities, and far better service.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
Loyalty appears to mean very little at The London EDITION.

I’m a Marriott Bonvoy Platinum member, five nights away from Titanium. After excellent stays at the Madrid and Shanghai EDITIONs, I considered EDITION my favorite Marriott brand. This experience has seriously changed that.

We’re staying for three nights, and both of us are Marriott Bonvoy members. We needed separate beds, but no twin rooms were available. A two-bedroom suite and a one bedroom suite was showing as available for our dates, so I spoke with the front desk supervisor about a possible upgrade. The alternative offered was a rollaway bed.

I understood that this was a significant request, not a guaranteed benefit. What frustrated me was the supervisor explaining that even Ambassador members would not be upgraded into these particular suite categories. The explanation was a blanket refusal rather than a lack of availability for our stay.

For a three-night stay at a luxury hotel, I would hope that finding a way for two loyal guests to sleep in proper beds would warrant some flexibility. Having a Platinum member approaching Titanium sleep on a rollaway while a suite remains available hardly feels like meaningful loyalty recognition.

Marriott promotes suite upgrades as a reason to earn elite status. If these categories are excluded regardless of loyalty level, guests deserve a clear explanation of what the benefit actually delivers.

A luxury hotel can decline a request and still make guests feel valued. This interaction left me questioning why I’ve invested so many nights in Marriott.

Five nights from Titanium, and this hotel has given me a compelling reason to stop chasing it.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
The London EDITION est un hôtel fantastique, alliant design minimaliste et architecture historique (bâtiment classé de 1835) dans le quartier calme de Fitzrovia.
Le personnel est aux petits soins, discret et ultra-professionnel, un vrai sens du service 5 étoiles.
Les chambres sont spacieuses (même les catégories d’entrée font 20 m² minimum), avec tous les petits détails qui font la différence : literie haut de gamme, produits Le Labo, technologie moderne, salles de bains élégantes. On s’y sent immédiatement bien.
Côté restauration, Berners Tavern (chef Jason Atherton) est une référence gastronomique, et The Punch Room figure parmi les bars à cocktails les plus atmosphériques de Londres. Parfait pour un dîner ou un verre dans un cadre sophistiqué.
Emplacement idéal : à 8 min à pied de Tottenham Court Road et Oxford Circus, proche de Soho, Covent Garden et du West End, tout en restant dans une rue calme. Une vraie expérience dans le luxe, au cœur battant de Londres.

reviews.text:
Stayed here for two nights for a wedding

I'll start by saying that this hotel has massive potential, however I was left disappointed.

Firstly the rooms are finished to a poor standard, with things like lamps glued to the worktops not square, the light switches are wonky and the kettle doesn't even have a plug near it.

The bathroom could have done with a good scrub to be completely honest, with staining onost of the tiles around the shower.

For anyone wanting a nice relaxing evening on the balcony overlooking the harbour. It might be worth noting that this hotel is directly under the flight path for Heathrow.

The mattress was very firm (which I know is to some people's liking), leaving my shoulders hurting each morning.

Now my biggest gripe.

The staff.

I will quickly mention that the bellhop (who's parents live locally) was excellent, funny, helpful and generally awsome.

However the entire rest of the staff seemed to be completely useless.

From pouring a cup of tea so full you couldn't put milk in it let alone lift it to drink it.

Asking for a peppermint tea bag which we never received.

I phoned the front desk whilst we were at the wedding to ask if a child's bed could be moved from one room to another, no answer.

I called again an hour later to be told this was impossible and they would have to make up a pull out bed in another room (we had three rooms between the party).

Turns out that this had been prearranged anyways and that I was just calling to make sure that this happened.

Luckily someone else tried calling and got someone useful.

We also had an incident where we were trying to explain that a food delivery was being delivered to the hotel that needed to go on a bus that would arrive for it. (Now I know this is a weird request).

However we had to speak to 3/4 different people before anyone understood what we were even talking about. This was EXTREMELY painful to deal with.

Luckily our favourite bellhop turned up to save the day, and immediately understood.

It might also be worth mentioning when we arrived it took 2 hours for our bags to arrive in our room.

To summarise, if you want a top tier hotel (as they seem to be charging by), stay somewhere else.

The service is lackluster and the quality of the hotel itself seems to be slipping.

I will make a final point that the view is fantastic.

I would like to say a heartfelt thank you to the whole team at Chelsea Harbour Hotel, and especially to Hafsa, for the kindness and care shown to my relatives during what was an incredibly stressful and difficult time.  It was in a busy time as the design centre had events on.

A close relative had to come to London for treatment at The Royal Marsden after being diagnosed with cancer. They were feeling very poorly and understandably extremely stressed about being in London, so I arranged for them to stay at Chelsea Harbour Hotel. My husband and I had stayed previously and always experienced such wonderful customer service, and the hotel's location, comfort and peaceful surroundings made it an ideal choice.

I arranged an early check-in for them, and when I returned to the hotel after a meeting, I spoke with Hafsa about the situation, the diagnosis and the level of stress and support my relatives needed. Hafsa was absolutely wonderful. She was so caring, empathetic and understanding, and went above and beyond to make sure they felt looked after.

Every time we have stayed at the hotel, we have had the pleasure of dealing with Hafsa, and she has always made our experience so much better. On this occasion, her kindness and support made a real difference. Between the calm, comfortable hotel, its wonderful location and the support Hafsa was able to organise, my relative's stress visibly came down and she told me she finally felt more at ease.

Hafsa arranged a late check-out, helped organise a taxi service and pointed us towards people who could provide ongoing support while my relatives were staying in London for treatment. These things may seem small, but at a time when someone is overwhelmed and worried, they mean so much.

The hotel itself is lovely, yes it does need a little updating in some rooms but the marina rooms have plenty of room with Dyson hairdryer, fridge, safe, tea and coffee facilities etc.  The breakfast has a good selection, and if there is something else you would like, the team are happy to help. Lunch and dinner are also lovely, with a beautiful view over the harbour.  My relatives were able to enjoy a calm stroll around the hotel, the harbour and along the river, which gave them a little peace and fresh air during an incredibly difficult time.  There is parking available at hotel and their is the design centre and parking just next door.
Thank you to Hafsa and the entire Chelsea Harbour Hotel team for your compassion, kindness and outstanding customer service. You made a very difficult experience that little bit easier, and we are genuinely grateful. Your care and understanding will not be forgotten and my relatives personally asked me write a review for Hafsa for reducing their stress and doing everything she could to make them comfortable.

The Bloomsbury Hotel delivered one of the finest hotel experiences I have ever had. Ideally located in London's vibrant Soho district, it offers convenient access to Covent Garden, Leicester Square, theaters, museums, and many of the city's most iconic attractions.

The hotel strikes the perfect balance between luxury and charm. Its stylish, distinctly British décor creates a warm and sophisticated atmosphere, while the rooms are exceptionally comfortable. The beds are among the most comfortable I have slept in, and every meal was beautifully prepared and delicious.

Most impressive of all was the staff. Their professionalism, warmth, and genuine desire to ensure guests have an exceptional experience are unmatched. The level of service exceeded every expectation and made my stay truly memorable. I highly recommend The Bloomsbury Hotel to anyone visiting London.

宿泊予定の1ヶ月前に予約しました
北東の日が当たらないシングルベット2つの部屋
料金は2泊3日の朝食付き22.3万円
家族４人で宿泊したので、2部屋借りて、44.6万円
3階と5階でフロアが別。隣は難しくても、せめて同じフロアにしてほしかったが、気が利かない。
部屋を歩くと床全体がベコベコ音が鳴り、沈む。古びた印象。
部屋のエアコンの暖房はスイッチ入れて15分後に5秒ファンが回り、すぐ止まるので暖房は機能しなかった。ロンドンの冬は寒いので凍えますね。
その為、1泊目はダイソンの偽物のようなポータブル暖房機を貸し出され、「明日は別の部屋が空くので、そちらに移動もできます」とマネージャーみたいな女性から言われた。
しかし、その後、マネージャーとすれ違って目が合っても、「昨晩は寒く無かったですか？」とか「お休みになれましたか？」「部屋を交換しましょうか？」などの声掛けは一切無い。
ポータブル暖房機で寒さはしのげた。
カードキーは、2回ぐらい使うと、ドアが開かなくなるので、フロントに再発行してもらう。3回再発行してもらった。
2日目のベッドメイキングの時に、浴室のバスタオルがなぜかドアにかけてあり、新しいバスタオルが１つ不足していた。清潔感が無い。
フロント横の壁面が花のレストランは、席は空いているが、カフェ利用ができず、予約必須で食事前提で、断られた。
立地は静かで2分歩けば人通りの多い商業施設が多い通りに出れるので良いと思う。
朝食は種類が豊富でスタッフは親切丁寧。
２日目は、団体客が入っていたので、朝食は騒がしくゆっくりは食事できない状況。
ベットメイクのチップは10ポンド置いたけどテーブルに返却された。
ロンドンでは、古びた部屋で中程度のサービスで1人1泊5万円。どんな評価で5つ星なのか疑問です。
2年前にロンドンのヒルトンに宿泊したけど、とても清潔、親切で設備も問題無かった。やはり一流ホテルの方が良い。
そして、日本のホテルの素晴らしさを再認識した。

reviews.text:
Update von Oktober 2026:
Wir waren erneut im "The Westminster" weil das Personal im März so hilfsbereit war. Das Herz und die Seele in diesem Hotel ist für uns weiterhin Herr Vijay Pamuani. Er ist so unbeschreiblich herzlich und hilfsbereit!! Jedoch war das restliche Personal (hier gab es wohl auch einen Wechsel) dieses Mal eher kühl und zurückhaltend. Sehr negativ war: wir hatten einen frühen Termin und mussten das Hotel um 6:45 h verlassen. Auf Nachfrage ob es ein Frühstück to go gibt wurde uns mitgeteilt, dass das nicht geht und wir uns in diesem Fall selber versorgen müssen. Frühstück war aber bereits bezahlt. Das fanden wir sehr schade. Frühstück ab 7:00 h ist für uns zu spät, wenn wir schon um 8:00 Uhr einen Termin haben.
Wir würden trotzdem wieder kommen!

Personal + Service suuuper!! Alle waren extrem nett und hilfsbereit. Wir bekamen Tips für tolle Insider Restaurants. Die sehr nette Begrüßung von Vijay Pamuani gab uns gleich das Gefühl herzlichen willkommen zu sein. Das Frühstück fanden wir lecker mit viel Auswahl. Zu den Zimmern: die Vorhänge am "Eckfenster" konnten nicht ganz weggeschoben werden um den View voll zu sehen. Wir sahen nur auf andere Häuser. Wäre nicht so schlimm, wenn man nicht extra ein Zimmer mit Eckfenstern wg. der Aussicht gebucht hätte. Die Größe war für uns völlig in Ordnung. Die Kopfkissen sind leider unbequem und an manchen Stellen im Zimmer (Boden + Duschtüre) war es nicht so wirklich sauber.
Die Lage ist gut. Fazit: sehr gut mit kleinen Abstrichen. Wir würden wieder dort buchen. Hauptsächlich wg. dem netten Personal und dem guten Frühstück  :-)

reviews.text:
Wir haben uns bewusst für dieses Hotel entschieden, da insbesondere die online beworbene, vielversprechende Bar ein ausschlaggebender Grund für unsere Buchung war. Umso enttäuschender war es, vor Ort festzustellen, dass diese Bar überhaupt nicht mehr existiert, obwohl weiterhin damit geworben wird. Das ist für uns absolut unverständlich und inakzeptabel!

Auch die Kommunikation mit dem Hotel war äußerst enttäuschend. Bereits vor unserer Anreise hatte ich versucht, das Hotel zu kontaktieren. Trotz intensiver Suche konnte ich lediglich drei verschiedene E-Mail-Adressen im Internet finden. Ich habe alle drei angeschrieben, jedoch auf keine einzige Nachricht eine Antwort erhalten. Dass ein Hotel für seine Gäste im Vorfeld praktisch nicht erreichbar ist und Anfragen einfach unbeantwortet bleiben, ist für mich absolut inakzeptabel und zeugt von mangelnder Kundenorientierung.

Zum Zimmer: Die Ausstattung war schön und ansprechend. Allerdings quietschten alle drei Betten bei jeder noch so kleinen Bewegung, was den Schlafkomfort erheblich beeinträchtigte.

Auch der Zimmerservice ließ zu wünschen übrig: Während unseres dreitägigen Aufenthalts wurden weder Toilettenpapier noch Taschentücher nachgefüllt. Besonders ärgerlich war, dass wir die leere Taschentuchbox sogar extra aus der dafür vorgesehenen Plastikhalterung genommen und gut sichtbar auf das Waschbecken gelegt hatten. Dennoch wurde sie nicht ersetzt.

Positiv hervorzuheben sind hingegen der Check-in und Check-out, die beide äußerst schnell, unkompliziert und effizient abliefen.

reviews.text: I found sleep impossible because my room was fitted with 3 bright flashing lights. A smoke alarm that flashes the whole room in bright green light every few seconds, a 2nd smoke alarm that flashes the room red and a faulty sensor light that randomly flashes white light. It felt like strobe lighting at a disco. Staff told me this is a common problem in all the rooms and rather than fixing it they gave me a black disc that cello tapes on to the broken sensor light. The problem is the cello tape loses its stickiness during the night and falls off. So if you want to sleep at night, I don’t recommend this hotel.

We stayed at the Radisson Hotel London Euston Square for 3 nights and had a really enjoyable experience.

The room was very comfortable, clean, and well maintained, making our stay relaxing and pleasant. The breakfast was also amazing, with a good variety of options and great quality.

The hotel is in a very convenient location, within walking distance of shopping areas, restaurants, and some popular London attractions. It was very easy to get around and explore the city from the hotel.

Overall, we were very happy with our stay and would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting London. We would happily stay here again! 😊

Very Disappointing Experience – Not Recommended

My stay at this hotel was extremely disappointing. The bed was uncomfortable, and the room was not clean to an acceptable standard. When I requested extra pillows and blankets, I was told they were unavailable, showing a lack of consideration for guest comfort.

The room was also missing basic amenities, including a dental kit. Disposable slippers were not provided either; I had to request them and wait a long time to receive them.

The staff were uncooperative and unfriendly when I asked about early check-in and late check-out. What made the situation even more frustrating was that I agreed to pay the additional charge for a late check-out, but the hotel later changed its mind about allowing me the extra time. This was unprofessional and extremely disappointing, especially after I had already agreed to the fee.

The most concerning incident was when housekeeping opened my room door while I was sleeping, despite having placed the “Do Not Disturb / Privacy” sign on the door. This was a serious breach of privacy and made me feel uncomfortable during my stay.

Overall, the hotel fell far below my expectations in terms of cleanliness, comfort, basic amenities, customer service, and respect for guest privacy. The lack of hospitality, inconsistency in service, and unwillingness to accommodate reasonable requests made this a very unpleasant experience.

I would not recommend this hotel, and I would not stay here again.

reviews.text:
I would say the hotel has a good location in London and the price is reasonable. However, considering the age of the building and the overall service, I feel the hotel could be better. The location is definitely the main advantage, and some of the staff were very friendly and helpful, but unfortunately, not all of them.

Things to take note of before booking Millennium Knightsbridge London:

1. we were three people in the room and had paid extra for this, but the housekeeping team was quite limited with the amount of bottled water provided. We had to ask for more several times

2. Breakfast is required as part of the booking, and it is actually cheaper to book the room with breakfast included. However, the breakfast options are quite limited, especially for Muslim guests. The menu was almost exactly the same every day with very little variety. Considering that a large number of the hotel’s guests are Arab, I expected more suitable and varied options

I also asked for some ice, which I understood to be a basic complimentary service, but I was asked to pay for it

3. There is no bidet/shattaf next to the toilet, which can be inconvenient for Muslim guests

4. We were three people staying in the room for around 8–9 nights, so we asked if there was any possibility of getting a slightly larger room. Unfortunately, instead of trying to help or offering another option, we were immediately told that we would need to pay extra for an upgrade

Overall, the location is the biggest advantage of this hotel. It is convenient and in a good area, but there are several areas where the hotel could improve, especially in terms of service, breakfast variety, and being more accommodating to guests

reviews.text:
Very disappointing and misleading experience. I truly wonder the review of others when they're say 4 or 5. I should have read more reviews with low stars. That is more reality of what I experienced.
The hotel’s website created expectations that did not match reality. It advertises room service and prominently shows a breakfast tray on a beautifully presented bed overlooking London, but there was no room service for breakfast. Breakfast was only a buffet, which was not clearly explained on the website.
The room itself was uncomfortable and poorly designed. There were no convenient electrical outlets near the bed or tables, making it extremely difficult to charge devices. The bed was also very uncomfortable, and the mattress felt extremely hard and unsupportive.
I specifically requested a room away from the elevator, yet my room was only three doors away. Noise from the hallway and neighboring rooms was clearly audible. There was also very limited space for luggage, forcing me to place my suitcase on a table that I needed for other things.
Communication from the staff was poor and disorganized. During my stay, I also witnessed several other guests at reception complaining about their rooms and showing staff photos of the conditions.
Overall, I feel I paid primarily for the location, not the quality of the hotel. My biggest concern is the difference between what is presented on the website and what guests actually experience. I strongly recommend carefully checking the details before booking rather than relying solely on the hotel’s website and photographs.

reviews.text: UNSAFE! My bag was given to a member of staff upon our arrival where it was placed in an unsecured area of the lobby. While we were checking in, my bag was stolen by a person who entered the lobby, grabbed my bag and ran out the door with it.  Management was immediately made aware of what had happened and their response was that we should call the police. Since the bag was in the hotel’s custody when it was taken, it was the hotel’s responsibility to report the theft. They refused. Both the duty manager, Barry, and the front desk manager, Zeeshan Kalim, made absolutely no effort to compensate us for the loss of all the items in the bag, not to mention the bag itself. We didn’t even get so much as an apology! So please be aware that Millennium’s The Bailey’s Hotel puts your safety at risk and then denies any responsibility for what happens as a result. We will never stay at a Millennium Hotel again!

reviews.text: I stayed at the Baileys for 2 nights. My husband and I arrived first then our 30 family members arrived on their private bus. Looking at how our luggage was handled from taxi/bus and smooth transition to holding before check-in then move to the assigned rooms, it was all seamless! My family had 80 pieces of luggage! The staff were all courteous polite and knowledgeable despite the huge influx of stress. Absolutely wonderful staff and facility. The hotel is old and they’ve made steps to improve which are all practical. There’s also fridge in the room for our medication. The air conditioning is crispy cold! Plus ironer and ironing board. Absolutely wonderful stay! Also the breakfast was very good. The buffet had a lot of variety. The price for breakfast is very reasonable and cheaper than places nearby. The tube is right beside so the location was awesome!! There are also many convenient stores, fast food restaurants, and pubs/restaurants nearby. reviews.text: The room was very spacious, extremely clean and the beds big and comfortable. Bathroom was immaculate, and the shower was glorious. Rooms definitely the selling point of this hotel. Service is ok but pretty indifferent. Gym is a complete disappointment. You have to walk 5 mins via a pretty derelict high street, and the gym itself is well equipped but a bit dirty and depressing. Location of the hotel is not great. It’s Kilburn, not Maida Vale and is situated at the bottom end of the high road. If you know London, it is what it is, but  not sure it’s what a tourist near central London would be looking for. We returned from a function on a Saturday night at 23.15 and headed to the bar for a night cap only to find it closed. When I expressed surprise the staff member looked at me like I was a deranged alcoholic and directed me to the pub up the road. Easy check in, good location, had a king bedroom on the 7th floor with a great view of the park. Didn’t notice any noise from the street or other rooms, comfortable bed, the bedding was a bit itchy and non-breathable, but at least the air conditioning worked well.
When we checked in, we were told about the dinner special and breakfast in the restaurant, and were asked if we wanted to add it on. I said I wanted to look at the breakfast menu before deciding, and were directed to the bar to glance at the breakfast menu. We decided to pay ahead of time for breakfast as we had an early flight and there weren’t any restaurants serving a full breakfast nearby that early in the day.
The following morning, we show up to breakfast and are led to the buffet. We thought we would be ordering off the menu we were told to look at, and told the employee that we were misled. We had to go to the front desk, ask for a refund for the buffet (they made us feel like it was a huge inconvenience), go back into the restaurant, and order for the menu. It caused confusion for everyone, but there was no way I was paying 40 pounds for 2 basic buffet breakfasts.
We ordered a Florentine benedict and a regular eggs benedict then took over 30 minutes to make, and the eggs were not poached. We noticed that no one else in the breakfast area had ordered food from the kitchen and the buffet area was fully stocked, so it didn’t make sense to have to wait over 30 minutes for a small benedict with no sides. It was overpriced and such a poor value.
Wish we would have just stopped somewhere on the way to the airport for a legit breakfast, as that was a joke.
To top that morning off, the water stopped working in the building when we were trying to get ready for the day and packing up. That was fun. Will be staying elsewhere next time we’re in London.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
**H10 Waterloo London – Toller Aufenthalt mit (ganz) kleinen Abzügen**

Wir hatten bereits in Venedig sehr gute Erfahrungen mit einem H10 Hotel gemacht, und auch das H10 Waterloo in London hat uns überzeugt. Schon beim Check-in wurden wir herzlich von **Valentina** empfangen. Obwohl unser Flug früh angekommen war, bekamen wir bereits ein tolles Zimmer. Ihre Freundlichkeit und Hilfsbereitschaft sorgten direkt für einen perfekten Start in unseren Aufenthalt.

Das Hotel überzeugt insgesamt mit einer sehr hohen Qualität. Besonders hervorzuheben ist die **Klimaanlage**, die außergewöhnlich leise und gleichzeitig sehr effizient arbeitet. Das sorgt gerade in einer Großstadt wie London für einen angenehmen Komfort.

Das absolute Highlight des Hotels ist jedoch die **Sky Bar**. Wir haben jeden Abend auf der Dachterrasse verbracht und die fantastische Atmosphäre sowie den Ausblick genossen. Allein dafür würden wir jederzeit wiederkommen.

Der einzige Kritikpunkt betrifft die Zahlungsrichtlinie des Managements. Sämtliche Bestellungen müssen sofort per Kreditkarte bezahlt werden. So sammelten sich an einem Abend gleich acht einzelne Belege an, obwohl alles problemlos auf das Zimmer hätte gebucht werden können. Das wirkt etwas umständlich und beeinträchtigt den ansonsten sehr guten Eindruck.

Beim Check-out wurde unser Aufenthalt durch die freundliche und professionelle Betreuung von **Pacxy** nochmals positiv abgerundet.

Insgesamt ein hervorragendes Hotel mit perfekter Lage, hoher Qualität und außergewöhnlich freundlichen Mitarbeitenden. Trotz des kleinen Kritikpunkts bei der Zahlungsabwicklung können wir das H10 Waterloo London uneingeschränkt empfehlen und würden jederzeit wieder dort übernachten.
★★★★★ (4,8/5)

Unfortunately, our experience with the staff was extremely disappointing from the moment we arrived until the moment we left.

Throughout our stay, we received very little warmth or courtesy. There was no greeting, no smile, and very little effort to make us feel welcome. At check-in, we encountered a particularly unpleasant member of staff, and at check-out, we were simply directed to a box where we were expected to leave our room key card, with no personal interaction or basic courtesy.

The only members of staff who were consistently pleasant and welcoming were some of the older members of the team. Sadly, our interactions with several of the other staff members were very different.

One incident in particular involved a male member of staff with a bandage on his nose, who was extremely rude to my husband. My husband does not speak English fluently, and there was a simple misunderstanding regarding our luggage, which had been left with the hotel. The situation only required a new luggage tag, yet the way my husband was spoken to was completely unnecessary and disrespectful.

We were spending almost £200 per day at this establishment, and we expected a basic level of courtesy, professionalism and hospitality in return. We understand that misunderstandings can happen, but there is no excuse for making guests feel unwelcome or being disrespectful towards them.

A hotel should make its guests feel valued and respected. Unfortunately, that was not our experience. I sincerely hope management takes this feedback seriously and reminds the staff that good customer service and basic courtesy are essential in the hospitality industry.

reviews.text:
Overall: Rated as a 4-star property, but the day-to-day guest experience was closer to a 2-star operation. Location is genuinely strong — steps from Southwark station — but that's the only consistent strength.

Pattern of "No" as a default response:

•	Luggage storage reversal: We emailed the hotel ahead of our trip specifically to confirm they could store our luggage, and received written confirmation that they could. This was reconfirmed verbally by front desk at check-in. On the day itself, however, a manager reversed this — stating the hotel doesn't offer this service and that "their GM would get angry" if they did. Her tone and delivery suggested a lack of basic training in handling a guest-facing conflict, let alone one the hotel had already committed to in writing. We had to insist at length before the hotel agreed to honor its own prior confirmation — an unnecessary situation given we'd already finalized our Edinburgh travel plans around having this storage in place, with no ability to simply carry everything with us.

•	Laundry: Called front desk to ask if our laundry had been delivered — told flatly "no, nothing was delivered." We had to go back to the laundromat, get a photo confirming front desk had received it, and only after showing that photo did staff re-check their own storage and find it.
•	Water bottle: Front desk called our room to say they had a water bottle we'd left at the restaurant. When we went to collect it minutes later, we were told "no, we don't have a bottle here" — reversed only after we pointed out they were the ones who'd called us about it.
•	Both incidents suggest a habit of answering from memory rather than checking the record — a costly default in a role built on retrieval and follow-through.

Floor staff conduct:

•	The staff member delivering requested items (towels, slippers, toothbrush) knocked continuously and without pause until the door was opened, with no allowance for guests needing a moment (e.g., mid-change). This reads as a lack of basic service etiquette training, not an isolated bad day.

Housekeeping consistency:

•	Towel counts didn't match room occupancy (3 guests, but some days only 2 towels supplied) — indicating housekeeping isn't cross-checking against reservation/occupancy records.
•	Visible dust buildup beneath the TV, discovered on our second-to-last day of a longer stay. Raised with front desk — no follow-up action taken. When asked whether rooms are vacuumed daily, staff said yes, but dust was present on return each time — indicating either the claim isn't accurate or execution is inconsistent.

Root cause, not just symptoms: These read less like individual staff failings and more like an absence of basic operational systems — no reliable log for items surrendered at the desk (laundry, lost-and-found), and no process tying housekeeping delivery to actual room occupancy or a verified cleaning checklist.

Context for fairness: We stayed at two other Accor properties on the same trip — Mercure Bankside and Novotel Edinburgh — and experienced excellent, frictionless service at both. This rules out "UK/London service culture" as the explanation; it's specific to this property's execution.

Bottom line: Fine as a short, convenient stopover given the location — not recommended for a longer stay. Guests would likely be better served by a cheaper, equally convenient alternative nearby.

Wasser im Zimmer

Beim Einchecken standen im Zimmer zwei kleine Flaschen Wasser bereit. Eine weitere Lieferung erfolgte erst nach drei Tagen.

Glücklicherweise befindet sich direkt gegenüber dem Hotel ein kleiner Shop, in dem wir uns mit Wasser versorgen konnten. Dadurch mussten wir nicht auf das deutlich überteuerte Wasserangebot des Hotels zurückgreifen.

Frühstück

Das Frühstücksbuffet wurde im Restaurant im Erdgeschoss angeboten.

Das Hotel war während unseres Aufenthalts gut gebucht, sodass der Frühstücksbereich am Vormittag entsprechend stark frequentiert war. Dadurch war es dort teilweise sehr laut.

Zur ohnehin üblichen Lautstärke durch die vielen Gäste kam das ständige Stühlerücken und Scharren der Holzbeine der Stühle auf dem Boden hinzu.

Offensichtlich hat man hier noch nichts von Filzgleitern für Stühle gehört. Gerade in einem Hotel dieser Kategorie sollte es eigentlich selbstverständlich sein, die Geräuschentwicklung durch entsprechend geeignete Gleiter deutlich zu reduzieren.

Fazit

Insgesamt waren wir von mehreren Punkten enttäuscht. Besonders ärgerlich war, dass die ausdrücklich gewünschte tägliche Zimmerreinigung trotz entsprechender Absprache beim Check-in nicht eingehalten wurde. Auch die mehrfach notwendige Nachfrage wegen eines einfachen Handtuchwechsels entspricht aus unserer Sicht nicht dem Service, den man von einem Hotel dieser Kategorie erwarten kann.

Auch beim Badezimmer und beim Frühstücksbereich gibt es aus unserer Sicht deutlichen Verbesserungsbedarf.

reviews.text:
I've stayed at this hotel twice now for upwards of a week each when in London. I stayed at their sister branch down the street at Park Plaza Westminster once, but I would contend this is a bit better for price, location and overall ambiance.

The rooms have always been very clean, well kept and while not particularly spacious, really all you need as a single or couple on a vacation or business. The only thing I'd mention is some bathrooms have a dual standalone shower with the toilet and a sliding door back and forth between the two, which isn't necessarily the most appealing. You're getting your money's worth in comparison to many other nearby options. Depending on what room you get, it could be just a bit noisy from other guests or morning staff, but not awful. As for outside noise, it IS in Central London so, expected.

There are many great nearby breakfast options. In a pinch, their breakfast buffet or the Florentine restaurant are both perfectly fine. For lunch and dinner though, may as well go to one of the hundreds of nearby spots for a new or local experience. There is also a Sainsbury's and Tesco within a 2 minute walk that are good for essentials. The Lambeth North tube station is right across the street that connects you to almost every part of London in one way or another.

The staff is helpful and polite enough. I have not encountered one particularly rude or dismissive one as of yet.

Overall, Park Plaza Waterloo has been a solid, conveniently located hotel with many restaurants, attractions and options for public transportation within walking distance. When in London again, if not staying with family or friends, I'd come back here.
