##Update after 2nd stay (September 2026)##
We stayed at the Hilton London Bankside for three weeks in September 2026. While we previously enjoyed a wonderful family stay here, this trip with my teenage daughter unfortunately fell short of our expectations.

Location & Amenities:
The location is absolutely central and ideal for reaching all major sights and the West End. The breakfast buffet was also very good. However, our room experience was lacking: we received a basic Twin Room on the lowest floor with a view of a dirty courtyard. The TV was unreliable, as streaming services and HDMI capabilities vanished after software updates. On a positive note, the room was perfectly clean, quiet, and the Wi-Fi worked flawlessly. The gym is small but well-equipped, and the pool is wonderfully long and wasn't crowded (note that there is no SPA).

Executive Lounge & Facilities:
The lounge is beautifully furnished and conveniently located. Unfortunately, it was always kept far too cold. The evening food offering ran on a repetitive 3-day cycle for a whole month with practically no meat options—my daughter couldn't find anything she liked. The drink selection, however, was extensive.
There was constant construction going on; while the noise didn't bother us much, the fact that almost never were all three elevators working caused significant delays. We ended up taking the stairs most of the time. Also, it was a pity to see that the kid-friendly amenities from August (like play-food and kid-friendly lounge meals) were completely replaced by a business setup.

Service & Hilton Honors Recognition:
As a Hilton Honors Diamond member, the recognition was very disappointing. There was no personal welcome—not even a card—and despite multiple requests, we did not receive a room upgrade. Only the bare minimum benefits (breakfast and lounge access) were provided. Housekeeping was fantastic and perfectly accommodated our requests to clean the room during our lunch hours. The concierge, however, was unhelpful: instead of simply mailing our postcards, they directed us to a shop that didn't even sell international stamps, forcing us to go searching elsewhere.

Conclusion:
In contrast to our previous stay in a lovely family room, a multi-week stay for two simply didn't pay off this time. Because the lounge food was so weak, we had to eat out anyway. We would have been better off booking a significantly cheaper hotel in a similar location. What a pity.

##Former review (August 2026)
We recently stayed at the Hilton London Bankside as a family of four (my wife, our two daughters 13y & 3y old) and had a wonderful experience.
First of all, we received a very warm and personal welcome, which was highly appreciated after a long journey. The hotel is exceptionally child-friendly! Our youngest was thrilled with the Moomin theme, which included a great play corner and movies shown in the lobby. Our family room was perfectly prepared with adorable fox-themed bedding and a matching cuddly toy. It was also refreshing to see that children are genuinely welcome (and well-represented) at the breakfast buffet, in the lounge, and in the beautiful pool area.
The hotel is certainly high-priced, but given the fantastic location and the excellent service, we felt the price was absolutely justified.
There are only a few neutral to negative points to mention regarding the facilities: The gym is quite small and lacks a variety of strength equipment (for example, there is no leg press); it is mostly focused on cardio machines. Additionally, it is a bit of a pity that there is no wellness area or sauna available to relax in.

As a final note: I have just returned to the hotel with my older daughter for a second stay, and I will make sure to update this review once our current visit is complete!

reviews.text: We stayed at Hilton Bankside for almost a month in August. We chose this hotel after extensive research as we were going to be at the hotel for a few weeks and ended up picking this hotel because of the amazing reviews on being family friendly. We selected the adjoining rooms for our 2 girls and this quickly became one of their favourite hotels! The fox theme was a huge hit, they loved the fox themed room, goody bags, scavenger hunt, and the Moomin theme play area. The breakfast buffet had a nice selection of baked goods, salad bar, fruits, egg station, pancake/waffle station, and more (the candy bar was a huge hit with the kids!). As we were diamond members, we also had access to the lounge, which actually allowed children (unlike other hilton hotels we have been to) and they had drinks and canapes in the evenings. There is a big pool, gym and spa, which I find rare in London due to space. The rooms were modern and more spacious than the hotels that you would get in London and the room service was very attentive. The rooms were cleaned regularly and when we encountered an issue with our room that was quickly resolved when we spoke to the front desk. The location was nice as it was walking distance to the Tate Modern Museum, Borough Market, several grocery stores and restaurants, riverwalk along the thames, and even a few tube stations. Overall, we had a wonderful stay and a special thanks to Miro who made sure when we arrived we were comfortable and even brought a small dessert for our daughter's birthday; Julia who always welcomed us at breakfast and ensured our issues were resolved and many other staff members that we could not remember their names but were lovely to our kids (the staff at the lounge, guest services and cleaning staff). Having stayed for almost a month, we can confidently recommend this hotel to those travelling with families, especially little ones (they have set high expectations to our future travels). Thank you so much to the staff at Bankside Hilton!

We had a very comfortable stay and the moment we entered the lobby, we were offered water. We had some leftover food, and the lady kindly offered to store it in their main fridge for us. They also offered to bring our luggage up to our rooms for us, though we declined since we were fine carrying them up ourselves. They have staff arranged to push the elevator buttons for hotel guests. After settling into the room, we spent the evening out visiting Westminster Abbey, Big Ben, London Eye, Piccadilly, Chinatown. We had access to bus and tube but decided to walk. When we returned to the hotel, water in glass bottles and glass cups were prepared on the bedside tables for us. We experience such amazing service here and the beds were very comfortable after a long day of touring.

We received complimentary breakfast and the restaurant’s display of the food was very pretty. I loved that they had freshly squeezed juices and fresh soy milk and fresh almond milk. Coffee from the machine was not that good so we skipped it and went to Borough market (just a 10 min walk) for a yummy cup of joe and lunch before checking out.

When we checked out, I had a shopping bag that was ripped and asked the lobby staff if they had any extra bags, to which he said I could buy one at the nearby Tesco. As we were walking out, another staff who had overheard my conversation had run towards me with a shopping bag. He was so kind and helped me transfer my items.

I would highly recommend this hotel. The location, staff and rooms were excellent. We did not have time to use any amenities, but there is a pool!

The Standard has been a hotel I've wanted to stay in for a number of years so when a work trip came up and I had the opportunity to stay, I was thrilled. It's clear why so many people love this hotel and return time and time again, while I really enjoyed my time here, there were a couple of things which stopped this from being a five-star stay. On check-in, I was prompted to pay again despite paying in advance, the receptionist eventually realised this but there was a lack of attention to detail and I found them to be a little cold. It also wasn't explained to me where breakfast was the following morning as this was included in my stay - small things I know but they matter.

I stayed in a single room which was lovely for just me, this is one of those hotels which goes all-in on the retro quirky decor and is unapologetically itself which I absolutely love, however, having to climb up into bed wasn't something I was a fan of. If I stayed again, I would probably book a different room type. I ate dinner in The Lounge and the food was really delicious, however, my meal came out well before my drink arrived and I had to ask for cutlery, just tiny things again that were missed. That said, the service at breakfast also in The Lounge was excellent and the staff were really lovely. I also used the gym during my stay and loved that they had two Peloton bikes, a real treat.

I'd definitely return to this hotel again in the future, it's wonderful and couldn't be better located.

One of the worst hotel stays I’ve had in London.

Housekeeping repeatedly moved our luggage, and we later found dirty cleaning cloths and a bottle of cleaning product left with our personal belongings inside the room. That alone was extremely unhygienic and unacceptable.

Then, on our final night, the hotel hosted a loud party/event above the guest rooms. Heavy bass and people jumping continued past 2 AM, making it impossible to sleep even with earplugs. We complained multiple times, the hotel said they contacted the event, but there was no meaningful improvement. No comparable quiet room was offered — only a downgrade.

For a hotel at this price point, basic cleanliness and the ability to sleep should be the minimum. I would not recommend staying here.

reviews.author: Guest
reviews.text:
This would have been a 2-star review had I paid the full advertised rate. Fortunately, the hotel price-matched Trivago, allowing me to book directly at a more reasonable price.

The location is undoubtedly the hotel’s strongest asset, being ideally situated for central attractions and transport links. Unfortunately, several aspects of our stay fell well short of what one would expect from a five-star luxury property.

We dropped our bags off at midday, understanding our room would probably not be ready. Reception assured us they would call when it was available and that this would be by the advertised check-in time of 3pm.

When 3pm came and went without contact, I called reception myself. After some time on hold, I was told the room was ready. As we were only five minutes away, we returned, only to encounter further confusion, with several phone calls and an apparent debate over room allocation. We even overheard a discussion about using out-of-service rooms before one was eventually assigned to us.

The room was a reasonable size, clean and tidy, although the layout was unusual. However, there was visible mould on the shower sealant, which was disappointing.

The Blind Spot cocktail bar is an attractive space with a great atmosphere, but the experience was less impressive. The cocktail offer runs from 5–7pm, extended to 9pm for hotel guests. The waiter showed us the cocktails included, but the two we initially selected were unavailable, so we chose alternatives. The cocktails were mediocre, and we decided not to order any more.

When the bill arrived, we had been charged full price. On querying this, we were told the buy-one-get-one-free offer applied only to two identical cocktails. This restriction had not been explained when we were seated, nor could we find it mentioned on the website. After some discussion and a further wait, the bill was amended.

The following morning brought another inconvenience. We had prepaid for our stay, including breakfast, yet a member of staff informed us that breakfast was not included and we would be charged.

I explained that we had email confirmation stating breakfast was included. Rather than checking this and resolving the issue, I had to leave the dining room and go to reception myself. Reception was unmanned, so I had to wait for someone to arrive. Once a member of staff appeared, the matter was dealt with promptly.

Although resolved, this was another example of poor communication and a lack of attention to detail. Breakfast itself was mediocre at best. Having stayed at The Langham in May, where breakfast was on an entirely different level, the comparison highlighted the shortcomings here.

It is difficult to reconcile these experiences with the hotel’s five-star luxury positioning. The location is excellent and the room was generally comfortable, but the repeated administrative errors, poor communication, disappointing breakfast and visible maintenance issues detracted considerably from our stay.

I suspect that 20 years ago this was the hotel to stay at if you wanted to be seen. Sadly, it no longer lives up to that reputation. In my opinion, the property is showing its age and would benefit from substantial refurbishment, alongside a renewed focus on service standards and attention to detail.

The location remains a major selling point, but location alone cannot justify premium prices. At the full advertised rate, I would have felt seriously short-changed. Even at the reduced price, the experience fell short of what I would expect from a hotel of this calibre.

Finally, having read the hotel’s responses to previous reviews, in which criticisms are apparently taken on board and fed back to management, I have to question how effective that process really is. If the same issues persist, management appears either unable or unwilling to address them.

We spent three nights at The Grazing Goat. As lovers of boutique hotels, we felt this property could be so much better with more attentive management.
There was no warm welcome. We collected our key from the manager at a busy bar and were simply directed upstairs. The room had several shortcomings: an inoperable safe with batteries removed, a heated towel rail that didn't heat, no luggage rack, and no bathroom shelf or vanity space for toiletries.
Footsteps on the oak flooring in the room above were extremely loud, perhaps something an area rug could help. Surprisingly, the room was otherwise quiet at night, even with a busy pub below. However, on Saturday morning, pub staff blasted music from 7:30 opening until around 10 a.m. This wasn't an issue on the other two mornings.
On the positive side, the beds, linens and bathroom products were excellent. The location is fantastic, and overall it represents good value.
The Grazing Goat has all the ingredients of a charming boutique hotel, but the lack of attention to detail and hospitality lets it down. With better management, it could be excellent.

This was our second stay at the hotel. Unfortunately, our room was noticeably smaller than during our first visit, even though we had booked exactly the same room category. Apart from that, everything was good, and the room was always very clean.

One issue we experienced during both stays was the rather late housekeeping service. Although it is stated that room cleaning is carried out until 3:30 PM, on both visits we returned to our room after that time, only to find that it still hadn't been cleaned. During our previous stay, we had to wait quite a long time in the lobby for housekeeping to finish. This time, fortunately, they managed to clean the room within half an hour. Nevertheless, this is quite inconvenient, especially when guests expect their rooms to be ready by the stated time.

Another thing we noticed was that our neighbours frequently ordered room service, and the used trays and leftover food were then left outside their room in the hallway. On several occasions, these remained there for almost an entire day before being collected. This is certainly not what I would expect from a hotel of this standard.

However, the main reason I am deducting one star is an incident that happened on Tuesday. A member of staff knocked on our door and immediately opened it without waiting for a response or permission to enter. She then asked whether everything had been fine with the room cleaning. I told her that everything was fine, although I was honestly quite shocked that she had simply opened the door.

What surprised me even more was that she then asked me if I was okay. Considering that she had just entered our room without giving me a chance to answer the door, I found that question rather inappropriate and quite rude.

For me, this is an absolute no-go. Guests should be able to expect privacy in their hotel rooms, and staff should always wait for permission before entering. I found this behaviour unprofessional and certainly not up to the standards I would expect from a hotel.

Overall, we had a pleasant stay, and the cleanliness of the room itself was very good. However, the housekeeping organisation, the room service trays left in the hallways, and especially the lack of respect for guests' privacy are areas that definitely need improvement.

We stayed for 4 nights and had a wonderful experience. The hotel’s location was absolutely amazing and made it very easy to get around.

The staff was super helpful, friendly, and welcoming throughout our stay. We really appreciated the thoughtful extras, including complimentary bottled water every day and a mini fridge that was regularly replenished with beer, wine, soft drinks, and sparkling water. They also provided free snacks in the room, which was a lovely touch.

Our hotel package included breakfast, and that was a game changer for us. There was a great selection, and it made starting our days so much easier.

The hotel was exceptionally clean, and the rooms were incredibly spacious. We were travelling with three large suitcases and could easily open all three in the room without feeling cramped. The only thing that could use some attention in the room is the carpet, which could benefit from a deep cleaning. It was a bit dirty.

One thing to note is that the hotel layout can be a little confusing at first. To get to our room, we had to take two different lifts and walk through a corridor. Once you figure it out, though, it’s perfectly fine. Just be patient, as the lifts can be quite slow.

Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and would definitely recommend this hotel!

reviews.text:
My one night stay at the Clermont on 3/4 October was fantastic from start to finish. Without it even being mentioned at check-in, my room had been upgraded at no charge and I could already take up occupancy at around 11.00. The Clermont has a great policy of calling guests when their room is ready. I'd just finished looking around an exhibition at the neraby National Portrait Gallery when their call came. I'd already checked-in and left my bags before going to the gallery.

My room was fabulously large and well-furnished and had a free mini-bar. I even got a "Welcome Back Martin" chocolate cake. The views towards Trafalgar Square were great. Despite being above Charing Cross Station and next to a very busy main road, the room was also extremely quiet and I slept very well.

Normally, I try to stay at small hotels. The only time I was really aware of the number of guests at the Clermont was at breakfast but it didn't cause any delay or other issues. The breakfast buffet selection was huge. You can order "freshly cooked for the table" dishes for an extra £5 but I was happy with the buffet. If you take proper advantage of what's on offer the breakfast is certainly good value for central London.

Speaking of central London, my main initial reason for choosing this hotel was its location. For visiting theatre shows and exhibitions it couldn't be better located. Obviously, it is also directly above a mainline train station and very near to two tube stations.

One final thing. I found all members of staff very friendly, helpful and efficient. I wish I had noted her name but the lady at the front desk who checked me in deserves a special mention. I had several interactions with her during my short stay and she couldn't have been more pleasant.

Good Hotel, but Service Needs Improvement

Overall, our stay at The Hey Hotel was pleasant. The rooms were comfortable and well-maintained, but unfortunately, the service did not fully meet our expectations for a four-star hotel.

As younger guests, we sometimes felt that we were treated differently. Regardless of age or appearance, every guest deserves to feel equally welcomed and valued, especially when booking well in advance and informing the hotel of a special occasion.

Check-in took longer than expected, and on several occasions, when returning from dinner, staff repeatedly asked, “Can I help you?” despite having seen us earlier. While we understand the intention may have been to assist, these interactions made us feel somewhat unwelcome.

Breakfast was very good in terms of quality, but service was extremely slow, often taking between 60 and 100 minutes. We also experienced inconsistent charges. On our first morning, toast and bacon were included without any additional cost, but on another morning, we were unexpectedly told we had to pay extra. This was never explained beforehand, creating unnecessary confusion and negatively affecting the start of our day.

Although we enjoyed the accommodations, these small but important service details affected our overall experience. We hope the hotel takes this feedback constructively and improves its communication, consistency, and hospitality to better reflect the standards expected of a four-star property.

- Rubén Espada

In fairness to the hotel staff, we ultimately received everything we asked for or needed, and I appreciated their willingness to accommodate us. That said, there were many points throughout our stay where we needed assistance.

Our arrival in particular felt unnecessarily chaotic. We weren’t looking to check in early—we simply needed some information and a place to change before heading out for the day—but getting clear guidance proved difficult. At several points during our stay, communication felt inconsistent but there was one female associate who became my go to and i am appreciative of her.

The hotel itself has a very cool, moody atmosphere, although that experience didn’t fully translate to our room. Our original room had an uncomfortable bed and a noticeable musty smell. We had two rooms in our reservation, and when our friends checked into theirs, the difference was immediately apparent—their room felt fresher and more comfortable, which confirmed that something wasn’t quite right with ours. After several conversations with the staff, we were thankfully able to move to another room.

We enjoyed the breakfast and  the location is excellent.

Overall, there’s a lot to like about the hotel, but I would not stay there again personally. Our frustration was less about the final outcome and more about how much assistance, follow-up, and persistence seemed to be required to get there.

reviews.text: While the staff at ME London was wonderful, and the location was exactly what we were hoping for (we were easily able to go to two West End shows, last minute), there was a very strong mildew odor throughout the hotel. Our first room was on floor 6, and the minute the elevator doors opened, after we checked in, I could smell the mildew. The odor was even worse in our room, and we noticed what appeared to be a mildew stain on the carpet near the window. Hoping the smell would dissipate, we spent the afternoon walking around the city, but when we returned to the room, the odor was still present so we asked to change rooms. The manager was incredibly accommodating, as was the staff that helped us change rooms. We were moved to the 4th floor, which seemed a bit better in the hallway, but our room, again, had a mildew odor to it  (though not nearly as strong as our first room). Because we were only in town for a few nights, we stayed at ME London and just dealt with the odor. The room was otherwise comfortable, as were the beds. The hotel is definitely "tired" and in need of some attention, as there were water marks on the ceiling and stains on some of the towels. We will not choose to stay here again.
